宮島（紅葉谷公園）.types: Iroha maple, Oba maple, Nomura maple, and other varieties
宮島（紅葉谷公園）.address: 廣島縣廿日市市宮島町紅葉谷
宮島（紅葉谷公園）.access_train: About 10 min by ferry from Miyajimaguchi Station on the JR Sanyo Line, then about 20 min on foot
宮島（紅葉谷公園）.access_car: Park at a lot near Miyajimaguchi Pier and transfer to the ferry
宮島（紅葉谷公園）.tagline: Step into the sacred back garden of Itsukushima Shrine, a World Heritage site on the island of the gods, and bow before the vermilion Momiji Bridge mirrored in a sea of two hundred ancient maples.
宮島（紅葉谷公園）.desc:
Momijidani Park sits at the foot of sacred Mount Misen on Miyajima, right next to the World Heritage site of Itsukushima Shrine, making it one of the island's premier spots for autumn color. From mid- to late November, roughly two hundred old maple trees lining both banks of the Momijidani River reach peak color, blanketing the deep mountain ravine in a riot of red and gold.

The park's classic view pairs the vermilion wooden Momiji Bridge with the clear stream below and the full canopy of color overhead. The vivid foliage leans in over the gentle waterside, and when morning light filters through the branches onto the still water — often alongside a wandering wild deer — it captures the quiet, ancient elegance the island is famous for.

The park's paths are built flat along the natural terrain, and the walk from the Miyajima pier is shaded and pleasantly cool, making it an easy day trip. Crowds are heavy, so it's best to catch the first ferry on a weekday morning if you want the maple bridge to yourself for photos.

三段峽.types: Japanese maple, Zelkova, and other maple varieties
三段峽.address: 廣島縣山縣郡安藝太田町柴木
三段峽.access_train: About 75 min by highway bus from JR Hiroshima Station to Sandankyo-guchi
三段峽.access_car: About 10 min from Togouchi IC on the Chugoku Expressway
三段峽.tagline: Drift through a 16-km primeval gorge in Nishi-Chugoku Sanchi Quasi-National Park, where black wooden boats glide beneath cliffside foliage at Kurobuchi.
三段峽.desc:
Sandankyo is a sweeping 16-km gorge famed across western Japan for its untamed, primeval scenery — a designated Special Place of Scenic Beauty. From late October to mid-November, the ancient forest clinging to its sheer cliffs and deep ravines turns color in stages, filling the once-green gorge with vivid, living color.

The gorge's signature scene is its layered composition of waterfalls, jewel-toned pools, and cliffside foliage. Riding a traditional black wooden boat through Kurobuchi, where hundred-meter cliffs tower on either side, you can look up at a wall of color and cascading water at once — a striking mix of stillness and motion.

Trails mostly follow the natural terrain, though some stretches are narrow with natural stone steps, so sturdy, grippy hiking shoes are strongly recommended for photography. The gorge is long, so plan on half a day to walk it at ease. Weekday mornings are best for the mist to clear, with direct sunlight ideal for catching perfect reflections.

佛通寺.count: several hundred trees across the temple grounds and approach
佛通寺.address: 廣島縣三原市高坂町許山22
佛通寺.access_train: About 40 min by bus from JR Mihara Station to the Buttsuji stop
佛通寺.access_car: About 15 min from Mihara-Kui IC on the Sanyo Expressway
佛通寺.tagline: Visit one of the Sanyo region's great Rinzai Zen head temples, where a colossal wooden approach and cliffside foliage frame the ancient grounds.
佛通寺.desc:
Buttsuji is a storied old Zen temple tucked deep in the Mitsugigawa valley outside Mihara. From mid- to late November, several hundred old maple trees across the spacious grounds and along the approach that crosses the stream turn color together, wrapping the solemn precincts in brilliant autumn hues.

The most striking scene pairs the temple's towering wooden main hall with the clear Mitsugi River and a tunnel of maples along the approach. When the night illumination switches on, dappled light plays across the old founder's hall and moss-covered stone steps, giving the temple its distinctive sense of history and quiet mystery.

The main approach and the bridges crossing the river are flat and well maintained, making for an easy walk. Crowds build during festival season, when the temple runs its dreamlike night lighting. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is stillest, for the clearest shots of the temple's untouched, contemplative scenery.

大步危小步危.count: extensive primeval forest along the gorge
大步危小步危.address: 德島縣三好市山城町重實至上名
大步危小步危.access_train: About 20 min on foot from JR Oboke Station on the JR Dosan Line to the boat dock
大步危小步危.access_car: About 35 min from Ikawa-Ikeda IC on the Tokushima Expressway
大步危小步危.tagline: Listen to the Yoshino River roar through a deep gorge, and take the Oboke Gorge sightseeing boat past a mountainside blanketed in color.
大步危小步危.desc:
Oboke and Koboke form a formidable V-shaped gorge carved over centuries by the Yoshino River, known for its dramatic crystalline schist cliffs. From mid- to late November, tall Japanese beech and maple trees lining the sheer cliffs and clear river turn a brilliant gold along both banks.

The must-do experience here is the Oboke Gorge sightseeing boat. Small wooden boats carry visitors slowly into the gorge, weaving between churning rapids and giant boulders, with a deep emerald river on one side and a wall of color close enough to touch on the other.

Winds can be sharp along the gorge and the autumn air bites, so bring a warm coat and windproof hat. It's worth checking boat schedules online in advance — a morning departure catches the light at its best as it reaches down into the V-shaped valley floor.

祖谷蔓橋.count: primeval forest of a remote gorge
祖谷蔓橋.address: 德島縣三好市西祖谷山村善德162-2
祖谷蔓橋.access_train: About 20 min by bus from JR Oboke Station to the Kazurabashi stop
祖谷蔓橋.access_car: About 1 hour from Ikawa-Ikeda IC on the Tokushima Expressway
祖谷蔓橋.tagline: Cross one of Japan's three great vine bridges hidden in legend-steeped Iya, and take in the raw rapids and blazing foliage of the Iya River below.
祖谷蔓橋.desc:
The Iya Vine Bridge, woven from roughly five tons of wild actinidia vine, is one of Japan's three great "strange bridges," hidden in a valley steeped in legends of the fleeing Heike clan. From mid- to late November, the towering old-growth forest lining the steep banks of the Iya Gorge turns red in unison, filling the deep mountains with color.

The bridge's famous, slightly nerve-wracking scene pairs its rustic vine construction with the jagged rapids of the gorge below and a wall of foliage on the cliffs. Stepping across wooden slats spaced 10 cm apart, with the clear blue-green Iya River rushing far below, delivers a real jolt of vertigo and visual drama.

The bridge runs one-way and sways noticeably, with wide gaps between the slats, so proper athletic shoes and a secure grip on phones and cameras are strongly recommended. The gorge is deep, and mist is at its most beautiful in the early morning. Go on a weekday morning to have the remote scenery mostly to yourself.

栗林公園.hours: 07:00–17:00 (varies by month; extended during night illumination)
栗林公園.access_train: About 3 min walk from Ritsurin-koen Kitaguchi Station on the JR Kotoku Line
栗林公園.access_car: About 15 min from Takamatsu-chuo IC on the Takamatsu Expressway
栗林公園.tagline: Wander a Special Place of Scenic Beauty framed by Mount Shiun, and take in Kikugetsu-tei from Hiraiho as the pond mirrors the maples in perfect stillness.
栗林公園.desc:
Ritsurin Garden is a classic Edo-period stroll garden built up over generations by the lords of the Takamatsu domain, and it's designated one of Japan's Special Places of Scenic Beauty. From late November through early December, the countless old maples around the garden's "Maple Shore" reach peak color in refined, classical fashion.

The garden's signature scene pairs the elegant wooden Kikugetsu-tei teahouse, the arched bridge over the South Lake, and its reflection in the water. Looking down from Hiraiho, the garden's finest viewpoint, the mirror-still water perfectly reflects the winding old embankment, the 300-year-old boxed pines, and the full sweep of autumn color — open, balanced, and serene.

Most of the garden is flat, with well-maintained gravel paths and stone walkways, making it very easy going for visitors with strollers or older family members. Japan's most spectacular illumination takes over at night during the autumn festival. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the clearest reflections and emptiest paths.

寒霞溪.types: Japanese maple and over 50 other tree species
寒霞溪.count: scattered across the island's bizarre rock formations
寒霞溪.address: 香川縣小豆郡小豆島町神懸通
寒霞溪.access_train: Take the Shodoshima Bus (Kusakabe Port Line) from any port to the ropeway station
寒霞溪.access_car: About 15 min from Kusakabe Port (ferry required to reach Shodoshima)
寒霞溪.tagline: Ride the ropeway over one of Japan's three great gorges on Shodoshima, where maples weave through bizarre rock spires above the Seto Inland Sea.
寒霞溪.desc:
Kankakei sits on Shodoshima Island, a massive volcanic gorge carved over eons and ranked among Japan's three most scenic ravines. From early to late November, over 50 species of maple growing across the broad, hilly forest burst into color, filling the primeval mountainside with red and gold.

The visual highlight is riding the Kankakei Ropeway. As the cabin rises, riders look down on a surreal jumble of jagged rock formations wrapped in fiery foliage, with the multi-island beauty of the Seto Inland Sea stretching blue in the distance — an open, dramatic panorama.

The summit has an accessible observation deck and benches, welcoming to walkers and joggers alike. Mosquitoes can be a nuisance in the hills, so bring repellent and plenty of water. Weekday mornings offer the coolest, most comfortable conditions.

寶滿宮竈門神社.access_train: About 10 min by "Mahoroba-go" bus from Nishitetsu Dazaifu Station
寶滿宮竈門神社.access_car: About 20 min from Dazaifu IC on the Kyushu Expressway
寶滿宮竈門神社.tagline: Visit Dazaifu's storied shrine of love and fortune, where 300 maples blaze through a torii-framed forest lit up for a romantic night illumination.
寶滿宮竈門神社.desc:
Houman-gu Kamado Jinja, at the foot of Mount Homan, is an ancient shrine with over 1,300 years of history, celebrated locally for matchmaking and warding off misfortune. From mid- to late November, some 300 maple and other trees around its solemn torii gate and main hall reach peak color, dusting the sacred grounds in early-autumn hues.

The visual centerpiece here is the classical pairing of mossy stone steps, the great torii, and a full tunnel of color. Climbing the well-maintained gravel approach, walls of vivid foliage rise nearly to eye level on either side. When the special night illumination switches on, the whole hillside turns gold, taking on a mystical, almost otherworldly quality.

The approach to the main hall is gently graded and easy walking, making for a comfortable morning visit — the full route takes about 40 minutes round trip. During festival season, shrine staff offer limited-edition maple-themed charms and seal stamps. Weekday mornings see the fewest visitors, ideal for photographing the shrine's quiet, sacred atmosphere.

雷山千如寺大悲王院.types: Great maple (Prefectural Natural Monument), Japanese maple
雷山千如寺大悲王院.access_train: About 30 min by bus from JR Maebaru Station to the Raizan-Kannon-mae stop
雷山千如寺大悲王院.access_car: About 15 min from Maebaru IC on the Nishi-Kyushu Expressway
雷山千如寺大悲王院.tagline: Visit a thousand-year-old temple with deep ties to the Soga clan in Itoshima, and stand beneath a nationally designated 400-year-old giant maple.
雷山千如寺大悲王院.desc:
Senjuji Daihioin is a storied Tendai temple founded by the priest Seiga. From early to mid-November, the hundreds of maples in its famous old garden turn color together, dressing the sacred grounds in brilliant hues — crowned by a single maple tree some 400 years old, the largest in the prefecture.

The centerpiece here is the dialogue between this nationally designated Natural Monument — a colossal 400-year-old maple — and the moss carpeting the ground beneath it. Its huge canopy spreads across the sky like a giant multicolored torch, and once peak color passes, the fallen leaves blanket the ground in a thick crimson carpet, blending stillness and motion into a scene steeped in history.

The temple grounds are flat and compact, making for an easy morning stroll for independent travelers, though visitors must change into temple slippers to enter the Daihi-den main hall and view the Muromachi-era garden. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is stillest, for the best light to bring out the wood grain of the old buildings in evocative, story-rich shots.

御船山樂園.types: Iroha maple, Oba maple, Azalea (autumn foliage)
御船山樂園.address: 佐賀縣武雄市武雄町大字武雄4100
御船山樂園.access_train: About 5 min by taxi from JR Takeo-Onsen Station
御船山樂園.access_car: About 15 min from Takeo-Kitakata IC on the Nagasaki Expressway
御船山樂園.tagline: Explore the Nabeshima clan's sprawling 15,000-tsubo garden, where cutting-edge digital illumination meets fiery foliage against Mount Mifune's jagged cliffs.
御船山樂園.desc:
Mifuneyama Rakuen is a massive traditional Japanese stroll garden covering some 150,000 square meters, built over many years by Takeo domain lord Nabeshima Shigeyoshi. From mid-November through early December, several thousand maples spanning dozens of varieties reach peak color, filling this natural landmark with brilliant hues.

The garden's biggest draw is its "Night Maple Illumination," among the grandest in all of Japan. Looking out over the still reflecting pond, maples lit in vivid color stand out against the rugged cliffs of Mount Mifune behind them, and when the water perfectly mirrors the scene, the effect is downright magical.

The grounds are expansive, with gently graded main paths that are friendly to strollers and visitors with mobility needs. The garden's famous Chikurintei bamboo pavilion and cutting-edge art installations are also on-site. Arrive around 4pm to catch the vivid daylight foliage before sunset and the illumination as it comes alive after dark.

九年庵.address: 佐賀縣神埼市神埼町的1696
九年庵.access_train: About 15 min by seasonal shuttle bus from JR Kanzaki Station
九年庵.access_car: About 10 min from Higashi-Sefuri IC on the Nagasaki Expressway
九年庵.tagline: Step into a Saga industrialist's hand-built retreat, open just nine days a year for one of the finest maple carpets in the country.
九年庵.desc:
Kyunenan is a nationally designated scenic garden built over nine painstaking years by Saga businessman Itami Yatarō, in the classical sukiya style. To protect its delicate ecology and moss, it opens for a mere nine days each year, from mid- to late November, drawing photographers and independent travelers from across Japan.

The garden's defining feature is the dialogue between its exquisitely deep green moss, a running stream, and a full sweep of red maple. Walking the gently winding stone path, walls of foliage rise almost to eye level on either side, and at peak color, fallen leaves blanket the natural slopes and mossy ground in a display of refined, private garden artistry.

Because the garden opens for only nine days, strict limits apply to daily entry tickets during the season, so arriving early to queue is strongly recommended. The grounds include some fine stone steps and dirt paths, so casual sneakers are advised. The moment right after opening is the only real window to catch it free of crowds.

九重夢大吊橋.address: 大分縣玖珠郡九重町田野1208
九重夢大吊橋.access_train: About 20 min by bus from JR Bungo-Nakamura Station
九重夢大吊橋.access_car: About 20 min from Kokonoe IC on the Oita Expressway
九重夢大吊橋.tagline: Stand on Japan's tallest pedestrian-only suspension bridge and look down on the Naruko River gorge and the roaring 'Shindo Falls' framed in color.
九重夢大吊橋.desc:
The Kokonoe Yume Otsurihashi spans the deep Kusui Gorge at a staggering 390 meters long and 173 meters high — the tallest of its kind in Japan. From late October to mid-November, the massive blue steel structure and the primeval forest of surrounding Mount Ogiri turn color together, filling the gorge with vivid red and purple.

The visual highlight is the pairing of the massive bridge with the foliage-filled ravine below. Looking down from the bridge deck, a hundred meters up, you can see the rushing Naruko River below and, on either side, "Shindo Falls" (male and female falls), ranked among Japan's 100 best waterfalls — a sweeping 360-degree panorama.

Both ends of the bridge have well-built viewing plazas and fully flat, accessible walkways, friendly to strollers and older visitors. Because of the high, exposed setting, winds are strong year-round, so secure hats and gear carefully when shooting photos. Come at dusk, when the sunset light gives the foliage its most magical glow.

由布院（金鱗湖）.count: several dozen trees around the lakeshore
由布院（金鱗湖）.address: 大分縣由布市湯布院町川上1561-1
由布院（金鱗湖）.access_train: About 20 min walk from JR Yufuin Station
由布院（金鱗湖）.access_car: About 10 min from Yufuin IC on the Oita Expressway
由布院（金鱗湖）.tagline: Wander the dreamy spring-fed lake at the foot of Mount Yufu, where a torii rising from the water, onsen mist, and full maple color meet in perfect reflection.
由布院（金鱗湖）.desc:
Kinrin-ko Lake sits in the laid-back, artsy resort town of Yufuin Onsen, famous for a water temperature kept naturally mild by the mix of a cold spring and hot spring feeding it. From mid- to late November, the maple grove ringing the lakeshore reaches peak color, filling this scenic spot with vivid, living hues.

The lake's signature scene pairs the torii of the underwater Tenso Shrine, wisps of onsen steam that never fully disappear even in winter, and a full mirror of maple color. The glassy, ripple-free water turns almost mystical when cold morning air meets the mild lake surface, producing a soft white mist that blends with the surrounding foliage for a deeply atmospheric scene.

The lakeshore has flat, well-built wooden boardwalks and paths, welcoming to older visitors and strollers alike. The surrounding old town is full of artsy shops and cafes, making it easy to fill a whole day. To catch the famous morning mist and a perfect reflection of the foliage, aim to arrive before 7am.

高千穗峽.address: 宮崎縣西臼杵郡高千穗町三田井御塩井
高千穗峽.access_train: About 90 min by bus from Nobeoka Station to Takachiho Bus Center
高千穗峽.access_car: About 10 min from Takachiho IC on the Kyushu-Chuo Expressway
高千穗峽.tagline: Listen to Manai Falls thunder over towering columnar-jointed cliffs, and drift beneath a gorge draped end to end in autumn color.
高千穗峽.desc:
Takachiho Gorge is a formidable canyon of columnar-jointed granite formed by an ancient eruption of Mount Aso, designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty. From mid-November through early December, foliage reaches its peak, with the towering gray cliffs and the maple grove above turning color together and filling this mythic ravine with vivid hues.

The visual centerpiece is the 17-meter Manai Falls, framed by rowboats on the water and a wash of red maple color. Walking the trail, you can watch the falls come thundering down like a stampede of horses, with clear, ribbon-like turquoise water at your feet. Renting a rowboat and looking up from the water delivers an even more dramatic view.

The gorge has well-maintained flat paths and viewing platforms along its length, making for easy, comfortable walking suited to a family riverside stroll. Since the main viewpoints sit deep within the rocky gorge, aim for around midday, when the sun reaches straight down to the valley floor — foliage color is most vivid then, and it's ideal for scenic photography.

縮景園.address: 廣島縣廣島市中區上幟町2-11
縮景園.access_train: Right at the Shukkeien-mae stop on the Hiroshima Electric Railway streetcar line
縮景園.access_car: About 20 min from Hiroshima IC on the Sanyo Expressway
縮景園.tagline: Wander an Edo-era daimyo garden in the heart of Hiroshima, where an arched bridge over Takei Pond meets a full wall of layered autumn color.
縮景園.desc:
Shukkeien is a historic stroll garden built by master tea master Ueda Soko on the order of Hiroshima domain lord Asano Nagaakira in the Edo period. From mid- to late November, the countless maples ringing the garden's central pond reach peak color, bringing rich autumn hues to this refined oasis in the city center.

The garden's centerpiece pairs a great arched stone bridge, a classical Japanese teahouse, and the mirrored reflection of maple color. Looking out from the pond's edge, the beautifully shaped bridge, built of natural granite, sits perfectly reflected in the still surface of Takei Pond alongside the vivid surrounding foliage — open, balanced, and serene.

The garden's interior is compactly and cleverly laid out and mostly flat, though the high ground around Yuishinzan hill has a few natural steps; the main gravel paths are well maintained and friendly to older visitors. Hiroshima Museum of Art sits right next door, making for an easy, relaxed day out. Weekday mornings have the fewest visitors and offer the clearest reflections for photos.

帝釋峽.count: 18 km of primeval limestone gorge forest
帝釋峽.hours: Open 24 hours (sightseeing boat and shops vary by season)
帝釋峽.address: 廣島縣神石郡神石高原町及庄原市東城町
帝釋峽.access_train: About 15 min by bus or taxi from JR Tojo Station on the JR Geibi Line (to the upper plateau)
帝釋峽.access_car: About 15 min from Tojo IC on the Chugoku Expressway
帝釋峽.tagline: Wander a vast limestone karst gorge in the Chugoku mountains and marvel at Obashi, one of the world's three great natural bridges, framed in autumn color.
帝釋峽.desc:
Taishakukyo is an 18-km Special Place of Scenic Beauty famed nationwide for its massive limestone karst landscape. From late October to mid-November, the forested mountains along the shores of Lake Shinryu and the primeval Taishakugawa gorge turn color in sequence, dressing the rugged canyon in a vivid, living palette.

The gorge's legendary sight is Obashi, one of the world's three great natural bridges, set against the river and cliffside foliage. This enormous natural stone arch, carved by nature over tens of thousands of years, stands alongside cascading red maple color — a sweeping, powerful composition.

The Lake Shinryu area has gentle lakeside paths and sightseeing boats, friendly to older visitors and strollers, while the trail to Obashi runs mostly over natural gravel, so comfortable, grippy shoes are a good idea. Weekday mornings are best for the mist to clear, offering the clearest view of the towering cliffs and full display of foliage.

劍山.count: extensive alpine forest on Shikoku's second-highest peak
劍山.address: 德島縣三好市東祖谷、美馬市、那賀町交界
劍山.access_train: Seasonal sightseeing bus from JR Sadamitsu or Anabuki Station
劍山.access_car: About 90 min from Mima IC on the Tokushima Expressway to the Minonokoshi trailhead
劍山.tagline: Climb Shikoku's second-highest peak, a sacred site for mountain ascetics, and take in golden pampas grass and a sweeping wall of color along the Jiro-gyu ridge.
劍山.desc:
Standing 1,955 meters tall, Mount Tsurugi is one of Japan's 100 Famous Mountains and Shikoku's second-highest peak — long revered as a sacred site for Shugendo mountain ascetics. Its cool, high-altitude climate brings an early foliage season, reaching peak color by mid-October, as scrub alder and maple lay a colorful carpet across the sprawling alpine terrain.

The mountain's core appeal is the sweeping view along the Jiro-gyu ridge, where a high alpine meadow meets a full wash of color. From the ridge trail, the endless mountains unfold in layered gold, red, and green, and when morning clouds drift through the valleys, the whole peak seems to float above a sea of mist in an almost mythical scene.

A two-person chairlift carries visitors easily from the trailhead up to Nishijima Station, and the main trail from there to the summit is laid with well-built boardwalks, making for a relatively easy, safe climb. The alpine terrain offers little shelter and winds run strong, so bring a warm, windproof coat for outdoor shooting. Clear late mornings offer the best visibility.

祖谷溪.count: primeval forest of a deep V-shaped gorge
祖谷溪.address: 德島縣三好市池田町松尾至西祖谷山村
祖谷溪.access_train: About 55 min by bus toward Iya Onsen from JR Awa-Ikeda Station
祖谷溪.access_car: About 45 min from Ikawa-Ikeda IC on the Tokushima Expressway
祖谷溪.tagline: Explore a hundred-meter-deep V-shaped gorge in the mountains of Shikoku, and catch the Peeing Boy statue against a full carpet of color.
祖谷溪.desc:
Iya Valley, one of Japan's three great hidden regions, is a massive V-shaped gorge carved by the Iya River through the mountains of Shikoku. From mid- to late November, foliage reaches its peak, with wild forest turning color in stages across hundreds of meters of elevation, from the valley floor to the ridgeline, forming a striking, layered carpet of color.

The valley's signature scene pairs the daring "Peeing Boy" statue perched on a solitary cliff with the winding river below and a full mountainside of color. Standing at the edge of a cliff with a sweeping view, the statue — not for the faint of heart — sits framed by the green-ribboned river below and a slope streaked gold and red, for an open, powerful composition.

Most viewpoints sit along the narrow, winding Iya road, with several well-equipped overlooks, making the drive convenient for older visitors and self-driving travelers. The mountain air turns distinctly cool in late autumn. Visit around midday on a clear day, when sunlight reaches deepest into the valley, for the best shots of the sweeping scenery.

金刀比羅宮.count: approx. 800 trees along the approach and around the Oku-sha
金刀比羅宮.address: 香川縣仲多度郡琴平町892-1
金刀比羅宮.access_train: About 15 min walk from JR Kotohira Station on the JR Dosan Line, or Kotoden Kotohira Station (to the trailhead)
金刀比羅宮.access_car: About 15 min from Zentsuji IC (vehicles can only reach the lower parking area)
金刀比羅宮.tagline: Climb the 1,368-step stone stairway up Mount Zozu and find Asahi-sha and the deep-mountain maples in quiet, historic conversation.
金刀比羅宮.desc:
Kotohira-gu, set on the slopes of Mount Zozu, is the head shrine of Japan's guardian deity of the sea, long said to be a pilgrimage "everyone should make once in their life." From mid-November through early December, hundreds of old maples across the long approach, the Omote Shoin, and the sprawling mountain grounds up to the Oku-sha turn color, dressing the shrine precincts in autumn hues.

The centerpiece is the historic dialogue between the vermilion Asahi-sha hall, rustic stone lanterns, and a tunnel of maple color. Vivid foliage crowds around the layered old wooden halls, and when morning light filters through the branches onto the stone steps and mossy ground, the scene blends motion and stillness into the shrine's distinctive, sacred calm.

Reaching the Main Shrine requires climbing 785 stone steps, and 1,368 in total to the Oku-sha, so comfortable, professional running shoes are strongly recommended, along with staying hydrated at the shaded rest points along the way. Arrive right when the mountain opens at 6am on a weekday for the fewest crowds and the best shots of the shrine's quiet, sacred atmosphere.

秋月城跡.count: approx. 20 maple trees plus surrounding natural forest
秋月城跡.address: 福岡縣朝倉市秋月野鳥
秋月城跡.access_train: About 20 min by Amagi Sightseeing Bus toward Akizuki from Amagi Station on the Amagi Railway
秋月城跡.access_car: About 20 min from Amagi IC on the Oita Expressway
秋月城跡.tagline: Wander the 'Little Kyoto of Chikuzen' and its black-lacquered historic gate, where the old Kuromon and Nagayamon meet a blaze of cherry-and-maple color.
秋月城跡.desc:
Akizuki Castle Ruins occupies the former site of the Edo-period Akizuki Castle, seat of the Kuroda clan, and preserves a well-kept old castle-town atmosphere. From late November through early December, hundreds of old maple and cherry trees around the famous historic landmarks of Kuromon (Black Gate) and Nagayamon (Row House Gate) turn a deep red together.

The scene's core appeal is its classical pairing of the imposing black wooden gate, sturdy stone walls, and autumn color. Vivid clusters of red and orange spill down along the gentle gravel path, draping over the solemn black gate and the moss beneath it — a blend of motion and stillness that captures the quiet, weathered history of the old castle town.

The historical park is completely flat, with well-maintained old paths, friendly to older visitors and strollers. The well-known Kuromon Chaya teahouse nearby serves traditional kuzumochi. Set aside about an hour to walk the grounds; weekday mornings have the fewest visitors, ideal for photographing the historic ruins free of crowds.

光明禪寺.count: an intricately arranged dry landscape (karesansui) garden
光明禪寺.hours: 09:30–16:30 (※ interior currently closed for renovation; exterior viewing only recommended)
光明禪寺.access_train: About 5 min walk from Nishitetsu Dazaifu Station
光明禪寺.access_car: About 15 min from Dazaifu IC on the Kyushu Expressway
光明禪寺.tagline: Step into a Rinzai temple beside Dazaifu Tenmangu, and take in the moss and raked-gravel Hashin-tei garden framed by maple color.
光明禪寺.desc:
Komyozenji, affiliated with the Tofukuji school of the Rinzai sect, is affectionately known as the "moss temple" for the lush moss carpeting its grounds. From mid- to late November, dozens of old maples across the terraced grounds bloom without restraint, dressing the sacred precincts in a refined, deeply atmospheric autumn palette.

The temple's most striking sight is the minimalist contrast of white sand, green moss, and red maple. Looking out from the main hall's wooden veranda, the "Hashin-tei" dry landscape garden — white sand representing the sea, moss and rocks forming the character for "Buddha" — sits beneath a cascade of violet-blue reflected color, showing off a refined, elegant gardening aesthetic.

This is a retreat far from the noise of the city, dedicated to quiet and meditation, so please keep your voice down while visiting and photographing. Stepping onto the lawn or sand of the viewing garden is strictly forbidden; visitors instead sit on the veranda to take it in. Morning visits on weekdays offer the deep-mountain temple's rare stillness all to yourself.

大山祇神社.types: Japanese maple, Ginkgo, Great camphor tree
大山祇神社.count: several dozen trees on the shrine grounds
大山祇神社.address: 佐賀縣武雄市武雄町大字武雄
大山祇神社.access_train: About 15 min walk from JR Takeo-Onsen Station
大山祇神社.access_car: About 10 min from Takeo-Kitakata IC on the Nagasaki Expressway
大山祇神社.tagline: Visit a guardian grove on the slopes of Mount Kusenbu in Tosu, and find nine centuries-old sacred trees framed by bamboo lanterns along the approach.
大山祇神社.desc:
Oyamazumi Jinja sits on a quiet slope of Mount Kusenbu in Tosu, a hidden gem designated a "Saga Prefecture Heritage" site. From mid-November through early December, the old shrine grounds set amid unspoiled rural scenery come into foliage season, as a tall grove of maples turns color, dressing the shrine in autumn hues.

The shrine's core visual appeal is the classical dialogue between nine towering, nationally recognized sacred trees, the old wooden main hall, and the surrounding color. These nine ancient giants seem to stand guard around the wooden shrine building in quiet dialogue. During the maple festival, a special night illumination lines the approach with rows of bamboo lanterns, lending a mystical, dreamlike quality.

The shrine grounds are compact and flat, making for an easy walk — the full visit takes about 40 minutes. Visitor numbers here stay relatively low, making it an excellent hidden gem for self-driving travelers seeking a high-quality, unhurried autumn color experience. Morning visits on weekdays are best for capturing the rich, tranquil light of the surrounding forest and fields.

耶馬溪.count: extensive natural forest among towering rock cliffs
耶馬溪.address: 大分縣中津市耶馬溪町深耶馬
耶馬溪.access_train: About 1 hour by bus from JR Nakatsu Station to the Shin-Yaba stop
耶馬溪.access_car: About 15 min from Kusu IC on the Oita Expressway
耶馬溪.tagline: Wander a nationally designated scenic gorge of jagged cliffs along the Yamakuni River, and take in the layered color of 'Ichimo-Hakkei' from its famous overlook.
耶馬溪.desc:
Yabakei is a rugged granite gorge carved over centuries by the Yamakuni River, ranked among Japan's three great scenic wonders and the "New Three Views of Japan." From late October to mid-November, foliage season sets in, and because of the steep elevation change, color spreads downward from upper Oku-Yabakei, dressing the towering cliffs in vivid hues.

The gorge's most talked-about sight is "Ichimo-hakkei" (Eight Views at a Glance), the centerpiece of Shin-Yabakei. From the specially built overlook, visitors can take in the surrounding jagged peaks — Meoto-iwa (Husband-and-Wife Rocks), Eboshi-iwa, and more — alongside a swaying carpet of gold and red foliage, a sweeping and powerful sight.

A well-equipped scenic road and cycling path run the length of the gorge over flat, open terrain, making it ideal for self-driving or a leisurely bike ride. Since the main viewpoints sit deep within the rocky gorge, visiting between 10am and noon lets sunlight reach the valley floor directly, when foliage color is at its most vivid.

五瀨川溪谷.count: gorge forest stretching along the Gose River
五瀨川溪谷.address: 宮崎縣西臼杵郡高千穗町、五瀨町
五瀨川溪谷.access_train: Bus from Nobeoka Station to Takachiho Bus Center, then transfer
五瀨川溪谷.access_car: About 10 min from Takachiho IC on the Kyushu-Chuo Expressway
五瀨川溪谷.tagline: Follow a hidden waterside corridor through the Takachiho range, where Hinokage's riverbanks vanish beneath acres of autumn color.
五瀨川溪谷.desc:
Gosegawa Gorge stretches through the Hinokage area along the clear waters of the Gose River. From mid- to late November, the Japanese beech and maple lining its broad banks reach peak color, dressing this once-quiet, green mountain forest in the soft hues unique to early autumn.

The visual highlight is the layered interplay of the crystal-clear river, a massive bridge, and walls of color. Ribbons of red and gold line the gentle riverbank and gravel paths, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the blue sky, the towering modern steel arch bridge, and the lush foliage in front of it, the scene shows off nature at its purest.

The riverside paths are flat and well maintained, with several stretches ideal for a relaxed drive-and-stroll morning outing. Shade is limited along the way, so bring sun protection for midday visits. Early morning is best for capturing the rich, meditative stillness in the air.

蝦野高原.types: Japanese silver grass, Nanakama maple, Lacquer tree
蝦野高原.address: 宮崎縣えびの市大字末永
蝦野高原.access_train: Bus or reserved taxi from JR Ebino-Iino Station
蝦野高原.access_car: About 30 min from Ebino IC on the Kyushu Expressway
蝦野高原.tagline: Climb an active volcanic highland in the Kirishima range and take in Onami-ike, Fudo-ike, and Japan's finest grass foliage.
蝦野高原.desc:
Ebino Kogen sits within Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park at an elevation of 1,200 meters, making it one of Kyushu's premier highland spots for autumn color. From late October to early November, the volcanic soil and climate bring red rowan and golden, feathery silver-grass plumes into peak color together, filling the highland with vivid hues.

The plateau's most talked-about sight is the sweeping pairing of Fudo-ike, a crater lake, with the active volcano behind it and the golden grass in front. Along the well-maintained nature trail, hikers can catch the emerald and cobalt-blue waters of the lake set against the barren, rugged volcanic cliffs behind and the swaying golden meadow in front — a powerful, expansive scene.

The highland terrain is open, with gentle, well-built trails connecting each viewpoint, convenient for older visitors and those exploring by car. Weather at this elevation shifts quickly and winds run strong year-round, so bring a warm, windproof coat for outdoor shooting. Visit on a clear morning with good visibility for the most vivid foliage color.

赤目四十八瀑布.types: Iroha maple, Japanese maple, Mountain cherry
赤目四十八瀑布.address: 三重縣名張市赤目町長坂861-1
赤目四十八瀑布.access_train: About 10 min by bus from Akameguchi Station on the Kintetsu Line
赤目四十八瀑布.access_car: About 40 min from Ueno IC on the Meihan National Route
赤目四十八瀑布.tagline: Listen to the Taki River roar through a deep-cut gorge, and marvel at Nino Falls framed by acres of autumn color.
赤目四十八瀑布.desc:
Akame 48 Falls is a celebrated gorge within Muro-Akame-Aoyama Quasi-National Park, carved over centuries by the Taki River, and ranked among Japan's 100 best waterfalls. From early to late November, several thousand maple and beech trees along the steep cliffs turn color together, filling the gorge with vivid hues.

The greatest visual impact comes from the pairing of stunning Nino Falls, its massive rock walls, and a wash of red maple. Climbing the zigzagging old gravel trail, hikers can see fast-moving streams cascading down through a canopy of gold. During foliage season, a dreamlike bamboo-lantern illumination lights the evenings.

The main trail has well-built wooden boardwalks along the streamside, though some sections near the riverbed can be slippery, so grippy hiking shoes are strongly recommended. The gorge also holds historical significance as a ninja training site. Visit around midday when sunlight reaches the valley floor directly, for the most vivid foliage color.

御在所纜車.count: across the entire slope of Mount Gozaisho
御在所纜車.address: 三重縣三重郡菰野町湯之山溫泉
御在所纜車.access_train: About 10 min by bus from Kintetsu Yunoyama-Onsen Station
御在所纜車.access_car: About 10 min from Komono IC on the Shin-Meishin Expressway
御在所纜車.tagline: Ride Japan's tallest cableway and look down on the jagged rock of the Suzuka mountains beneath a three-tiered wash of color.
御在所纜車.desc:
Mount Gozaisho, within Suzuka Quasi-National Park, rises 1,212 meters and ranks among Japan's 200 Famous Mountains. Because of its elevation and unique geology, foliage color starts at the alpine moss-covered summit in mid-October and spreads gradually downward through late November, filling the deep valley with vivid hues.

The mountain's most talked-about sight is riding the Gozaisho Ropeway. As the cabin climbs, and especially as it passes Japan's tallest white cable tower at 61 meters, riders get a bird's-eye view of rugged boulders interwoven with a sweeping natural carpet of gold and red — a powerful, sprawling panorama.

The ropeway carries visitors directly to the open summit plateau, though winds run strong there and temperatures already dip close to single digits by late October, so bring a warm, windproof coat for shooting. Mountain weather can change quickly, so a clear morning with good visibility is strongly recommended for the brightest, most three-dimensional light.

伊勢神宮.count: natural forest along the Isuzu River and shrine grounds
伊勢神宮.address: 三重縣伊勢市宇治館町1
伊勢神宮.access_train: About 6 min by bus from Kintetsu Isuzugawa Station
伊勢神宮.access_car: About 5 min from Ise IC on the Ise Expressway
伊勢神宮.tagline: Step into Japan's most sacred shrine and take in the Isuzu River's Mitarashi purification site beneath ancient cedar and glowing maple.
伊勢神宮.desc:
Ise Jingu (Inner Shrine) is a supreme historic site with over 2,000 years of history, affectionately regarded as the pinnacle of all Japanese shrines. From late November through early December, hundreds of old maples reach peak color around the solemn Uji Bridge, the great torii, and the banks of the sacred Isuzu River.

The core scene here pairs the sacred Mitarashi purification site on the Isuzu River, moss-covered stone lanterns, and maple color in a classical composition. Vivid foliage crowds around rustic stone lanterns and towering old trees, and the still, clear stream perfectly reflects the dense canopy of maple overhead, capturing the shrine's distinctive, quiet reverence.

The path to the main hall is completely flat, with an extremely well-maintained gravel approach, friendly to older visitors and strollers. To avoid the heavy crowds and capture the cleanest, most classical shots of the sacred grounds, arrive early — right at the 5am opening on a weekday is strongly recommended.

名花之里.count: approx. 300 trees (including reflections in the mirror pond)
名花之里.address: 三重縣桑名市長島町駒江漆畑270
名花之里.access_train: About 10 min by direct shuttle bus from Kintetsu Nagashima Station
名花之里.access_car: About 10 min from Nagashima IC on the Higashi-Meihan Expressway
名花之里.tagline: Wander a sprawling flower park in Kuwana and marvel at one of Japan's largest illuminations mirrored in a lakeside wall of maple color.
名花之里.desc:
Nabana no Sato is a massive landscaped park world-famous for its huge illumination displays and greenhouse gardens. From late November through late December, its famous maple corridor and lakeside area reach peak color, as hundreds of old maple trees dress the park's European-style setting in vivid hues.

The park's most talked-about sight is the reflected mirror image of its extraordinary night illumination, the "Water Corridor," and the maple color. Looking out over the still reflecting pond, the maples lit in vivid color stand out against distant illuminated landmarks, and as a breeze passes over the water, the scene turns downright magical.

The park's grounds are extremely well planned with fully accessible, flat paths throughout, very friendly to older visitors and strollers. Arrive around 4pm to catch the vivid daylight foliage before sunset, along with the striking, atmospheric night display as the lights first come on.

水杉並木.address: 滋賀縣高島市マキノ町寺久保
水杉並木.access_train: About 6 min by bus from JR Makino Station to the Pickland stop
水杉並木.access_car: About 30 min from Kinomoto IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
水杉並木.tagline: Drive a 2.4-km grand avenue in Takashima lined with 500 towering dawn redwoods, ablaze in a golden tunnel on both sides.
水杉並木.desc:
The Metasequoia Avenue in Makino, Takashima (Makino Kogen Metasequoia Namiki), is an iconic tree-lined road ranked among Japan's 100 Best Roads and famous worldwide. Along its dead-straight 2.4-km stretch, some 500 towering dawn redwoods line both sides, reaching peak color from late November onward.

The road's greatest visual appeal is the seemingly endless carpet of color running along its full length. Whether driving through slowly or stopping roadside, the vivid orange and gold feathery foliage sits close enough to touch on both sides. The neatly cone-shaped canopies interlace overhead, giving the scene an open, striking impact.

Since this is fundamentally an open, public road for vehicles, walk carefully when looking for photo angles and never cross the center of the road. This is a world-class attraction, so arriving before dawn on a weekday morning is strongly recommended, when the light is at its most vivid and three-dimensional.

雞足寺.count: approx. 200 trees (famous for its maple-leaf carpet)
雞足寺.address: 滋賀縣長濱市木之本町古橋
雞足寺.access_train: About 15 min by seasonal bus from JR Kinomoto Station
雞足寺.access_car: About 10 min from Kinomoto IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
雞足寺.tagline: Walk the approach of a forgotten temple above Lake Biwa's northern shore and find Japan's finest crimson leaf-carpet on its ancient stone steps.
雞足寺.desc:
Keisokuji, formerly Hanpukuji, is a historic abandoned temple on the mountainside above Nagahama, now lovingly maintained by local residents. From mid- to late November, some 200 old maples lining the long stone stairway to the old ruins reach peak color, earning the temple its reputation as a top foliage spot in the Hokuriku region.

The visual highlight is the classical pairing of ancient mossy steps, the weathered old structures, and a full carpet of red. Vivid foliage crowds tightly along the long gravel approach, and at peak color, fallen leaves blanket the old stone paving and stairway, turning the whole corridor a deep red steeped in the passage of time.

Reaching the old temple ruins requires walking a gently sloped natural gravel mountain path from the small market at the base, so comfortable, grippy shoes are strongly recommended. To protect the fragile natural scenery and historic site, check official notices before your visit. Arrive before dawn on a weekday morning for the emptiest, most photogenic scenery.

清水寺.address: 京都府京都市東山區清水1-294
清水寺.access_train: About 15 min by bus from JR Kyoto Station to the Gojo-zaka stop
清水寺.access_car: Parking is very limited nearby; public transport is strongly recommended
清水寺.tagline: Climb to a World Heritage stage on the slopes of Mount Otowa and look out over a thousand Iroha maples set ablaze against the old capital.
清水寺.desc:
Kiyomizu-dera, head temple of the Hosso sect with over a thousand years of history, is a World Heritage site. From late November through early December, roughly a thousand Iroha maples around the majestic main hall and Otowa mountainside bloom together, dressing the sacred grounds in vivid color, and earning the temple its reputation as Kansai's most iconic foliage spot.

The temple's core scene pairs the National Treasure Kiyomizu Stage with a sea of maple color suspended below it. From the observation deck at Oku-no-in, the grand, cantilevered wooden main hall sits framed against the swaying red maples on the water's edge. During the special night viewing, a beam of deep blue Kannon light cuts through the darkness, performing alongside the illuminated foliage for a dreamlike effect.

Being world-famous, Kiyomizu-zaka and the temple grounds get crowded with visitors from around the world during foliage season. The whole temple is built along the hillside, and the approach includes plenty of steps, so comfortable walking shoes are strongly advised. To photograph the historic buildings without crowds of tourists in frame, arrive right at the 6am opening.

永觀堂.address: 京都府京都市左京區永觀堂町48
永觀堂.access_train: About 15 min walk from Keage Station on the subway Tozai Line
永觀堂.tagline: Discover why they call it 'Eikando of the maples,' and lose yourself in the reflecting pond and stone-walled foliage of this Pure Land temple.
永觀堂.desc:
Eikando has long carried the nickname "Eikando of the maples," a Pure Land temple celebrated for its scenery across all four seasons. From late November through early December, some 3,000 maple trees across the hillside grounds bloom without restraint, dressing the sacred precincts in vivid color.

The temple's most talked-about sight is the reflected image of the Hojo-ike pond, the vermilion Gokuraku Bridge, and the surrounding maples. Standing at the pond's edge, the vermilion bridge and its wall of colorful foliage sit perfectly mirrored in the still water, and when the night illumination switches on, the layered scene captures the temple's distinctive sense of history and quiet reverence.

The temple is built along the hillside, with the main worship route running along interior wooden floors; the air turns quite cool in late autumn and winter, so warm socks are strongly recommended. Queues for the night illumination run long, so arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the cleanest shots of the sacred grounds and their perfect reflections.

瑠璃光院.address: 京都府京都市左京區上高野東山24
瑠璃光院.access_train: About 5 min walk from Yase-Hieizanguchi Station on the Eizan Railway
瑠璃光院.access_car: No parking available; driving not recommended
瑠璃光院.tagline: Visit a hidden garden at the foot of Mount Hiei near Yase, famous the world over for its full mirror of color on a lacquered black writing desk.
瑠璃光院.desc:
Rurikoin is a historic sukiya-style building tucked away amid the natural beauty of Yase, open to the public only briefly in spring and autumn. From mid- to late November, dozens of maple varieties around the meticulous "Ruri Garden" reach peak color, dressing the sacred grounds in vivid, living hues.

The temple's world-famous centerpiece is the reflection of the foliage on the polished black lacquered desk on the second floor of the study hall. The glassy, ripple-free desktop reflects the deep green moss outside the window and the layered red-and-gold foliage in a perfect mirror image, blending a sense of history with mystical wonder for a striking visual effect.

During foliage season, entry is fully reservation-based, keeping the atmosphere inside notably calm. The study hall's interior is flat and comfortable to walk through. Seasoned photographers actually prefer a lightly overcast day over full sun for shooting here — the softer light makes it far easier to capture the desk's perfect mirrored reflection.

箕面瀑布.count: extensive natural forest along the valley
箕面瀑布.address: 大阪府箕面市箕面公園
箕面瀑布.access_train: About 40 min walk to the falls from Hankyu Minoo Station on the Hankyu Minoo Line
箕面瀑布.access_car: Traffic restrictions apply on holidays during foliage season; public transport recommended
箕面瀑布.tagline: Drive into Meiji-no-Mori Minoo Quasi-National Park and catch the famous falls and vermilion Ryuanji temple bursting with early-autumn energy.
箕面瀑布.desc:
Minoo Falls sits in the forested hills of Minoo City, a top-tier natural park ranked among Japan's 100 best waterfalls. From mid- to late November, the "Taki-michi" trail winding along the Minoo River comes into foliage season, filling the once-green valley with vivid, living color.

The greatest visual impact comes from the pairing of the 33-meter waterfall with a wash of red maple. Standing before the falls' pool, you can watch the white cascading water thunder down, framed by dense, fiery Iroha maple that blocks out the sky. When mist forms a rainbow in the air, the whole scene takes on real visual power.

The full walk from Minoo Station to the falls covers about 2.8 km on completely flat, well-maintained paths, making it an easy hike for the whole family. Along the way, try the local specialty, maple-leaf tempura. Weekday mornings have the fewest crowds, the most comfortable temperatures, and the best conditions for scenic photography.

御堂筋銀杏並木.address: 大阪府大阪市中央區御堂筋
御堂筋銀杏並木.access_train: Right at the exits of Yodoyabashi, Hommachi, or Shinsaibashi stations on the Osaka Metro
御堂筋銀杏並木.access_car: This runs along the city's main artery; the subway is recommended instead
御堂筋銀杏並木.tagline: Walk the 4-km artery from Umeda to Namba and pass through a golden tunnel between the skyscrapers.
御堂筋銀杏並木.desc:
Midosuji is the iconic main artery running through the heart of Osaka. From late November through early December, 800 towering ginkgo trees lining both flat sidewalks reach peak color, their four rows of canopy interlacing overhead into a brilliant, unbroken sheet of gold — a striking display of urban autumn.

The street's core appeal is its refined urban aesthetic, pairing modern high-rises and upscale shopping streets with a golden tunnel of leaves. As leaves fall, the ground fills with a thick golden carpet that stands in sharp contrast to the flow of traffic passing through. At night, the world-class "Midosuji Illumination" show adds real visual drama.

This spot sits in the middle of the city's busy commercial district on completely flat ground, making it an easy morning walk for independent travelers, and very stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. Experienced photographers strongly recommend arriving before dawn on a weekday for a clean shot of the golden street, free of cars and pedestrians.

好古園.fee: Adults ¥310 (combination ticket with Himeji Castle available)
好古園.access_train: About 15 min walk from JR Himeji Station
好古園.access_car: About 15 min from Himeji-Higashi IC on the Sanyo Expressway
好古園.tagline: Step into nine connected samurai-residence gardens beside Himeji Castle and take in the Palace Garden pond mirrored in maple color.
好古園.desc:
Kokoen skillfully makes use of the ruins of the Edo-period West Residence, forming a proper traditional Japanese stroll garden spanning 3.5 hectares. From mid-November through early December, hundreds of maple trees across the garden reach peak color, dressing this historic landmark in a refined, classical autumn palette.

The visual centerpiece pairs an exquisite reflecting pond, a stream and waterfall, and the maple color in a dialogue across time. The rustic wooden corridor "Choontei" sits beside the clear waterside, and when the mirror-still surface of the "Palace Garden" pond perfectly reflects the cascading sea of red above and Himeji Castle's keep in the distance, the space feels open and deeply serene.

The garden grounds are well laid out with flat, well-maintained gravel paths, very friendly to older visitors and strollers. During foliage season, a famous, dreamlike night illumination runs, making the reflections even more ethereal. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the best light to bring out the old buildings' texture in evocative photos.

竹田城跡.hours: 04:00–17:00 (varies by season; sea of clouds visible at dawn)
竹田城跡.address: 兵庫縣朝來市和田山町竹田古城山
竹田城跡.access_train: About 40 min walk from JR Takeda Station, or take the Tenku Bus
竹田城跡.access_car: Vehicles can only park at 'Yamajo no Sato' at the base; walk or take the shuttle bus from there
竹田城跡.tagline: Climb the 'Castle in the Sky' stone ramparts and catch dawn mist over the Maruyama River beneath a sweeping wall of color.
竹田城跡.desc:
Takeda Castle Ruins sits atop Mount Kojo (elevation 353 m), ranked among Japan's 100 Fine Castles, and earned its nickname as Japan's "Machu Picchu" for its extraordinary late-autumn dawn scenery. From late October to mid-November, the famous foliage-covered slopes reach peak color, adding a touch of early autumn to the massive, weathered castle ruins.

The site's legendary sight is the interplay of morning mist, the massive stone ramparts, and the surrounding color. Viewed from the Ritsuunkyo overlook across the valley, the solitary castle ruins seem to float on an endless sea of white cloud, with a mountainside streaked gold and red behind it — a truly sweeping scene.

Reaching the hilltop ruins requires walking a gently sloped natural mountain path from the small market at the base, so grippy hiking shoes are strongly recommended. The sea of clouds typically forms on clear, windless dawns with a sharp temperature swing. Arrive at dawn for the best chance to capture this dreamlike, mystical scene.

談山神社.access_train: About 25 min by bus from JR/Kintetsu Sakurai Station
談山神社.access_car: About 45 min from Tenri IC on the Nishi-Meihan Expressway
談山神社.tagline: Visit a historic shrine on Mount Tonomine tied to Fujiwara no Kamatari, and find the world's only wooden 13-story pagoda amid 3,000 maples.
談山神社.desc:
Danzan Jinja, set deep in the mountains of Tonomine, is a world-class historic shrine steeped in nature worship. From mid- to late November, some 3,000 maples across the shrine's towering 13-story pagoda, old halls, and approach quietly bloom together, earning it a reputation as Kansai's finest foliage site.

The shrine's core appeal is the classical approach lined with color leading to the world's only wooden 13-story pagoda. Vivid foliage crowds around the old wooden pagoda and moss-covered stone steps, and when afternoon mist drifts through the mountains, the foliage seen through the haze alongside historic monuments captures the shrine's distinctive stillness.

Reaching the main hall and the 13-story pagoda requires climbing several hundred old stone steps, so comfortable, grippy shoes are strongly recommended for the visit. During foliage season, a dreamlike night illumination runs. Arrive right when the mountain opens on a weekday morning, when the air is stillest, for the best classical, atmospheric shots.

高野山.count: along Jabara-michi path and across the temple grounds
高野山.address: 和歌山縣伊都郡高野町高野山
高野山.access_train: Nankai Rinkan bus from Koyasan Station on the Nankai Koya Line
高野山.access_car: About 45 min from Kihoku-Katsuragi IC on the Kyoto-Nara Expressway
高野山.tagline: Climb to a Shingon Buddhist sanctuary 900 meters up, and take in Konpon Daito pagoda and the maple-lined Jabara-michi path.
高野山.desc:
Koyasan is a massive religious mountain town founded by the monk Kukai, sitting 900 meters above sea level, and its entirety is designated part of the Kongobuji World Heritage site. Because of its elevation, foliage here turns earlier than anywhere else in Kansai, reaching peak color from late October to early November as maples and old trees across the mountain turn brilliant red together.

The mountain's legendary sight pairs the vermilion Konpon Daito pagoda with a tunnel of maple color along Jabara-michi. Walking the well-maintained gravel path, walls of vivid foliage crowd in on both sides nearly to eye level, complemented by old stone lanterns and historic monuments, expressing a refined, sacred Eastern religious aesthetic.

The mountaintop terrain is open and flat, with well-maintained streets, making for comfortable, safe walking. Because of the extreme elevation, dawn temperatures already dip close to single digits by late October, so bring a warm coat for outdoor shooting. Weekday mornings see fewer pilgrims, letting you take in the purest morning bells and the rich, meditative air alone.

黑部峽谷.count: gorge forest along a 20-km rail line
黑部峽谷.hours: Trolley train operates approx. 08:00–16:00 (varies by season)
黑部峽谷.fee: Free (trolley train adults round-trip approx. ¥4,000, varies by route)
黑部峽谷.address: 富山縣黑部市黑部峽谷口11
黑部峽谷.access_train: About 5 min walk from Unazuki-Onsen Station on the Toyama Chiho Railway to the trolley train station
黑部峽谷.access_car: About 20 min from Kurobe IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
黑部峽谷.tagline: Ride a vintage open-air trolley train through Japan's deepest V-shaped gorge, and catch the vermilion Okukane Bridge in autumn color.
黑部峽谷.desc:
Kurobe Gorge is a formidable V-shaped canyon carved over centuries by the Kurobe River, ranked among Japan's three great gorges. From late October to early November, maple and beech trees blanketing the steep cliffs and clear river turn color without restraint, dressing this primeval forest in vivid hues.

The must-do experience here is the Kurobe Gorge Unazuki Railway trolley train. Vintage, small open-air sightseeing cars carry passengers gently into the mountains, crossing dramatic bridges and passing through tunnels, with a deep emerald river on one side and a wall of color close enough to touch on the other.

Because winds run strong through the gorge and the train's open-air cars offer no shelter, the mountain air turns bitterly cold in autumn even when the lowlands are still mild, so bring a warm coat and windproof hat. It's worth reserving seats online in advance, and a morning departure catches the light at its best in the V-shaped valley.

立山黑部（室堂）.types: Nanakama maple, Alpine azalea, Mongolian oak
立山黑部（室堂）.hours: First Alpine Route departure around 07:00, last around 17:00
立山黑部（室堂）.address: 富山縣中新川郡立山町蘆峅寺
立山黑部（室堂）.access_train: Take Alpine Route transportation from Tateyama Station or Shinano-Omachi to Murodo
立山黑部（室堂）.access_car: Large parking available near Tateyama Station; a dedicated bus is required from there
立山黑部（室堂）.tagline: Climb to a sky-high sanctuary at 2,450 meters, and marvel at Mikuriga-ike pond and Japan's earliest three-tiered autumn color.
立山黑部（室堂）.desc:
Tateyama Kurobe Murodo sits within Chubu-Sangaku National Park at a striking 2,450 meters, an alpine hideaway known nationwide as the site of Japan's earliest autumn color. Because of the elevation, alpine plants begin turning by mid-September, and by late September the entire mountain is blanketed in deep red and gold gradients.

The mountain's legendary sight pairs the magical emerald-green Mikuriga-ike pond with the majestic Tateyama range. From the lakeside observation deck, visitors can capture the rare "three-tiered autumn color" — snow-capped peaks above, colorful foliage in the middle, and lush green conifers at their feet — all at once, with reflections doubling the scene's impact on a still day.

This is true high-alpine terrain, and by late September summit temperatures already dip close to single digits, so proper hiking boots and a warm, windproof coat are essential for shooting here. Private vehicles are banned throughout the area, so visitors must transfer to low-emission buses. Early mornings offer the clearest, most contemplative light.

五箇山.count: forest surrounding the World Heritage villages
五箇山.access_train: World Heritage bus from JR Takaoka Station or Jōhana Station
五箇山.access_car: About 5 min from Gokayama IC on the Tokai-Hokuriku Expressway
五箇山.tagline: Walk into the World Heritage thatched-roof village of Ainokura, and find traditional gassho-zukuri houses framed by a wall of beech-leaf color.
五箇山.desc:
Gokayama, ranked alongside Shirakawa-go, is a World Heritage site made up of the two historic gassho-zukuri thatched-roof villages of Ainokura and Suganuma. From late October to early November, the primeval forest surrounding these old villages turns color, dyeing this remote, unspoiled valley in the rich hues of early autumn.

The classic composition here is the panoramic view from the Ainokura village overlook. From this elevated vantage point, dozens of rustic thatched-roof houses sit framed against a mountainside streaked with fiery red and gold, as if stepping into a traditional Japanese folk tale.

The village itself is completely flat and easy to walk, with well-organized cultural exhibits and historic displays. Compared to Shirakawa-go, this spot draws far fewer tourists, making it ideal for independent travelers seeking a calmer, higher-quality experience. Weekday mornings offer the purest rural stillness and the best light for photography.

雨晴海岸.types: Pine, with the distant Tateyama range's autumn color
雨晴海岸.count: coastal pines set against distant mountain foliage
雨晴海岸.address: 富山縣高岡市太田雨晴
雨晴海岸.access_train: About 5 min walk from Amaharashi Station on the JR Himi Line
雨晴海岸.access_car: About 15 min from Takaoka-Kita IC on the Noetsu Expressway
雨晴海岸.tagline: Stand on a coastline ranked among Japan's finest, and frame Meoto-iwa rock, a retro painted train, and layered mountain color.
雨晴海岸.desc:
Amaharashi Coast sits within Noto Peninsula Quasi-National Park and is ranked among Japan's 100 Best Beaches. From late October to early November, the maples planted along the gentle shoreline and around Yoshitsune-iwa rock reach peak color, adding a soft touch of early autumn to this dramatic, solitary coastal view.

The coast's most striking sight pairs Meoto-iwa (Husband-and-Wife Rock) in the sea with the distant Tateyama range and autumn color. On clear days with good visibility, the snow-capped Tateyama peaks appear to float above the water, framed together with vivid maple swaying on the shore and the retro painted JR Himi Line train passing gently by — a powerful, sweeping scene.

The coastline is mostly natural sand with some rocky terraces, so comfortable walking shoes are strongly recommended. Because this is an exposed coastal headland, sea winds run strong year-round, so secure your tripod carefully while shooting. Visit at dusk, when the sunset gives both the sea and the foliage their most magical glow.

兼六園.fee: Adults ¥320 (free entry during select night illumination hours)
兼六園.access_train: About 15 min by Kenrokuen shuttle bus from JR Kanazawa Station
兼六園.access_car: Prefectural parking nearby; about 15 min from Kanazawa-Morimoto IC
兼六園.tagline: Wander a garden fit for the Kaga domain's million-koku lords, and take in Kasumi-ga-ike pond, the Kotoji lantern, and color that never quite dies.
兼六園.desc:
Kenrokuen, ranked alongside Kairakuen and Korakuen as one of Japan's three great gardens, perfectly embodies the "stroll garden" aesthetic of the Edo period. From late November through early December, hundreds of maples across the garden reach peak color, dressing this historic space in vivid hues.

The garden's classic scene pairs the iconic Kotoji-style stone lantern, the Kotobashi arched bridge, and maple color in a mirrored composition. Vivid foliage leans in along the gentle gravel paths, and when the mirror-still surface of Kasumi-ga-ike pond reflects the historic landmark, the old Karasaki pine, and the sweeping color above, the space feels open and elegantly serene.

The garden grounds are flat with well-maintained paths, very friendly to older visitors and strollers. Starting November 1st, the garden's famous pines are traditionally rigged with cone-shaped "yukitsuri" ropes to protect against snow — a rare chance to catch maple color and yukitsuri in the same frame. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the fewest crowds and best photos.

那谷寺.count: several hundred trees across the grounds and around the rock-formation trail
那谷寺.address: 石川縣小松市那谷町ユ122
那谷寺.access_train: Take the Kaga Loop Bus 'CANBUS' from JR Kaga-Onsen Station
那谷寺.access_car: About 20 min from Kaga IC or Komatsu IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
那谷寺.tagline: Visit a thousand-year-old temple of Hakusan mountain worship set among jagged rock, where maples grow from stone and a foliage-filled valley meets the main hall.
那谷寺.desc:
Natadera, founded by the priest Taicho, is a historic Shingon-sect temple with over 1,300 years of history. From early to mid-November, several thousand maples and beech trees around its dramatic, volcanically formed "Kigan Yusenkyo" rock formations turn color together, wrapping the deep-mountain temple in vivid hues.

The temple's classic composition pairs its distinctive gray rock cliffs, stone Buddha statues, and a full sweep of red maple. The rustic wooden Daihikaku (main hall) spans a cave hollowed out by water, with a sea of deep red maple cascading down the valley slope at its feet. When afternoon mist drifts through the mountains, it best captures the temple's distinctive, quiet reverence.

Reaching the rock-formation overlook requires climbing some natural stone steps through narrow passages, so comfortable, grippy shoes are strongly recommended for visiting. The grounds are well maintained, making for a cool, pleasant walk. Arrive right when the mountain opens on a weekday morning, when the air is stillest, for the best classical, atmospheric shots.

白山 White Road.address: 石川縣白山市中宮至岐阜縣大野郡白川村
白山 White Road.access_train: No direct public transport; a rental car is recommended
白山 White Road.access_car: Enter via the Nakagu tollgate on the Ishikawa side or the Magari tollgate on the Gifu side
白山 White Road.tagline: Drive the ridgeline of Hakusan National Park and marvel at Uba Falls and miles of layered color along the way.
白山 White Road.desc:
The Hakusan Shirakawa-go White Road is a scenic corridor spanning Ishikawa and Gifu prefectures, running across wild highland terrain at around 1,000 meters elevation. From early to late October, thousands of maple and beech trees lining the road turn color together, forming a genuine tunnel of color the entire way.

The road's greatest visual appeal is the layered band of color rising and falling with the mountain terrain. Whether driving through slowly or stopping roadside, both sides are packed with vivid red and gold foliage close enough to touch. The colorful band winds up and down with the terrain, paired with "Uba Falls," ranked among Japan's 100 best waterfalls, and the sweeping Hakusan range beyond — a powerful, dramatic scene.

This is a tolled, open-air mountain road that closes for winter due to snow from around mid-November, so check official updates before setting out. Winds run strong at the summit and it feels distinctly cool, so bring a warm coat for shooting, and pick a clear morning with good visibility for the most comfortable drive.

九頭龍湖.count: extensive natural forest around the lakeshore
九頭龍湖.access_train: About 15 min by taxi from Kuzuryuko Station on the JR Etsumi-Hoku Line
九頭龍湖.access_car: About 20 min from Shirotori IC on the Tokai-Hokuriku Expressway
九頭龍湖.tagline: Stand beside a reservoir lake deep in Oku-Echizen and take in the Seto Bridge against a shoreline of golden beech.
九頭龍湖.desc:
Kuzuryuko is a massive artificial reservoir formed by the Kuzuryu Dam, renowned across the Hokuriku region for its broad, deep-blue waters and shifting seasonal scenery. From mid-October to early November, the Japanese beech and maple lining its expansive shoreline reach peak color, dressing this natural landmark in vivid hues.

The lake's classic sight pairs the Seto Bridge spanning the water with a wash of color along the shore. The massive steel bridge, set against cliffs streaked with color, stands in quiet dialogue with the still water, backed by the endless deep-blue lake and a full sweep of foliage — open and beautifully balanced.

The road circling the lake is well maintained, ideal for a scenic drive or a relaxed cycling trip. Mornings and evenings in the deep Oku-Echizen mountains run cool and windy, so bring a warm coat for outdoor shooting. Visit on a calm, clear morning for the best chance at a perfect reflection of the foliage on the water.

永平寺.count: several hundred trees across the old temple grounds
永平寺.address: 福井縣吉田郡永平寺町志比5-15
永平寺.access_train: About 30 min by Eiheiji shuttle bus from Fukui Station
永平寺.access_car: About 10 min from Eiheiji-Sando IC on the Chubu-Jukan Expressway
永平寺.tagline: Step into the Soto Zen sect's grand seven-hall monastery and find Jakko-zeki and old maples in quiet, meditative dialogue.
永平寺.desc:
Eiheiji, founded by the Zen master Dogen, is the leading head temple of the Soto Zen sect, still home today to many monks in training. From early to mid-November, hundreds of old maples along the solemn Sanmon gate, the Buddha Hall, and the mountain paths bloom without restraint, dressing the sacred, austere grounds in a touch of Japanese elegance.

The temple's classical scene pairs its massive wooden halls, an old training path, and maple color in a dialogue across time. Vivid foliage crowds tightly along the long gravel approach, complemented by old stone lanterns and historic monuments, blending motion and stillness into a display of the temple's distinctive, quiet reverence.

The temple's interior is built along the mountainside with long corridors and stairways; the main worship route runs over tatami and wooden floors, and visitors must change into temple slippers. As this is a world-class religious site, please stay completely quiet during your visit and never photograph monks in training face-on. Weekday mornings offer the stillest air.

白川鄉.count: Several hundred trees around the gassho-zukuri village
白川鄉.hours: 24 hours (observation deck shuttle bus until around 16:00)
白川鄉.address: 岐阜縣大野郡白川村荻町
白川鄉.access_train: Take a Nohi bus from JR Takayama Station or Kanazawa Station
白川鄉.access_car: About 5 minutes from the Shirakawa-go IC on the Tokai-Hokuriku Expressway
白川鄉.tagline: Step into the UNESCO-listed gassho-zukuri village and take in its thatched roofs and blazing hillsides from the Ogimachi Castle Ruins overlook.
白川鄉.desc:
Shirakawa-go is a UNESCO World Heritage village famous the world over for its traditional gassho-zukuri thatched-roof farmhouses. From late October to early November, the untouched forests surrounding the old settlement turn with autumn color, washing this secluded, rustic valley in rich early-fall tones.

The classic view is the panorama from the Ogimachi Castle Ruins observation deck. From this hilltop vantage point, you can frame dozens of rustic thatched-roof farmhouses together with the fiery red and gold hillside behind them — like stepping straight into a scene from a traditional Japanese folktale.

The village itself is completely flat and easy to walk, with air-conditioned cultural halls and historical exhibits to explore. Because it's a world-famous hotspot, tour groups pack the streets by day, so an early weekday morning visit is best for peaceful, unspoiled views and the best light for photography.

新穗高高空纜車.count: Foliage color shifts in layers with elevation
新穗高高空纜車.address: 岐阜縣高山市奧飛驒溫泉鄉新穗高溫泉
新穗高高空纜車.access_train: About 90 minutes by limited-express bus from JR Takayama Station
新穗高高空纜車.access_car: About 1 hour from the Takayama IC on the Chubu-Judan Expressway
新穗高高空纜車.tagline: Ride Japan's only double-decker ropeway and take in a jaw-dropping carpet of color spread across 2,000 meters beneath Mount Nishihotaka and Yarigatake.
新穗高高空纜車.desc:
Set within Chubu-Sangaku National Park, the Shin-Hotaka Ropeway is famous nationwide as Japan's only double-decker aerial tramway. With an elevation change of nearly 1,000 meters, the color starts at the summit each early-to-late October and spreads downward, blanketing the deep valley in a riot of red and gold.

The must-do experience is the ropeway ride itself: rising slowly through crisp mountain air, you get a bird's-eye view of a rolling carpet of yellow and red stretching along the valley floor, with the snow-capped peaks of the Northern Alps looming behind — a genuinely striking sight.

This is true high-mountain terrain — by mid-October, temperatures at the summit observation deck are already near freezing, so bring a proper windproof, insulated jacket. The exposed alpine terrain also gets gusty, so secure hats and tripods. Go up on a clear morning for the best visibility.

莫內之池.types: Maple, water lilies (autumn color reflected on the water)
莫內之池.count: A few dozen trees around the small pond by the shrine
莫內之池.address: 岐阜縣關市板取下ケ本1643-17
莫內之池.access_train: No direct public transit; from Seki Station, take one of the infrequent buses or rent a car
莫內之池.access_car: About 35 minutes from the Seki-Hiromi IC on the Tokai-Kanjo Expressway
莫內之池.tagline: Visit the hidden spring-fed pond by Nemichi Shrine to catch koi gliding beneath a mirror-perfect reflection of autumn leaves.
莫內之池.desc:
Known officially as the nameless pond of Nemichi Shrine, "Monet's Pond" is a crystal-clear spring-fed pool tucked into the foothills of Seki that became world-famous for its resemblance to Monet's Water Lilies. From mid to late November, the maples ringing the pond hit their peak, painting this secluded spot in deep autumn color.

The scene that made it famous online: impossibly clear, mirror-still water where colorful koi glide gracefully among blooming water lilies, while red and gold maples reflect off the surface — a genuinely otherworldly, almost surreal sight.

A flat, well-maintained boardwalk and viewing deck circle the pond, so it's an easy walk. For the clearest water and the sharpest reflections, aim to visit between 11am and 1pm on a calm, sunny day, when overhead light hits the surface directly and the colors pop the most.

寸又峽.count: Emerald-green reservoir waters framed by valley foliage
寸又峽.hours: Sunrise to sunset (one-way traffic control may be enforced during peak crowds)
寸又峽.address: 靜岡縣榛原郡川根本町千頭
寸又峽.access_train: About 40 minutes by bus from Senzu Station on the Oigawa Railway to Sumatakyo Onsen
寸又峽.access_car: Roads are narrow, so leave early; about 90 minutes from the Shimada-Kanaya IC on the Shin-Tomei/Shin-Meishin Expressway
寸又峽.tagline: Ride the slow Oigawa Railway into a deep gorge to reach the Yume-no-Tsuribashi suspension bridge, suspended over an emerald mirror of water framed by layered autumn color.
寸又峽.desc:
Sumatakyo is a deep gorge carved over centuries by the Sumata River at the foot of the Southern Alps. From late October to mid-November, thousands of Japanese beech and maple trees along miles of steep cliff face turn together, blanketing the mountains in color.

The showstopper is the Yume-no-Tsuribashi ("Dream Suspension Bridge") spanning the reservoir. Standing at its center — barely two planks wide — you'll look straight down at water that glows a dreamlike emerald (thanks to light refracting off suspended particles), ringed by cliffs cascading with color.

Reaching the bridge means a 90-minute loop trail with some rough stone steps and steep sections, so wear proper walking shoes. Only 10 people are allowed on the bridge at a time, and lines get long during peak season — arrive at first light on a weekday if you can.

田貫湖.count: Several hundred trees around the lakeshore (with views of Diamond Fuji and autumn reflections)
田貫湖.access_train: About 45 minutes by bus from JR Fujinomiya Station
田貫湖.access_car: About 40 minutes from the Shin-Fuji IC on the Shin-Tomei Expressway
田貫湖.tagline: Stand at this broad reservoir on the Asagiri Plateau for the full sweep of upside-down Mount Fuji and a golden shoreline corridor.
田貫湖.desc:
Set on the wide Asagiri Plateau, Lake Tanuki is a natural reservoir famous nationwide for its picture-perfect reflections of Mount Fuji. From early to mid-November, the maples and beeches around its gentle shoreline reach peak color, dressing this scenic spot in a spectrum of hues.

The signature shot combines a majestic Mount Fuji — sometimes even "Diamond Fuji" — with a mirror-still lake reflecting both mountain and foliage. Ribbons of red and gold line the calm water, and when conditions are right the surface reflects Fuji and the surrounding trees in perfect symmetry.

The lakeside road is well maintained with a comfortable waterside boardwalk, making it ideal for a relaxed bike ride or camping trip. Mornings and evenings can be windy and chilly at this plateau lake, so bring a warm layer. Go early on a calm, clear morning for the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection.

香嵐溪.types: Iroha maple, Ōmomiji maple, and 11 maple varieties in all
香嵐溪.address: 愛知縣豐田市足助町飯盛
香嵐溪.access_train: About 70 minutes by bus from Higashi-Okazaki Station on the Meitetsu Line
香嵐溪.access_car: About 15 minutes from the Chikaraishi IC on the Sanage Green Road (extremely congested during peak foliage season)
香嵐溪.tagline: Visit the Tokai region's top foliage destination and lose yourself in 4,000 illuminated maples framing the Kourankei Bridge over the Tomoe River.
香嵐溪.desc:
Kourankei is a dramatic gorge carved by the Tomoe River in Toyota's Asuke district, and one of Japan's most celebrated foliage destinations. From mid to late November, around 4,000 maples of 11 varieties — first planted generations ago by the 11th abbot of Kojaku-ji Temple and local residents — reach their peak.

The signature scene is the bright red Kourankei suspension bridge arcing over the clear Tomoe River, framed by a cascade of red and gold maples. Once the night illumination switches on, the whole hillside glows gold — a genuinely poetic sight.

As a top Tokai attraction, roads around the area get badly congested during peak season. Trails along both banks of the river include natural stone paths and historic stone steps, so wear comfortable, non-slip shoes. Go on a weekday morning to beat the crowds and get clean, uncluttered shots.

德川園.hours: 09:30–17:30 (extended to around 20:00 with illumination during foliage season)
德川園.address: 愛知縣名古屋市東區德川町1001
德川園.access_train: About 10 minutes on foot from Ozone Station on the JR Chuo Main Line
德川園.access_car: About 15 minutes from the Kurokawa IC or Horita IC on the Nagoya Expressway
德川園.tagline: Step into the strolling garden of the Owari Tokugawa clan and see maples mirrored perfectly on Lake Ryusen beside the Kansenro pavilion.
德川園.desc:
Tokugawaen is a pond-strolling garden built by Tokugawa Mitsutomo, second lord of the Owari domain, and it still captures the full grandeur of an Edo-period daimyo's estate. From late November to early December, hundreds of Japanese maples throughout the garden reach their peak, giving this historic site an elegant, classical air.

The visual centerpiece is the pond itself: colorful maples line the gravel paths, and when Lake Ryusen turns glassy-still, it perfectly mirrors the grand Kansenro pavilion and the surrounding foliage — a spacious, quietly elegant composition.
