The garden's gravel paths are flat and well maintained, making it easy going for elderly visitors and strollers alike. During the foliage festival, evening illumination makes the reflections even more ethereal. Arrive right at opening on a weekday for the emptiest shots of the historic buildings.

常陸海濱公園.address: 茨城縣ひたちなか市馬渡字大沼605-4
常陸海濱公園.access_train: About 15 minutes by bus from JR Katsuta Station
常陸海濱公園.access_car: Directly accessible from the Hitachi Kaihin Koen IC on the Hitachinaka Toll Road
常陸海濱公園.tagline: Waves of kochia turn coral red — the dreamiest hillside of autumn.
常陸海濱公園.desc: Hitachi Seaside Park is famous across Japan for its 3.5-hectare hillside of kochia bushes. Every October, the kochia blanketing Miharashi Hill turns a deep coral red, looking from a distance like a wave of fire spreading across the horizon. Paired with fields of cosmos blooming at the same time, it's one of Japan's most talked-about autumn photo spots — visit on a weekday to avoid the crowds.

袋田瀑布.address: 茨城縣久慈郡大子町袋田3-19
袋田瀑布.access_train: About 10 minutes by bus from JR Fukuroda Station
袋田瀑布.access_car: About 50 minutes from the Naka IC on the Joban Expressway
袋田瀑布.tagline: One of Japan's three great waterfalls, its four tiers framed by a mountainside of color.
袋田瀑布.desc: Fukuroda Falls is one of Japan's three great waterfalls, cascading down in four dramatic tiers. In autumn, the maples on the slopes on either side turn red from the top down, and from the viewing platform the falls and foliage blend into one seamless scene — Ibaraki's most spectacular autumn spectacle. Walk through the viewing tunnel and up to the second observation deck for different angles on the layered panorama.

足利花卉公園.types: Maple and various color-changing plants (famous for night illumination)
足利花卉公園.access_train: About 3 minutes on foot from Ashikaga Flower Park Station on the JR Ryomo Line
足利花卉公園.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Sano-Fujioka IC on the Tohoku Expressway
足利花卉公園.tagline: Wander this Hibiya Kadan-designed garden paradise, where autumn color and thousands of lights perform together against a backdrop of late hydrangea blooms.
足利花卉公園.desc:
Ashikaga Flower Park is world-famous for its spring wisteria, but come November its autumn foliage and hydrangea take center stage instead. Thousands of carefully placed trees blaze across the open grounds, then hand off seamlessly to one of Japan's top winter illumination displays, lighting up the elegant European-style gardens.

The signature sight is the reflection of the night illumination on the ponds: maples lit in rainbow colors mirror off the still water alongside floating lights, and as a breeze ripples the surface, the whole scene takes on a magical, painterly quality.

The park's paths are flat, barrier-free, and easy going for elderly visitors and strollers. Aim to arrive around 4pm so you can catch the vivid foliage in daylight before sunset, then stay for the striking moment when the lights first switch on.

高尾山.address: 東京都八王子市高尾町
高尾山.access_train: Get off at Takaosanguchi Station on the Keio Takao Line — the trailhead is right there
高尾山.access_car: About 5 minutes from the Takaosan IC on the Ken-O Expressway (parking fills up quickly)
高尾山.tagline: Climb this Michelin Green Guide three-star sacred mountain and ride the cable car through a tunnel of maple color to the hidden foliage of Yakuoin Temple.
高尾山.desc:
Awarded three stars in the Michelin Green Guide, Mount Takao is a beloved sacred mountain right on Tokyo's doorstep. Thanks to its variety of maples, from mid to late November the Iroha maples lining the trails and surrounding Yakuoin Temple all turn together, transforming this near-city peak into a gorgeous autumn forest.

The signature experience is riding the Takaosan cable car, said to be the steepest funicular railway in Japan. As it climbs, walls of maple color press in on both sides of the window — a slow-motion ride through a tunnel graded from yellow to red.

As one of the most accessible foliage spots from central Tokyo, the popular Trail No. 1 and cable car station see long lines on weekends. The temple grounds are mostly well-maintained stone paths, easy to walk. For people-free shots of the old buildings, get there before 8am on a weekday.

明治神宮外苑銀杏並木.address: 東京都新宿區霞丘町至港區北青山
明治神宮外苑銀杏並木.access_train: About 5 minutes on foot from Aoyama-itchome Station or Gaienmae Station on the subway
明治神宮外苑銀杏並木.access_car: Located in central Tokyo — taking the subway is strongly recommended
明治神宮外苑銀杏並木.tagline: Stroll the 300-meter avenue off Aoyama-dori and take in a golden tunnel framing the Meiji Memorial Picture Gallery.
明治神宮外苑銀杏並木.desc:
The Meiji Jingu Gaien Ginkgo Avenue is a world-famous, iconic tree-lined boulevard listed among Japan's 100 Best Roads. From late November to early December, its 146 towering ginkgo trees — trimmed into distinctive cone shapes along a 300-meter stretch — turn a solid wall of gold.

The main draw is the composition itself: four rows of manicured ginkgo lining a grand avenue, with the stately domed Meiji Memorial Picture Gallery framed at the far end. Walking the flat central path, golden branches arch overhead against the distant building — polished, modern, unmistakably Tokyo.

Right in the heart of the city, the avenue is easy to reach and stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. On select weekends during peak season, the city closes it to traffic for a pedestrian-only zone — well worth timing your visit around. For the crispest light, arrive at dawn on a weekday.

國營昭和紀念公園.count: About 100 ginkgo trees along the avenue, about 300 maples
國營昭和紀念公園.hours: 09:30–16:30 (extended hours with night illumination during foliage season)
國營昭和紀念公園.access_train: Right outside Nishi-Tachikawa Station on the JR Ome Line
國營昭和紀念公園.access_car: About 15 minutes from the Kunitachi-Fuchu IC on the Chuo Expressway
國營昭和紀念公園.tagline: Walk two golden corridors through Tachikawa and marvel at a canal lined with a carpet of vivid yellow leaves.
國營昭和紀念公園.desc:
Sprawling across an area 39 times the size of Tokyo Dome, Showa Kinen Park is one of the Kanto region's defining autumn landmarks. From early to mid-November, its two great ginkgo avenues take turns reaching peak color, their towering trees turning a solid, radiant gold.

The centerpiece is where the Tachikawa Gate fountain canal meets a golden tunnel of trees. Walking the 200-meter waterway, neatly trimmed ginkgo arch overhead on both sides, mirrored by the clear water and a European-style fountain; once the leaves start falling, the ground turns into a thick yellow carpet — a striking sight either way.

Given the park's huge size, renting a bike at one of the entrances is the easiest way to get around. The overlap between ginkgo and maple season is the year's busiest stretch, with big weekend crowds — seasoned photographers recommend arriving right at opening on a weekday for shots of the empty carpet of leaves.

箱根.types: Iroha maple, mountain cherry, Fuji cherry
箱根.hours: 24 hours (pirate ship cruise and ropeway operate until around 17:00)
箱根.address: 神奈川縣足柄下郡箱根町
箱根.access_train: Transfer to a Hakone Tozan Bus or the Hakone Tozan Railway from Odawara Station or Hakone-Yumoto Station
箱根.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Hakone-guchi IC on the Odawara-Atsugi Road
箱根.tagline: Ride the Hakone Tozan Railway through hot-spring hills and catch Mount Fuji framed by the vermilion torii at Lake Ashi.
箱根.desc:
The Hakone hot-spring region is a sprawling resort area combining an active volcano, historic sites, and art museums. From mid to late November, maples all along the Hakone Tozan Railway line — from Gora Park down to the shores of Lake Ashi — turn one after another, washing the whole mountainside in deep autumn color.

The classic composition pairs Mount Fuji with Hakone Shrine's iconic torii gate standing in the water. From the shore of Lake Ashi, you can frame Fuji's distant peak, the sacred torii, and red maples swaying at the water's edge all in one shot — a scene that balances grandeur with intimacy.

Hakone is large and its sights spread out, so it's worth buying a Hakone Free Pass to get around easily by pirate ship cruise and ropeway. Popular roads jam up during foliage season, so plan for two days if you can. Lake Ashi is calmest in the early morning — your best shot at a perfect reflection of Fuji and the maples.

上高地.count: Old-growth forest of the Japan Alps
上高地.address: 長野縣松本市安曇上高地
上高地.access_train: About 65 minutes by bus from Shin-Shimashima Station on the Matsumoto Dentetsu Line
上高地.access_car: Private cars are banned; park at Sawando or Hirayu and transfer to a bus
上高地.tagline: Walk the "path of the gods" through Chubu-Sangaku National Park and catch the clear Azusa River, Lake Taisho, and golden larches.
上高地.desc:
Sitting in a highland valley at roughly 1,500 meters, Kamikochi is a Special Scenic Spot nicknamed the "path of the gods." From mid to late October, the larches and Erman's birches here reach their peak, turning the whole pristine valley a radiant gold — about as ethereal as autumn scenery gets.

The classic frame combines the blue Azusa River, the snow-capped Hotaka peaks, and golden foliage. Walking the flat, well-kept boardwalks, you can shoot the landmark Kappabashi Bridge with the mountains rising behind it, or head to still Lake Taisho for reflections of bare trees and colorful hillsides on the water.

To protect the fragile ecosystem, private cars are banned throughout — you'll need to switch to an eco-friendly shuttle bus at a designated transfer point. The highland trails are flat but cold and somewhat rocky, so hiking shoes are recommended. Come on a weekday morning for the most ethereal shots, when mist often still lingers.

千疊敷窪地.hours: First ropeway car around 08:00 (varies by season)
千疊敷窪地.fee: Free (ropeway plus bus round-trip for adults about ¥4,000)
千疊敷窪地.access_train: About 45 minutes by bus from JR Komagane Station to the ropeway station
千疊敷窪地.access_car: Private cars are banned; park at Suganodai and transfer to a bus
千疊敷窪地.tagline: Take the Central Alps ropeway straight up to this sky-high cirque for Japan's earliest gold beneath the jagged peak of Mt. Hoken.
千疊敷窪地.desc:
The Senjojiki Cirque is a huge bowl-shaped basin carved by glaciers 20,000 years ago, sitting at 2,612 meters. Thanks to its elevation, this is where the color starts earliest in the Kanto region — from early to mid-September, the alpine plants covering the basin's slopes turn a solid gold.

The real impact comes from the contrast between Mt. Hoken's raw rock face and the sweeping cirque below it, carpeted in color. Riding the Central Alps Ropeway up, you get a bird's-eye view of a rolling patchwork of yellow and red stretched across the valley floor — genuinely striking.

This is serious high-mountain terrain — by late September, summit temperatures are already in the single digits with strong, near-constant wind, so bring proper hiking boots and a windproof, insulated jacket. A loop trail through the cirque takes about 40 minutes to walk. Go up on a clear morning for the best visibility.

白駒之池.types: Japanese rowan, Ōmomiji maple, Erman's birch
白駒之池.count: Old-growth forest and moss above 2,100 meters elevation
白駒之池.address: 長野縣南佐久郡小海町・佐久穂町
白駒之池.access_train: About 60 minutes by Mugikusa Pass Line bus from JR Chino Station
白駒之池.access_car: About 30 minutes from the Yachiho Kogen IC on the Chubu-Odan Expressway
白駒之池.tagline: Step into a pristine, moss-covered forest in the northern Yatsugatake range and find Japan's highest-elevation natural lake ringed with red maple.
白駒之池.desc:
Set deep in the old-growth forest of the northern Yatsugatake mountains at 2,115 meters, Shirakoma-no-Ike is Japan's largest natural lake above 2,000 meters elevation. From mid-September to early October, the maples and Erman's birches around the shore are among the first to turn, blanketing the plateau in rich early-autumn color.

The scene here is layered: a carpet of green moss, deep primeval forest, and fiery red maple all at once. Walking the well-maintained boardwalks, you pass golden foliage nestled among hundreds of rare moss species and towering ancient trees, and when the clear water perfectly mirrors the colors above, the effect is genuinely otherworldly.

It's only about a 15-minute walk from the parking lot to the lake, on a flat, easy boardwalk suitable for the whole family. Temperatures at this altitude run cold, so bring a warm, windproof jacket. Visit on a weekday morning for the most serene, meditative atmosphere.

河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.count: About 60 large maples along a 150-meter corridor
河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.address: 山梨縣南都留郡富士河口湖町河口
河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.access_train: About 20 minutes by the Kawaguchiko Sightseeing Bus from Kawaguchiko Station on the Fujikyu Line
河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.access_car: About 15 minutes from the Kawaguchiko IC on the Chuo Expressway
河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.tagline: Walk the north shore of Fuji Five Lakes and pass beneath a tunnel of maples lining the Nashigawa River.
河口湖（紅葉迴廊）.desc:
Lake Kawaguchi is a hugely popular destination built around views of Mount Fuji, and the Momiji Corridor on its north shore is the main autumn draw. From early to mid-November, maples lining several hundred meters of the Nashigawa River turn together, their branches meeting overhead in a deep red tunnel that adds even more drama to the Fuji backdrop.

The showstopper shot combines Mount Fuji, the river's reflections, and a wall of color all in one frame. Walking the flat central path, gold and red branches arch together overhead, and once the night illumination comes on, dreamlike light plays across the foliage for a genuinely magical scene.

As a world-famous spot, it sees heavy traffic and tour groups during the festival — leave early and aim to arrive at dawn on a weekday. The path is flat throughout and stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. Early weekday mornings offer the calmest, most peaceful atmosphere for photos.

清津峽.count: Old-growth valley forest paired with an art installation tunnel
清津峽.address: 新潟縣十日町市小出癸2119-2
清津峽.access_train: About 25 minutes by bus from JR Echigo-Yuzawa Station
清津峽.access_car: About 25 minutes from the Echigo-Yuzawa IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
清津峽.tagline: Walk into a mirrored tunnel inside one of Japan's three great gorges and take in the Tunnel of Light against a V-shaped cliff of color.
清津峽.desc:
Kiyotsukyo is a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty carved by the Kiyotsu River, and one of Japan's three great gorges alongside Kurobe and Osugidani. From late October to early November, the beech and maple trees towering over its steep, columnar-jointed cliffs turn a solid, brilliant gold.

The scene that made this place internet-famous is the "Tunnel of Light," designed by architect Ma Yansong. At the viewing platform inside, a semicircular pool of water perfectly mirrors the steep gray cliffs, jade-green river, and layered autumn color outside — an imposing, cinematic composition.

The gorge path has been rebuilt into a flat, safe, semi-enclosed viewing tunnel, so it's easy walking regardless of weather. During peak season, entry is fully reservation-based for safety, so check the official website before you go. Visit around midday, when sunlight reaches the valley floor and the color is at its most saturated.

定山溪.count: Throughout the hot-spring town and surrounding gorge
定山溪.hours: 24 hours (foliage shuttle bus runs until around 15:00)
定山溪.address: 北海道札幌市南區定山溪溫泉
定山溪.access_train: About 60 minutes by bus bound for Jozankei-shako-mae from JR Sapporo Station
定山溪.access_car: About 50 minutes from central Sapporo via Route 230
定山溪.tagline: Wander this hot-spring gorge on Sapporo's doorstep and catch the vermilion Futami Suspension Bridge mirrored beneath a mountainside of maple.
定山溪.desc:
Jozankei Onsen sits upstream on the Toyohira River on Sapporo's outskirts, and it's one of Hokkaido's signature gorge foliage spots. From early to mid-October, the forest surrounding the hot-spring town reaches its peak, blanketing the green ravine in every shade of red and gold.

The classic shot pairs the bright red Futami Suspension Bridge with the surrounding gorge in full color. It arcs over the clear river above cliffs cascading with red and gold rowan trees, and when the Toyohira River lies still, it mirrors both the cliffs and the foliage in a wide, poetic composition.

Weekends during peak season bring big crowds of drivers and onsen-town strollers, so get to the trails early on a weekday if you can. It's shaded and cool here, making it a great spot for a relaxing hot-spring day trip. Morning light filtering through the trees onto the river gives the best light for landscape photography.

北海道大學銀杏並木.address: 北海道札幌市北區北13條西5～7丁目
北海道大學銀杏並木.access_train: About 5 minutes on foot from Kita-Junijo Station on the Namboku subway line
北海道大學銀杏並木.access_car: General vehicles are not allowed on campus; use nearby paid parking lots
北海道大學銀杏並木.tagline: Walk through Sapporo's academic heart under a 300-meter golden tunnel that sheds into a carpet of leaves underfoot.
北海道大學銀杏並木.desc:
Hokkaido University's Ginkgo Avenue peaks each year from late October to early November, when its 70 towering ginkgo trees turn a brilliant, uniform gold, setting an unmistakably romantic autumn mood. Thanks to the trees' age and uniform planting, the color's intensity and scale are famous throughout northern Japan.

The centerpiece is a 300-meter golden tunnel. Walking the flat campus avenue, dense golden branches arch together overhead, making it feel like an endless corridor of color. Later in the season, the leaves carpet the ground in thick gold, which is just as striking as the canopy above.

Located right in central Sapporo, the avenue is easily accessible, free, and paved with flat, well-kept paths. On select weekends during foliage season, the campus closes the road to vehicles — worth timing your visit around. Arrive at dawn on a weekday for the quietest atmosphere and the best light.

奧入瀨溪流.address: 青森縣十和田市大字奧瀨
奧入瀨溪流.access_train: About 120 minutes by JR bus toward Lake Towada from JR Hachinohe Station or Aomori Station
奧入瀨溪流.access_car: Traffic control is in effect during peak foliage season; park at a designated lot and transfer to a shuttle bus
奧入瀨溪流.tagline: Wander Towada-Hachimantai National Park and lose yourself in moss-covered streams beneath a tunnel of golden beech.
奧入瀨溪流.desc:
The Oirase Gorge stream is a top-tier ecological corridor, designated both a Special Place of Scenic Beauty and a Natural Monument. From mid to late October, the trees lining its 14-kilometer length reach peak color, turning towering beech and maple a brilliant gold — quintessential northern Japan in early autumn.

The signature combination here is rushing waterfalls, ancient moss, and red maple all together. Walking the flat, well-kept trails, you'll pass rapids like the Ashura-no-Nagare, throwing up white spray against mossy rocks and leaf-strewn banks framed by colorful trees — polished, natural beauty.

The trail stretches on for miles but stays completely flat, making it ideal for an easy hike or a rented bike. Moisture left over from the rainy season sharpens the contrast between moss and foliage, and cool early mornings are best, when sunlight filtering through the canopy creates the prettiest dappled light.

弘前公園.types: Iroha maple, cherry (red autumn cherry leaves)
弘前公園.address: 青森縣弘前市下白銀町1
弘前公園.access_train: About 15 minutes by loop bus from JR Hirosaki Station
弘前公園.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Owani-Hirosaki IC on the Tohoku Expressway
弘前公園.tagline: Wander the grounds of Hirosaki Castle's three-story keep and catch a red bridge mirrored in a moat lined with maple.
弘前公園.desc:
Hirosaki Park occupies the grounds of the historic Edo-period Hirosaki Castle, blending nature and history in equal measure. From late October to mid-November, about 1,000 maples and 2,600 cherry trees turn together, dressing the castle's imposing stone walls in early-autumn color.

The classic view pairs the old moat with the surrounding foliage: colorful trees line the gentle waterway, and when the water lies still, it perfectly mirrors the vermilion Gejobashi Bridge, the original Edo-period wooden keep, and the trees around them — an elegant, distinctly Japanese composition.

The park is completely flat, with well-maintained paths along the moat, easy going for elderly visitors and those pushing strollers. During the foliage festival, evening illumination makes the reflections even more dreamlike. Weekday mornings see the fewest visitors and offer the best chance at a perfect mirror shot.

八幡平.count: Vast old-growth highland forest spanning two prefectures
八幡平.hours: 24 hours (winter road closure: early November to mid-April)
八幡平.address: 岩手縣八幡平市至秋田縣鹿角市
八幡平.access_train: About 120 minutes by bus toward Hachimantai-chojo from JR Morioka Station
八幡平.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Matsuo-Hachimantai IC on the Tohoku Expressway
八幡平.tagline: Drive the scenic road through Towada-Hachimantai National Park and take in the marshy shores of Lake Onuma turned red with autumn grasses.
八幡平.desc:
Hachimantai is a broad shield-volcano plateau spanning Iwate and Akita prefectures, reaching 1,613 meters at its highest. Because of its elevation and latitude, color arrives early here — from late September to early October, the alpine plants around its volcanic marshes and plains are among the first in the region to turn, blanketing the plateau in deep autumn hues.

The highlight is a slow drive along the Hachimantai Aspite Line. The road runs through golden foliage tucked among towering Erman's birch and beech, and the marsh grasses around famous Lake Onuma turn a deep red — a scene that captures the wild beauty of the northern highlands perfectly.

At this altitude, summit temperatures are already in the single digits by late September, so bring a proper windproof, insulated jacket. A gentle boardwalk circles Lake Onuma, and weekday mornings see the fewest visitors — ideal for an unhurried walk and some nature photography.

中尊寺.count: Several hundred trees along the Tsukimizaka approach and temple grounds
中尊寺.address: 岩手縣西磐井郡平泉町平泉衣關202
中尊寺.access_train: About 20 minutes on foot from JR Hiraizumi Station, or 5 minutes by loop bus
中尊寺.access_car: About 10 minutes from the Hiraizumi-Maesawa IC on the Tohoku Expressway
中尊寺.tagline: Climb to this UNESCO World Heritage site in Hiraizumi and walk the maple-lined Tsukimizaka approach to the National Treasure Konjikido Hall.
中尊寺.desc:
Chusonji is a storied head temple of the Tendai sect founded by the priest Jikaku Daishi, and a UNESCO World Heritage site. From early to mid-November, several hundred Iroha maples around the solemn main hall and deep temple grounds turn together, dressing this sacred site in dazzling color.

The classic composition brings together the National Treasure covered hall, ancient moss, and a maple-lined approach. Vivid color crowds both sides of the long, cedar-flanked stone steps of the Tsukimizaka approach, set off by old stone lanterns — a scene that captures the quiet, historic calm of an ancient temple.

The path from the main gate to the hall is a long, gently sloped stone track, so wear shoes with good grip. During the foliage festival, evening illumination lets visitors view the grounds at night. Weekday mornings right at opening offer the calmest atmosphere for photographing the historic buildings.

鳴子峽.count: Extensive foliage along a gorge up to 100 meters deep
鳴子峽.address: 宮城縣大崎市鳴子溫泉星沼
鳴子峽.access_train: About 30 minutes on foot from JR Nakayamadaira-Onsen Station, or take a seasonal bus from Naruko-Onsen Station
鳴子峽.access_car: About 50 minutes from the Furukawa IC on the Tohoku Expressway
鳴子峽.tagline: Listen to the roar of the Oya River far below and take in the Ofukazawa Bridge against a mountainside layered in color.
鳴子峽.desc:
Naruko Gorge is a dramatic ravine up to 100 meters deep, carved over the years by the Oya River. From late October to early November, thousands of maples and beeches around its steep white cliffs turn together, blanketing the whole gorge in color.

The iconic shot pairs the Ofukazawa Bridge with the colorful gorge behind it. From the observation deck, the massive concrete arch bridge spans cliffs streaked with color, and if you time it right, you can catch a JR Rikuu East Line train emerging from a tunnel and threading through the foliage — a wonderfully retro scene.

As one of Tohoku's top foliage spots, the Nakayamadaira-side observation deck fills with photographers from around the world during peak season. The Ofukazawa Trail has some ups and downs, so wear comfortable walking shoes. Go on a weekday morning to avoid the crowds and get the clearest view of the gorge.

秋保大瀑布.count: Old-growth forest surrounding the scenic falls
秋保大瀑布.address: 宮城縣仙台市太白區秋保町馬場大瀧
秋保大瀑布.access_train: About 90 minutes by bus toward Akiu Otaki from JR Sendai Station
秋保大瀑布.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Sendai-Minami IC on the Tohoku Expressway
秋保大瀑布.tagline: Listen to the roar of one of Japan's 100 best waterfalls, framed by a scenic gorge layered in autumn color.
秋保大瀑布.desc:
Deep in the hot-spring town of Akiu, Akiu Otaki is a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty and one of Japan's 100 best waterfalls, dropping 55 meters. From late October to early November, thousands of maples and beeches around the falls and the Natori River gorge burst into full color.

The dominant image is the thundering falls set against a valley wall draped floor-to-ceiling in color. The waterfall crashes down with tremendous force, and below it the slope is blanketed in a dense tapestry of red and gold foliage — a composition that balances raw power with soft color across a huge frame.

The path down to the base of the falls is mostly natural dirt track with steep, loose stone steps, and constant spray keeps it slippery year-round, so wear proper non-slip hiking shoes. If you'd rather take it easy, the well-maintained Takimidai viewing trail up top is an option — weekday mornings offer the best light.

角館武家屋敷.count: About 400 maples lining the historic street
角館武家屋敷.address: 秋田縣仙北市角館町表町至東勝樂丁
角館武家屋敷.access_train: About 20 minutes on foot from JR Kakunodate Station
角館武家屋敷.access_car: About 40 minutes from the Omagari IC on the Akita Expressway
角館武家屋敷.tagline: A samurai street turns red, blending Edo-era charm with autumn color.
角館武家屋敷.desc: Kakunodate is home to one of Japan's best-preserved samurai residence districts, and when the maples turn, their crimson leaves set off the neighborhood's black wooden walls in dramatic contrast. Walking through the Uchimachi district, branches from century-old trees meet overhead to form a canopy of gold and red — one of Tohoku's signature foliage walks.

小安峽.count: Old-growth forest along both banks near the Ofuruyu geyser
小安峽.address: 秋田縣湯澤市皆瀨新處
小安峽.access_train: About 50 minutes by bus from JR Yuzawa Station
小安峽.access_car: About 40 minutes from the Yuzawa IC on the Yuzawa-Yokote Road
小安峽.tagline: A geyser rising from the gorge floor, ringed on all sides by autumn color.
小安峽.desc: Oyasukyo is a striking gorge cut by the Minase River through a lava plateau, its cliff walls venting hot spring steam year-round for a distinctly geothermal landscape. During foliage season, follow the cliffside trail down and you'll find waterfalls and mountains of color closing in from every side — a very different kind of autumn thrill.

山寺（立石寺）.count: Spread along the full 1,015-step stone staircase
山寺（立石寺）.access_train: About 7 minutes on foot from Yamadera Station on the JR Senzan Line to the trailhead
山寺（立石寺）.access_car: About 20 minutes from the Yamagata-Kita IC on the Yamagata Expressway
山寺（立石寺）.tagline: A thousand stone steps turn autumn red at the site Basho immortalized in verse.
山寺（立石寺）.desc: Founded in 860, Risshakuji Temple — better known as Yamadera — sits above a climb of 1,015 stone steps flanked by pine and maple. In autumn, deep red and gold spread across its dramatic rock faces in layers. The view over the basin below inspired Matsuo Basho's famous haiku about cicada song sinking into the rocks — and in fall, the scene is even more poetic.

銀山溫泉.count: Natural forest of Shirogane Park behind the hot-spring street
銀山溫泉.address: 山形縣尾花澤市大字銀山新畑
銀山溫泉.access_train: About 40 minutes by bus from JR Oishida Station
銀山溫泉.access_car: General vehicles are not allowed into the hot-spring street; park at a designated lot and transfer to a shuttle
銀山溫泉.tagline: A Taisho-era streetscape where autumn leaves and gas lamps combine for a dreamlike night.
銀山溫泉.desc: Ginsan Onsen is a hot-spring street famous for its Taisho-era, Western-influenced wooden ryokan, built along the Ginzan River. After dark, gas lamps light up and reflect on the flowing water below. In autumn, maples above the inns turn red, and the color glows against the street lamps for a scene that feels like stepping back in time — one of Japan's most talked-about autumn night views.

磐梯吾妻 Skyline.address: 福島縣福島市町庭坂至土湯溫泉町
磐梯吾妻 Skyline.access_train: Seasonal sightseeing bus from JR Fukushima Station
磐梯吾妻 Skyline.access_car: About 30 minutes from the Fukushima-Nishi IC on the Tohoku Expressway
磐梯吾妻 Skyline.tagline: Panoramic foliage along a highland road, flanked by raw volcanic scenery.
磐梯吾妻 Skyline.desc: The Bandai Azuma Skyline is a roughly 29-kilometer highland scenic road passing through the volcanic terrain of Jododaira and the Takayu hot-spring area — Fukushima's most dramatic foliage drive. In early November, the shrubs and birch forest along the route are the first to turn, their gold and orange standing out sharply against the barren volcanic landscape; on a clear day, you can even see the Pacific Ocean in the distance.

五色沼.address: 福島縣耶麻郡北鹽原村大字檜原
五色沼.access_train: About 30 minutes by bus from JR Inawashiro Station
五色沼.access_car: About 25 minutes from the Inawashiro-Bandai-Kogen IC on the Ban-etsu Expressway
五色沼.tagline: Emerald, indigo, jade — autumn leaves mirrored across a cluster of mysteriously colored ponds.
五色沼.desc: The Goshikinuma ponds are a cluster of small lakes scattered through the forest of the Urabandai area, their waters taking on shades of blue, green, and emerald thanks to dissolved minerals and light refraction. In autumn, vivid maple color rings the ponds and reflects off their tinted surfaces for a genuinely dreamlike scene. The roughly 3.6-kilometer nature trail is the easiest way to link the ponds together on foot.

層雲峽.types: Iroha maple, Ōmomiji maple, Japanese rowan
層雲峽.count: 24 kilometers of sheer cliffs, with the showpiece Ryusei and Ginga waterfalls
層雲峽.address: 北海道上川郡上川町層雲峽
層雲峽.access_train: About 35 minutes by bus from JR Kamikawa Station
層雲峽.access_car: About 25 minutes from the Kamikawa-Sounkyo IC on the Asahikawa-Monbetsu Expressway
層雲峽.tagline: Look up at the cliffs of Daisetsuzan National Park and ride the Kurodake Ropeway over towering conifers and a fiery waterfall gorge.
層雲峽.desc:
Souunkyou lies upstream on the Ishikari River, a gorge known for 24 kilometers of massive columnar-jointed cliffs. From late September to early October, thousands of rowan and maple trees around its steep gray rock faces turn together, filling the deep valley at the foot of Mount Daisetsu with color.

The most striking sight pairs the twin waterfalls — Ryusei (Shooting Star) and Ginga (Milky Way) — with the surrounding color. From the viewing platform, both cascade down a hundred-meter cliff streaked red with foliage. Ride the Kurodake Ropeway up and you'll also get a bird's-eye view of a patchwork of colorful plains and dark conifer forest below.

As one of the earliest foliage spots in northern Japan, temperatures here are already close to freezing by early October, so bring a proper windproof, insulated jacket. The gorge trail is flat and easy, and a clear morning with good visibility is your best bet — that's when light reaches the valley floor and the colors look their richest.

阿寒湖.count: Natural lakeside forest turning red; the famous Takiguchi outlet is a top photo spot
阿寒湖.address: 北海道釧路市阿寒町阿寒湖溫泉
阿寒湖.access_train: About 2 hours by bus from JR Kushiro Station
阿寒湖.tagline: Stand in this volcanic corner of eastern Hokkaido and take in Mount O-Akan, an old hot-spring town, and a shoreline of autumn color.
阿寒湖.desc:
Lake Akan is a natural caldera lake within Akan-Mashu National Park, famous for its marimo — the round green algae balls designated a Natural Monument. From early to mid-October, the Japanese maples and beeches around its wide shoreline reach peak foliage, dressing this historic northern hot-spring retreat in a spectrum of color.

The classic view combines Takimi Bridge with the headwaters of the Akan River. Standing on the rustic bridge, you can watch clear rapids throw up white spray as they cut through gold and crimson maple forest. Taking a boat out on the lake, you can also frame the blue water together with towering Mount O-Akan behind it.

The area around the lakeside hot-spring town is flat with well-maintained paths, making it a great spot for an easy family walk in early autumn. Mornings and evenings in eastern Hokkaido can be windy and cold, so bring warm, windproof layers. Go on a clear morning for the calmest water and the best reflections of the surrounding color.

五稜郭公園.count: The star-shaped fort turns red and orange with maple and cherry leaves
五稜郭公園.address: 北海道函館市五稜郭町44
五稜郭公園.access_train: About 15 minutes on foot from the Goryokaku-koen-mae streetcar stop
五稜郭公園.tagline: Climb Hakodate's star-shaped fortress and look down on 1,600 trees forming a giant red-and-gold star.
五稜郭公園.desc:
Goryokaku Park is a Special Historic Site built as a Western-style star-shaped fort. From mid-October to early November, its roughly 1,600 Somei-yoshino cherry trees turn together, dressing this solemn site from the final days of the shogunate in deep autumn color.

The main draw is the view from the Goryokaku Tower observation deck. From 107 meters up, you can take in the entire moat-ringed star shape below, its clean lines traced out in a gradient of red and gold — an entirely different, equally striking beauty from its cherry-blossom self in spring.

The park itself is completely flat, with barrier-free paths along the moat, easy going for elderly visitors and strollers. For a clean reflection of the star shape, visit early in the morning when the wind is calm. In the afternoon and evening, low, slanting light filtering through the maples gives the best conditions for landscape photography.

大沼國定公園.count: 126 islets set against Mount Komagatake, reflected on the water
大沼國定公園.address: 北海道龜田郡七飯町大沼町
大沼國定公園.access_train: About 5 minutes on foot from JR Onuma-koen Station
大沼國定公園.tagline: Wander this waterside park at the foot of Mount Komagatake and catch wooden bridges linking islets beneath a mirror of autumn color.
大沼國定公園.desc:
Onuma Quasi-National Park, ranked among Japan's New Three Views, is a sprawling waterside park built around Lake Onuma, Lake Konuma, and the towering volcano Mount Komagatake. From mid to late October, the 126 islets scattered across the water and the maples ringing the shore reach their peak, dressing the waterfront in every shade of color.

The scene here brings together the volcano backdrop, the lake, and wooden bridges linking the islets. Red and gold trees line the gravel paths as you cross classic arched bridges between islands, and when the water stills, it perfectly mirrors both Mount Komagatake and the surrounding foliage — a spacious, crisp composition.

The park is large, so renting a bike at the plaza is the easiest way to explore. The main viewing route and waterside boardwalks are flat and well maintained. The lake is calmest in the early morning, when it's easiest to capture that fresh, open feeling along with a perfect reflection of the foliage.

知床五湖.count: Foliage from primeval forest and surrounding peaks reflected on still lakes
知床五湖.fee: Free (a paid briefing, about ¥250, is required for the ground-level trail)
知床五湖.address: 北海道斜里郡斜里町遠音別村
知床五湖.access_train: About 90 minutes by bus from JR Shiretoko-Shari Station
知床五湖.tagline: Walk through primeval forest in this World Natural Heritage site and take in the Shiretoko mountains from an elevated boardwalk lined with color.
知床五湖.desc:
The Shiretoko Five Lakes sit on the Shiretoko Peninsula, a World Natural Heritage site famous for its pristine ecosystem and resident brown bears. From early to mid-October, the primeval forest ringing five mysterious volcanic lakes turns with the season, washing this remote, unspoiled valley in deep early-autumn color.

The dreamlike view here pairs an elevated boardwalk with the Shiretoko mountains and lake reflections. Walking the 800-meter barrier-free boardwalk, protected by an electric fence, you can frame a wall of foliage in the foreground against the towering Shiretoko range and the blue Sea of Okhotsk beyond — genuinely breathtaking.

To reach any lake beyond the first, you'll need to walk the ground-level trail, which requires advance registration and a paid briefing. Weather up here changes fast and winds run strong, so wear hiking shoes with good grip and bring warm, windproof layers. Weekday mornings offer the most ethereal views, often with lingering mist.

十和田湖.count: A double caldera lake, its red maples ringing the Statue of the Maiden
十和田湖.access_train: About 2–3 hours by bus from JR Hachinohe Station or Aomori Station
十和田湖.tagline: Stand on the shore of this twin volcanic lake, steeped in the legend of Hachiro Taro, beneath a shoreline of golden beech.
十和田湖.desc:
Lake Towada is a vast double caldera lake straddling Aomori and Akita, designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty. From mid to late October, the beech and maple forest along its broad shoreline reaches peak color, dressing the deep blue lake in bold, sweeping color.

The classic view is the panorama from the Hakka Pass observation deck: from this hilltop vantage point, you can frame the distant Mikura Peninsula, the mirror-blue lake, and the color spreading below all in one shot. A sightseeing boat also lets you get up close to the shoreline foliage from the water.

The path around the lake is flat and easy, perfect for a relaxed early-autumn waterside walk. Mornings and evenings can be windy and cold at this elevation, so bring warm, windproof layers. Go on a calm, clear morning for the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection of the surrounding color.

八甲田山.count: A celebrated 360-degree carpet of color with views out to Mutsu Bay
八甲田山.address: 青森縣青森市荒川寒水澤
八甲田山.access_train: About 1 hour by bus from JR Aomori Station to the Hakkoda Ropeway Station
八甲田山.tagline: Visit the peaks where northern Japan's color begins first, and ride the Hakkoda Ropeway over a mountainside carpeted in autumn hues.
八甲田山.desc:
Mount Hakkoda is a dramatic range of active volcanoes and the earliest place in Honshu to see autumn color. From late September to mid-October, the alpine tundra plants at the summit turn first, followed by maple and Erman's birch cascading down the slopes, washing the whole range in deep autumn color.

The must-see experience is riding the Hakkoda Ropeway. As you rise slowly, you look down on a huge natural palette — yellow and red foliage woven through dark green conifer forest across the mountainside — a wide, genuinely striking view.

This is serious high-mountain terrain — summit temperatures are already near freezing by early October, so bring a proper windproof, insulated mountaineering jacket. Weather up here can change fast, so aim for a clear morning with good visibility, when the light brings out the richest color.

城倉大橋.count: 360 meters long, looking down 122 meters into the Joukura Gorge
城倉大橋.address: 青森縣青森市荒川南部
城倉大橋.access_train: About 80 minutes by bus from JR Aomori Station to Joukura Onsen, then 20 minutes on foot
城倉大橋.tagline: Stand on Japan's largest steel-box deck arch bridge for a 360-degree view of the Joukura Gorge in full color.
城倉大橋.desc:
Joukura Ohashi spans the Joukura Gorge for 360 meters, making it Japan's longest steel-box deck arch bridge. Each mid-October, this striking piece of modern engineering is set against the primeval forest turning around it, filling the deep valley with color.

The draw is the sheer scale of the bridge set against the steep, colorful gorge. Standing on the deck a hundred meters up, you look straight down at the fast-dropping Joukura River, flanked by golden beech and fiery maple cascading down the cliffs on either side — a sweeping 360-degree view.

Both ends of the bridge have well-maintained parking and flat walkways, so it's an easy stroll. Wind can be strong up here, so keep a firm grip on hats and tripods. Visit around midday, when sunlight reaches the valley floor and the color looks most vivid.

中野紅葉山.count: Known as "Little Arashiyama," with a waterfall and red torii accenting the maple grove
中野紅葉山.address: 青森縣黑石市中野不動舘27
中野紅葉山.access_train: About 30 minutes by bus from Kuroishi Station on the Konan Railway
中野紅葉山.tagline: Visit Kuroishi's own "Little Arashiyama" and lose yourself in Nakano Shrine, Fudo Falls, and illuminated maples.
中野紅葉山.desc:
Legend has it that Nakano Momijiyama's maples were originally brought from Kyoto by a lord of the Hirosaki domain, making this a historic foliage spot in its own right. From mid-October to early November, several hundred old maples around Nakano Shrine and the Nakano River valley burst into color, dressing this sacred site in vivid hues.

The classic composition brings together a vermilion torii, Fudo Falls, and the surrounding color. Vivid foliage crowds around the rustic wooden shrine buildings, moss-covered stone steps, and the stream, and once the night illumination switches on, the whole hillside turns gold — genuinely mysterious and dreamlike.

The trail winds through natural hills and valley terrain, with some rocky steps and slopes, so wear shoes with good grip. Weekday mornings offer the most solitary, meditative atmosphere, often with mist drifting through the old buildings — ideal for photography.

毛越寺.count: A World Heritage Pure Land garden, its maples reflected in Lake Oizumi
毛越寺.address: 岩手縣西磐井郡平泉町平泉大澤58
毛越寺.access_train: About 10 minutes on foot from JR Hiraizumi Station
毛越寺.tagline: Stroll a Pure Land mandala garden and lose yourself in the maple-lined shores of Lake Oizumi.
毛越寺.desc:
Motsuji is a UNESCO World Heritage temple founded by the priest Jikaku Daishi, celebrated nationwide for its remarkably well-preserved Pure Land garden. From late October to mid-November, the maples ringing the broad Lake Oizumi reach peak color, dressing this classic Japanese garden in vivid hues.

The visual centerpiece is the pond itself, with its curious rock islet and mirror-still reflections. Colorful trees line the gravel paths, and when the water lies perfectly still, it mirrors both the foliage and the distant temple ruins for a wide, quietly elegant composition.

The grounds are flat with fully paved paths, easy going for strollers and visitors with limited mobility. Set aside about an hour to walk through; early mornings see the fewest visitors, and sunlight filtering through the branches onto the foliage makes it the best time for a perfect reflection shot.

嚴美溪.count: Striking boulders and rushing water set off dramatically by autumn color
嚴美溪.address: 岩手縣一關市嚴美町瀧之上
嚴美溪.access_train: About 20 minutes by bus from JR Ichinoseki Station
嚴美溪.tagline: Listen to clear water roar past strange rock formations at the foot of Mount Kurikoma, and try the famous flying dango.
嚴美溪.desc:
Genbikei is a Special Place of Scenic Beauty carved by the Iwai River, known for its dramatic boulders and potholed rock formations. From mid-October to early November, the maples and beeches along both banks turn together, bringing this natural landmark to vivid, colorful life.

The strongest visual pairs crystal-clear water and potholed rock with fiery red maple. From Tenkukyo Bridge, you can watch fast rapids kick up white spray as they thread through golden trees. Don't miss the famous "flying dango" — sweets sent across the gorge on a rope-and-pulley system — a classic part of the experience here.

The gorge trail is flat and well maintained, great for an easy family walk along the river. Since the main viewpoints sit on open rock terraces, bring sun protection, and aim for a morning visit for the most comfortable conditions and the best landscape photography.

猊鼻溪.count: Wooden boat rides threading between cliffs up to 100 meters tall lined with foliage
猊鼻溪.address: 岩手縣一關市東山町長坂字町467
猊鼻溪.access_train: About 5 minutes on foot from JR Geibikei Station
猊鼻溪.tagline: Ride a traditional hand-poled wooden boat into a hundred-meter gorge lined with clear water and golden beech.
猊鼻溪.desc:
Geibikei, listed among Japan's 100 Scenic Spots, is a dramatic gorge carved by the Satetsu River. From mid-October to early November, the maples crowning its gray limestone cliffs — up to 100 meters tall — turn together, filling the deep valley with color.

The signature experience is riding a traditional flat-bottomed wooden boat, hand-poled by a boatman singing folk songs as you glide upstream. The calm, jade-green river runs on one side and cliffs cascading with color rise on the other.

Since the whole area is a deep, natural gorge, riverside winds can be brisk, so bring a light jacket. The round-trip boat ride takes about 90 minutes and the terrain is completely flat, making it great for families. Set out in the morning, when sunlight reaches deepest into the V-shaped valley.

盛岡城跡公園.count: Ancient stone walls interwoven with fiery maple
盛岡城跡公園.access_train: About 10 minutes by loop bus from JR Morioka Station
盛岡城跡公園.tagline: Climb the ruins of the Nanbu clan's Kozukata Castle for a sea of color against imposing granite walls.
盛岡城跡公園.desc:
Morioka Castle Ruins Park sits on the former grounds of the Nanbu clan's Morioka Castle, one of Japan's 100 Fine Castles. From late October to early November, the park's famous foliage rise reaches its peak, with hundreds of Iroha maples bursting into color against the castle's grand stone ramparts.

The visual focus is the contrast between the castle's distinctive granite walls and the surrounding color. Walking the well-kept paths, bright red and deep purple foliage plays off the thick white stone ramparts still standing from the old castle — history and nature in balance.

The park follows the original hilltop castle terrain, so some sections have a slope — wear shoes with good grip. It's spacious, with a large lawn plaza, making for a comfortable walk. Weekday mornings see the fewest visitors, ideal for a relaxed stroll and unhurried photography.

松島（圓通院）.count: Illuminated maples reflected on Kanji Pond after dark
松島（圓通院）.address: 宮城縣宮城郡松島町松島町內67
松島（圓通院）.access_train: About 5 minutes on foot from Matsushima-Kaigan Station on the JR Senseki Line
松島（圓通院）.tagline: Visit the historic temple built for Date Mitsumune and see illuminated maples mirrored across Kanji Pond.
松島（圓通院）.desc:
Entsuin is a historic Rinzai Zen temple in Matsushima, one of Japan's Three Great Views. From late October to late November, several hundred maples across its hillside grounds turn together, bringing this sacred site to vivid, colorful life.

The scene that made this temple famous online is its limited-run night illumination. Standing beside the still Kanji Pond, you can watch crimson maples and the surrounding dry rock garden reflect perfectly on the water. As a breeze ripples the surface, the layered reflections capture the quiet, historic calm of an ancient temple.

The temple grounds are compact and flat, easy to walk, with a full visit taking about 40 minutes. Lines for the night illumination can get very long, so consider a weekday morning right at opening instead, for the cleanest shots of the grounds and their reflections.

定禪寺通.count: Rows of towering zelkova turning gold and orange along the boulevard
定禪寺通.address: 宮城縣仙台市青葉區國分町
定禪寺通.access_train: Right outside Kotodai-koen Station on the subway
定禪寺通.tagline: Stroll the green lungs of downtown Sendai beneath a golden tunnel formed by four rows of towering zelkova.
定禪寺通.desc:
Jozenji-dori is an iconic tree-lined boulevard cutting through the heart of Sendai, listed among Japan's 100 Best Roads. From late October to early November, its 166 towering zelkova trees — planted in four rows along the central walkway — reach peak color, turning a solid, brilliant gold.

The centerpiece is a golden tunnel running the length of the avenue. Walking the flat central path, dense golden branches arch overhead, framed alongside Western-style bronze sculptures dotted through the trees — the polished, modern urban look Sendai, the "City of Trees," is known for.

Located right in the city center, it's easy to reach and well suited to a relaxed morning walk. The avenue is completely flat and stroller- and wheelchair-friendly. Arrive at dawn on a weekday for the cleanest streetscape and the best urban light for photos.

藏王 Eco-line.count: Dramatic elevation change reveals distinct layers of autumn color
藏王 Eco-line.hours: 24 hours (closed for winter from early November to late April)
藏王 Eco-line.access_car: About 1 hour by car from the Shiroishi IC or Murata IC on the Tohoku Expressway
藏王 Eco-line.tagline: Drive the Zao Eco-line toward the volcanic crater lake Okama and pass through miles of layered highland color.
藏王 Eco-line.desc:
The Zao Eco-line is a scenic highland road spanning Miyagi and Yamagata, running across a volcanic plateau roughly 1,000 meters up. From late September to mid-October, thousands of maples and beeches along the route turn together, turning the drive into a literal tunnel of color.

The main appeal is a ribbon of color that rises and falls with the road itself. Whether you roll down the window while driving or pull over to look, vivid red and gold foliage crowds close on both sides, stretching along the mountain and offset by the mysterious crater lake Okama in the distance — a truly sweeping scene.

Since this is essentially an open mountain road that closes for winter due to snow from late October, check the latest official notices before heading out. Winds can be strong and temperatures chilly at the summit, so bring a warm jacket, and aim for a clear morning with good visibility for the most comfortable drive.

抱返溪谷.count: Famous for the contrast between the gorge's cobalt-blue water and vivid red foliage
抱返溪谷.hours: 24 hours (shuttle bus runs during peak leaf season)
抱返溪谷.address: 秋田縣仙北市田澤湖卒田
抱返溪谷.access_train: About 15 min by seasonal shuttle bus or taxi from JR Kakunodate Station
抱返溪谷.tagline: A hidden gorge named for the narrow path where travelers once had to embrace the rock face to pass — now mirrored in fiery autumn color.
抱返溪谷.desc:
Daihōren Gorge takes its name from an old mountain trail so narrow that travelers had to hug the rock and sidle past one another. The stream running through it is a striking cobalt blue, and in autumn the maples layered along both banks blaze with color that reflects vividly on the water's surface.

The trail to Kaiko-no-Taki ("Looking-Back Falls") is postcard-perfect the whole way, making this one of Akita's most beloved hidden leaf-viewing routes.

田澤湖.count: The golden Tatsuko statue set against deep blue water and red foliage
田澤湖.access_train: About 15 min by bus from JR Tazawako Station
田澤湖.tagline: Japan's deepest lake turns its famous cobalt water into a mirror for the surrounding autumn slopes.
田澤湖.desc:
Lake Tazawa is Japan's deepest lake, prized for its clear, distinctive cobalt-blue water. In autumn the maples on the surrounding hillsides shift gradually into gold and burnt orange, casting their color across the lake's surface alongside the gilded statue of Princess Tatsuko.

The lakeshore loop is about 20 km, and cycling the full circuit is the best way to take in the panorama of fall color.

秋田駒岳.count: Sweeping views over Lake Tazawa from above, with the whole mountainside turning red
秋田駒岳.address: 秋田縣仙北市田澤湖生保內
秋田駒岳.access_train: Bus from JR Tazawako Station to "Komagatake Hachigome"
秋田駒岳.tagline: One of Tōhoku's earliest peaks to turn — alpine meadows blaze red while the rest of the region is still green.
秋田駒岳.desc: Mount Akita-Komagatake is one of the first great peaks in Tōhoku to color each year — by mid-September, the alpine grasslands above 1,600 meters are already washed in orange and gold. Ride the ropeway to the summit area and the meadows around Lake Amida, with Mount Iwate rising in the distance, form a sweeping panorama that draws mountain photographers from across the region.

藏王連峰.count: A striking pairing of an emerald crater lake with color-changing alpine plants
藏王連峰.access_train: About 90 min by bus from JR Yamagata Station
藏王連峰.tagline: Autumn color spreads outward from an emerald crater lake at the summit of one of Tōhoku's iconic ranges.
藏王連峰.desc: The Zao mountain range straddles Yamagata and Miyagi, and each autumn the color begins at the crater lake Okama near the summit before spreading outward. The lake's brilliant turquoise against the reddening slopes around it makes for a striking contrast. The full length of the Zao Echo Line is drivable, letting visitors take in layered color at different elevations — Yamagata's signature autumn drive.

最上川.count: Maple forests lining both banks of the Mogami Gorge, viewed from a heated boat
最上川.address: 山形縣最上郡戶澤村古口
最上川.access_train: About 8 min walk from JR Rikuu West Line Kuguchi Station to the boat landing
最上川.tagline: Drift past walls of maple color on one of Japan's three great rapids, to the boatman's traditional folk song.
最上川.desc: The Mogami River is one of Japan's three great rapids, and riding a traditional Mogami riverboat through banks of autumn color, to the boatman's folk songs, is one of the most poetic leaf-viewing experiences around. The poet Matsuo Bashō recorded his own boat trip down the Mogami in Oku no Hosomichi — in autumn, fallen leaves drift across the water like a moving ink-wash painting.

月山.count: Wide alpine meadows blanketed in gold with sweeping views
月山.address: 山形縣東田川郡庄內町
月山.access_train: Bus from JR Tsuruoka Station to the 8th station
月山.tagline: The main peak of the sacred Dewa Sanzan turns into a vast, golden alpine sea.
月山.desc: Mount Gassan is the highest of the three sacred Dewa Sanzan peaks and Yamagata's premier high-altitude leaf-viewing site. By late October the meadows around the 8th station turn a deep red; ride the ropeway up and you're rewarded with a sweeping panorama of golden highland color. Gassan Shrine near the summit sits amid the scene with a solemn, majestic air.

霞城公園.count: Maples framing the moat and old gates in a scene that pairs perfectly with the ruins
霞城公園.access_train: About 10 min walk from JR Yamagata Station
霞城公園.tagline: Autumn at the old Yamagata Castle ruins, where the moat mirrors gold and crimson.
霞城公園.desc: Kajo Park is built around the ruins of the second bailey of the old Yamagata Castle, and its moat is lined with maples and ginkgos that turn the whole park gold and red each autumn. The stone ramparts and the reconstructed Ichimonji Gate, framed by falling leaves, carry a quiet samurai-era atmosphere — a favorite autumn stroll for Yamagata City residents.

大內宿.count: Thatched roofs framed by mountain foliage, as if time had stopped
大內宿.address: 福島縣南會津郡下鄉町大內
大內宿.access_train: About 20 min by "Saruyugo" bus from Yunokami-Onsen Station
大內宿.tagline: A thatched-roof post town where autumn settles over the Edo period like a held breath.
大內宿.desc: Ouchi-juku is a beautifully preserved Edo-era post town, its two rows of thatched-roof houses running along a stone-paved street beneath hills that turn red with the season. In autumn, deep crimson maples punctuate the rustic rooflines like a scene frozen out of a period drama — one of Japan's most nostalgic places to see fall color.

鶴之城.count: The castle's red tile roof set beautifully against blazing maples
鶴之城.address: 福島縣會津若松市追手町1-1
鶴之城.access_train: Loop bus from JR Aizu-Wakamatsu Station to "Tsurugajo Iriguchi"
鶴之城.tagline: Red tile roofs meet red maples at the last great castle of the Aizu domain.
鶴之城.desc: Tsuruga Castle (Wakamatsu Castle) is the emblem of Aizu domain's history, known for its distinctive red-tiled roof. In autumn, maples around the moat and keep turn shade by shade, their color layering richly against the red tiles. A nighttime illumination event during peak season makes the whole castle seem to float on a sea of red — one of Aizu's signature autumn sights.

塔之岪.count: Dramatic rock towers, a suspension bridge, and maple color in one frame
塔之岪.address: 福島縣南會津郡下鄉町彌五島
塔之岪.access_train: About 3 min walk from Aizu Railway Tōnoizumi Station
塔之岪.tagline: Towering rock pillars turn crimson along a remote South Aizu gorge few tourists ever find.
塔之岪.desc: Tōnoizumi is a gorge along the Tadami River studded with dramatic rock spires that soar skyward, engulfed each autumn in maple color that spreads across the whole valley. Access is a little inconvenient, which is exactly why the scenery here has stayed so untouched. From the viewing platform, a waterfall plunges past the red-stained cliffs — one of Fukushima's most striking hidden leaf-viewing spots.

筑波山.access_train: About 40 min by bus from Tsukuba Station (Tsukuba Express) to "Tsukubasan-jinja Iriguchi"
筑波山.access_car: About 40 min from Tsuchiura-kita IC on the Joban Expressway
筑波山.tagline: A twin-peaked landmark rising from the Kanto Plain, with an entire autumn landscape spread out below.
筑波山.desc: Mount Tsukuba is a celebrated peak on the flat Kanto Plain, long paired in verse with Mount Fuji as "Fuji in the west, Tsukuba in the east." In autumn the maples and mixed woodland on its slopes turn shade by shade; ride the cable car or ropeway up and you can look out over color spreading across the vast plain below. The area around Tsukubasan Shrine is especially dense with maples, making it Ibaraki's most popular mountain for fall foliage.

花貫溪谷.count: Foliage runs continuously along the gorge
花貫溪谷.hours: 24 hours (bridge illumination until 20:00 during the season)
花貫溪谷.access_train: About 20 min by taxi from JR Joban Line Takahagi Station
花貫溪谷.access_car: About 15 min from Takahagi IC on the Joban Expressway
花貫溪谷.tagline: A tunnel of red arching over a suspension bridge — Ibaraki's very last stretch of autumn color.
花貫溪谷.desc: Hananuki Gorge is Ibaraki's latest and most concentrated stretch of fall foliage, with maples along the streambanks forming a natural red tunnel; the Shiomi suspension bridge is its best-known photo spot. Traffic is restricted here during peak leaf season, so visitors walk in — which, if anything, has preserved the gorge's quiet, unhurried atmosphere. It's an ideal escape from the crowds for anyone wanting to take autumn in slowly.

龍神大吊橋.address: 茨城縣常陸太田市天下野町2133-6
龍神大吊橋.access_train: About 40 min by taxi from JR Suigun Line Hitachiota Station
龍神大吊橋.access_car: About 1 hour from Naka IC on the Joban Expressway
龍神大吊橋.tagline: Honshu's longest pedestrian suspension bridge, floating 100 meters above a lake ringed in autumn color.
龍神大吊橋.desc: At 375 meters, the Ryujin Grand Suspension Bridge is the longest pedestrian suspension bridge on Honshu, spanning the gorge above Lake Ryujin some 100 meters below. During peak leaf season the color erupts across both ends of the bridge and the gorge walls at once — looking down from the deck, the red foliage tangled with the lake's deep green water makes for a dizzying, spectacular view. Bungee jumping also runs here during the same season.

龍王峽.address: 栃木縣日光市藤原龍王峽
龍王峽.access_train: Immediately at Ryuokyo Station on the Yagan Railway
龍王峽.access_car: About 30 min from Imaichi IC on the Nikko Utsunomiya Road
龍王峽.tagline: Listen to the Kinugawa River roar past volcanic cliffs said to writhe like a dragon, framed in a full canopy of color.
龍王峽.desc:
Ryuokyo Gorge was carved by volcanic activity over twenty million years ago along the Kinugawa River, its jagged rock formations said to resemble a coiling dragon. From late October to early November, the tall maples and beeches lining the steep Hakuryu and Seiryu cliffs reach their peak, filling the whole gorge with color.

The highlight is the interplay of Nijimi Bridge, Nijimi Falls, and the layered forest around them: as the mist thrown off by the falls catches the sunlight into a rainbow, it sets off the red-and-gold maples cascading down the cliffs and the weathered Goryū-ō Shrine below — an expansive, dramatic scene.

The main trail runs along the natural gorge and includes some rocky steps and boardwalk sections, so sturdy, non-slip footwear is strongly recommended. Direct sunlight only reaches this deep gorge for a limited window each day — arriving between 10am and noon gives the richest, most saturated color.

那須高原.count: Color spreads across the entire highland
那須高原.address: 栃木縣那須郡那須町湯本
那須高原.access_train: About 40 min by bus from JR Kuroiso Station to "Nasu-Yumoto"
那須高原.access_car: About 20 min from Nasu IC on the Tohoku Expressway
那須高原.tagline: Climb an active volcanic highland in the Nasu range and look out over a fiery alpine tundra from the ropeway.
那須高原.desc:
Nasu Highland sits in northern Tochigi around the active volcano Mount Chausu, and it's one of the earliest places in the Kanto region to turn each year. From late September into mid-October, color spreads down from Ubagahira near the summit, with red rowan and golden Erman's birch washing the whole highland in deep autumn tones.

The most striking way to see it is aboard the Nasu Ropeway: rising slowly above the mountainside, riders look out over a vast natural palette where sweeping red-and-gold forest meets rugged volcanic rock — an expansive, wild kind of beauty.

Because this is genuine high-altitude terrain, temperatures near the summit can drop close to freezing by early October, so a proper windproof, insulated jacket and sturdy footwear are essential. Mountain weather here can change fast — a clear morning is strongly recommended, both for safety and for the best light.

鹽原溫泉.count: Runs the full 25 km length of the gorge
鹽原溫泉.address: 栃木縣那須塩原市塩原
鹽原溫泉.access_train: About 40 min by bus from JR Nishi-Nasuno Station to "Shiobara Onsen Bus Terminal"
鹽原溫泉.access_car: About 20 min from Nishinasuno-Shiobara IC on the Tohoku Expressway
鹽原溫泉.tagline: A hot-spring town strung along the Houkigawa gorge by a chain of dramatic suspension bridges, all wrapped in red.
鹽原溫泉.desc:
Shiobara Onsen sits along the Houkigawa gorge, its many large suspension bridges linking together one of Japan's premier hot-spring leaf-viewing destinations. From late October to mid-November the untouched forest ringing the onsen town reaches its peak, covering the green gorge in a riot of color.

The signature view pairs Momiji-no-Tsuribashi ("Maple Suspension Bridge") with the foliage at Myōun-ji temple: a wooden bridge strung over the clear stream, with a full canopy of red maple spilling down beneath it, set against the temple's moss and old stone markers — a scene of understated, classic Japanese beauty when the breeze moves across the water.

The riverside promenade through the onsen town is flat and well maintained, perfect for an easy morning walk paired with a hot-spring soak. Because the main viewing bridge is narrow, please don't linger there too long while taking photos. Early morning is best, when mist still lingers over the gorge for an especially ethereal view.

榛名山/榛名湖.count: Broad foliage around the lakeshore and mountain base
榛名山/榛名湖.address: 群馬縣高崎市榛名湖町
榛名山/榛名湖.access_train: About 90 min by bus from JR Takasaki Station to "Harunako"
榛名山/榛名湖.access_car: About 50 min from Maebashi IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
榛名山/榛名湖.tagline: The crater-lake retreat made famous by Initial D, where Mount Haruna's perfect cone frames a full canopy of color.
榛名山/榛名湖.desc:
Mount Haruna is a cluster of dormant volcanoes, its crater lake Harunako a cool highland retreat at altitude. From mid-October to early November, the beech and maple forest around the gentle lakeshore reaches its peak, dressing the whole mountain in a riot of color.

The signature view here is the mirror-play between Mount Harunafuji's perfect cone, the lakeshore, and the surrounding foliage: bands of red and gold trace the shoreline, and when the still water reflects the mountain's flawless silhouette alongside the lush color, the scene takes on a striking, dynamic symmetry.

The lakeside road is well maintained and ideal for a scenic drive or an easy bike ride, and the Haruna Ropeway runs straight to the summit. Mornings can be windy up on this highland lake, so bring something warm. A calm, clear morning gives the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection.

谷川岳.count: Foliage covers a wide area from the base to the mid-slopes
谷川岳.address: 群馬縣利根郡みなかみ町湯檜曾字天神平
谷川岳.access_train: About 30 min by bus from JR Jomo-Kogen Station to "Tanigawadake Ropeway"
谷川岳.access_car: About 15 min from Minakami IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
谷川岳.tagline: Climb past the sheer rock walls of Ichinokurasawa to a full carpet of autumn color from the Tanigawadake ropeway.
谷川岳.desc:
Mount Tanigawa is ranked among Japan's 100 Famous Mountains, renowned nationwide for its knife-edge cliffs and the towering rock face of Ichinokurasawa. From early to late October, color spreads down from the alpine tundra at the summit, engulfing the whole deep valley in vivid reds and purples — one of the Kanto region's very first fronts of autumn color.

The most striking way to experience it is the Tanigawadake Ropeway: rising slowly, riders look out over a vast natural palette where sweeping red-and-gold forest meets rugged, dramatic peaks — a genuinely powerful view.

The trail toward Ichinokurasawa itself is relatively flat, but mountain weather at this altitude changes quickly — by mid-October temperatures near the summit can approach freezing, so proper trail shoes and a windproof, insulated jacket are essential. A clear morning is strongly recommended for the best visibility across this grand landscape.

尾瀨.count: Vast primeval forest surrounding the high moor
尾瀨.hours: Depends on the trail (Oze-ga-hara entrance from 05:00)
尾瀨.fee: Free (some mountain facilities charge a fee)
尾瀨.address: 群馬縣利根郡片品村戸倉
尾瀨.access_train: Bus from JR Numata or Jomo-Kogen Station to "Oze Tokura," then transfer
尾瀨.access_car: About 40 min from Numata IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway to the Oze parking area
尾瀨.tagline: Walk Japan's largest high-altitude marshland and take in golden autumn grasses set against Mount Hiuchi.
尾瀨.desc:
Oze National Park is Japan's largest high-altitude wetland, spanning several prefectures at an elevation of roughly 1,400 meters. Because of its altitude and latitude, autumn arrives here before almost anywhere else in the country: from mid-September into early October, the grasses lining the long boardwalks are already turning a brilliant, unbroken gold.

The signature scene is the pairing of golden autumn grass, quiet peat ponds, and the towering silhouette of Mount Hiuchi in the distance: walking the flat, well-maintained boardwalk, you're surrounded by golden fields threaded with clear ponds, and when a blue sky reflects on the water the whole scene turns almost otherworldly.

To protect the fragile ecosystem, private cars are banned throughout the park year-round — an eco-friendly shuttle bus is required to reach each trailhead. The wetland boardwalk itself is flat and easy, but the walk is long and temperatures can be low, so proper hiking shoes and windproof, cold-weather layers are essential. Weekday mornings are quietest.

赤城山.count: Wide foliage around the shores of Lake Ōnuma
赤城山.address: 群馬縣前橋市富士見町赤城山
赤城山.access_train: About 80 min by bus from JR Maebashi Station to "Ōbora"
赤城山.access_car: About 40 min from Maebashi IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
赤城山.tagline: One of the sacred Jōmō Sanzan peaks — see the shrine's vermilion bridge frame Lake Ōnuma in full color.
赤城山.desc:
Mount Akagi is a historic composite volcano, grouped with Mount Haruna and Mount Myōgi as the "Jōmō Sanzan." From early to late October, color arrives around Lake Ōnuma, the crater lake at its summit, as tall zelkova and beech turn into a blaze of foliage draping the sacred grounds in early autumn color.

The classic composition pairs Akagi Shrine's vermilion Kitsutsuki ("Woodpecker") Bridge with the color across the lake: vivid foliage crowds the old wooden shrine buildings, the red bridge arcs over still water, and behind it all stretches an endless expanse of blue lake and full canopy — a scene steeped in traditional Japanese aesthetics.

The trails around Lake Ōnuma are gentle and well maintained, ideal for an easy lakeside walk. Mornings and evenings can turn breezy and cool up at this mountain lake, so bring a light jacket. A calm, clear morning gives the best chance at the lake's serene, reflective mood.

草津溫泉.count: Foliage around the onsen town and the approach to Kōsen-ji
草津溫泉.address: 群馬縣吾妻郡草津町草津
草津溫泉.access_train: About 25 min by bus from JR Naganoharakusatsuguchi Station to "Kusatsu Onsen Bus Terminal"
草津溫泉.access_car: About 90 min from Shibukawa-Ikaho IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
草津溫泉.tagline: One of Japan's three great hot-spring towns, where Nishinokawara Park turns to color amid rising steam.
草津溫泉.desc:
Kusatsu Onsen is famed the world over for its enormous natural spring flow and traditional "yumomi" water-cooling ritual. From mid-October to early November, Nishinokawara Park at the edge of the onsen district reaches peak color, as maples and other trees turn one after another across the whole hillside, dressing this hot-spring retreat in vivid color.

The signature view is the contrast between steaming geothermal streams, bare volcanic rock, and full color: old stone paths and turquoise hot pools sit tightly ringed by pink and crimson foliage, and when white steam drifts through the golden canopy, the whole scene takes on an almost otherworldly mood.

The park's terrain is gently rolling with well-maintained walking paths, easy underfoot. Because Kusatsu is a world-famous destination, daytime crowds can be heavy. Early weekday mornings or the evening illumination hours are best for capturing the steam and foliage together in a quieter, more atmospheric shot.

伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.count: Concentrated along the stone steps up to Kajika Bridge
伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.address: 群馬縣渋川市伊香保町伊香保
伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.access_train: About 20 min by bus from JR Shibukawa Station to "Ikaho Onsen"
伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.access_car: About 20 min from Shibukawa-Ikaho IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.tagline: Climb the famous stone steps to a vermilion arched bridge lit up at night beneath a full canopy of maple.
伊香保溫泉（河鹿橋）.desc:
Ikaho Onsen is famous for its 365-step stone stairway lined with shops. From late October to mid-November, Kajika Bridge at the top of the steps reaches peak color, as several hundred Japanese maples turn together, dressing this venerable hot-spring town in early autumn shades.

The scene everyone comes for is the vermilion arched bridge set against a full canopy of red: the bright red bridge spans the mountain stream, with cascading red-and-gold maple beneath it, and when the nighttime lights come on, the whole hillside seems to glow gold — a striking blend of Eastern aesthetics and quiet fantasy.

Reaching Kajika Bridge means climbing part of the stone stairway, so non-slip shoes are strongly recommended. Crowds swell heavily during the evening illumination — for the cleanest shot of the bridge and its tunnel of maple, an early weekday morning before sunrise is your best bet.

長瀞溪谷.count: Wide foliage runs along the whole gorge
長瀞溪谷.address: 埼玉縣秩父郡長瀞町長瀞
長瀞溪谷.access_train: Immediately at Nagatoro Station on the Chichibu Railway
長瀞溪谷.access_car: About 30 min from Hanazono IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
長瀞溪谷.tagline: Ride a traditional wooden boat down the Arakawa past a nationally designated rock formation wrapped in a full canopy of color.
長瀞溪谷.desc:
Nagatoro Gorge is a nationally designated Scenic Beauty site, carved over ages by the Arakawa River into dramatic crystalline-schist cliffs. From mid to late November, thousands of maples along the imposing gray rock formation known as Iwadatami turn in unison, filling the whole gorge with color.

The must-do experience here is riding a traditional hand-rowed boat down the Nagatoro-Arakawa line: settled into a rustic wooden flat boat, listening to the boatman's folk songs, you glide with the calm green river on one side and cascading autumn color spilling off the sheer cliffs on the other.

The main viewpoints and trails are flat and easy, though the paths closer to Iwadatami are mostly natural rock terraces, so non-slip footwear is strongly recommended. A weekday morning is your best bet for avoiding crowds and catching a clean mirror reflection.

中津峽.count: Runs the full 10 km length of the gorge
中津峽.access_train: About 60 min by taxi from Seibu-Chichibu Station (Seibu Chichibu Line)
中津峽.access_car: About 80 min from Hanazono IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
中津峽.tagline: Listen to the Nakatsu River roar through Okuchichibu's deep cliffs, beneath a new bridge and 10 km of unbroken color.
中津峽.desc:
Nakatsu Gorge is a hundred-meter-deep ravine cut by the Nakatsu River, the premier dramatic gorge of the Chichibu area. From late October to early November, thousands of maples and beeches lining the 10-kilometer stretch of sheer cliff turn together, filling the whole deep gorge with color.

The biggest visual payoff is the pairing of the red Nakatsugawa Bridge with the full canopy of color below: from the high overlook, the striking vermilion bridge spans the vividly colored cliffs and stream, with cascading red-and-gold rowan spilling beneath it — a genuinely dramatic composition.

Because the main viewing route runs along a road through the deep rock gorge, watch for passing traffic if you stop to shoot photos on foot. This is a relatively undiscovered spot with light crowds. Arriving around midday gives sunlight the best chance to reach the gorge floor, when the color is at its most saturated.

三峯神社.count: Abundant foliage across the shrine grounds and approach
三峯神社.access_train: About 75 min by bus from Seibu-Chichibu Station (Seibu Chichibu Line)
三峯神社.access_car: About 90 min from Hanazono IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
三峯神社.tagline: Climb into the misty highlands of Chichibu to a sacred shrine where the vermilion Zuishinmon gate frames rare foliage.
三峯神社.desc:
Mitsumine Shrine sits deep in the mountains at 1,100 meters, a historic and deeply revered site of nature worship. By early November, hundreds of maples around the shrine's towering triple torii gate, its brilliantly colored Zuishinmon gate, and the main hall have quietly turned, dressing the sacred grounds in rich autumn color.

The signature scene here pairs the ornate old shrine buildings and ancient torii with the surrounding maples: colorful foliage crowds old stone lanterns and towering old-growth trees, and when afternoon mist drifts through the mountains, the maple sea glowing through it captures the temple's particular, quiet sense of the sacred.

Reaching the main hall involves some natural stone steps and paths, so comfortable, non-slip walking shoes are recommended. During leaf season the shrine staff release limited-edition, highly collectible amulets and seal stamps. Weekday mornings see fewer worshippers, making them the best time to photograph the shrine's classic atmosphere.

飯能（Moomin Valley Park）.count: Foliage around the shores of Lake Miyazawa
飯能（Moomin Valley Park）.access_train: About 10 min by bus from Hanno Station (Seibu Ikebukuro Line)
飯能（Moomin Valley Park）.access_car: About 15 min from Sayama-Hidaka IC on the Ken-O Expressway
飯能（Moomin Valley Park）.tagline: Walk a Nordic fairy-tale forest by Lake Miyazawa and catch the Moomins' lakeside cottage framed in ten thousand tsubo of color.
飯能（Moomin Valley Park）.desc:
Moominvalley Park sits beside Lake Miyazawa in Hanno, a sprawling theme park that faithfully recreates a Nordic, fairy-tale atmosphere. From mid to late November, the conifers and maples ringing the broad lakeshore reach their peak, dressing the whole Nordic-style village in vivid, lively color.

The core visual draw is the interplay between the rustic Moomin-style cottages, the lake, and the colorful forest: bands of vivid foliage line the gentle waterside boardwalk, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the wooden Nordic buildings alongside the full autumn color, the whole space feels open and full of natural charm.

The park charges admission, and its paths are flat and fully barrier-free throughout, making it ideal for families with grandparents or strollers in tow. Ample lawns and shaded benches make it a favorite for slow-paced travelers — arrive on a weekday morning for the quietest visit.

養老溪谷.count: Runs about 3 km along the gorge
養老溪谷.address: 千葉縣夷隅郡大多喜町粟又
養老溪谷.access_train: About 15 min on foot or by taxi from Yoro Keikoku Station (Kominato Railway)
養老溪谷.access_car: About 50 min from Ichihara IC on the Tateyama Expressway
養老溪谷.tagline: Walk the Boso Peninsula's finest riverside trail to Awamata Falls and the great torii gate of Kurokawa Bunto, all wrapped in color.
養老溪谷.desc:
Yoro Valley is a celebrated riverside leaf-viewing destination carved over time by the Yoro River. Because of the mild climate of the southern Boso lowlands, its foliage peaks later than almost anywhere else on Honshu — not until late November to early December — before spreading across the whole primeval gorge in vivid color.

The valley's signature feature is its long riverside cliffside trail: color lines the gentle riverbank and gravel path, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the famous tiered Awamata Falls alongside the full canopy of color, the scene takes on an elegant, meditative quality.

The route is long, but the main trails and riverside boardwalks are well maintained and comfortable to walk, though some streambed rocks can be slippery, so non-slip trail shoes are advised. Rainy days sharpen the contrast between wet green leaves and red foliage, making this a rewarding spot for nature photography in any weather.

成田山公園.access_train: About 15 min walk from Narita Station (JR or Keisei Line)
成田山公園.access_car: About 20 min from Narita IC on the Higashi-Kanto Expressway
成田山公園.tagline: Walk a sprawling classical garden behind the thousand-year Narita-san Shinsho-ji temple, past Monju Pond and a three-tiered pagoda in color.
成田山公園.desc:
Naritasan Park is a vast, traditional strolling garden covering 160,000 square meters directly behind the main hall of the thousand-year-old temple Narita-san Shinsho-ji. From mid to late November, some 250 old maples across the grounds reach their peak, dressing this sacred site in vivid, colorful splendor.

The park's signature scene pairs an exquisite classical pond, old stone lanterns, and full autumn color: rich foliage lines the gentle gravel paths, and when the mirror-still surface of Monju Pond perfectly reflects a red fountain alongside the surrounding color, the scene carries a refined, meditative elegance.

The park's grounds are well laid out and gently rolling, ideal for families to stroll while soaking in the history. Traditional koto and shakuhachi concerts are often held on weekends during the leaf-viewing festival, drawing large audiences. Weekday mornings see the fewest visitors — best for photographing a clean reflection.

清水公園.access_train: About 3 min walk from Shimizu Koen Station (Tobu Noda Line)
清水公園.access_car: About 20 min from Nagareyama IC on the Joban Expressway
清水公園.tagline: Step into Japan's first privately run nature park and take in the historic Konjo-in temple wrapped in a tunnel of color.
清水公園.desc:
