Shimizu Park blends rich natural scenery, historic sites, and large-scale outdoor adventure attractions — Japan's very first privately operated public park. From mid to late November, several hundred maples around the historic Konjo-in temple on the park's north side turn together, one after another.

The core visual highlight is the pairing of the temple's grand wooden gate, its Niō guardian gate, and the maple forest: vividly colored foliage lines the long gravel approach on both sides, set against old stone lanterns, and the interplay of stillness and color perfectly captures the temple's quiet, weathered sense of history.

The park is free to enter (some facilities charge), with flat, fully paved grounds that are welcoming to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. A large lawn area makes for a comfortable early-autumn picnic-and-foliage outing. Weekday mornings offer the fewest crowds and the best light for photographing the historic scenery.

本土寺.access_train: About 10 min walk from Kita-Koganei Station (JR Joban Line)
本土寺.access_car: About 10 min from Nagareyama IC on the Joban Expressway
本土寺.tagline: Visit Matsudo's beloved "Temple of Autumn Leaves," home to a five-story pagoda and a thousand Japanese maples.
本土寺.desc:
Hondo-ji is a venerable Nichiren-sect temple with over 700 years of history, affectionately known locally as the "Temple of Autumn Leaves" for its abundant seasonal plantings. From late November to early December, over a thousand Japanese maples across the spacious grounds bloom into color together, filling the sacred site with autumn splendor.

The temple's signature composition pairs a vermilion five-story pagoda and a weathered wooden gate with the surrounding maples: vivid foliage lines the old stone-paved approach on both sides, set against moss and historic markers, capturing the temple's particular sense of quiet and history.

The temple grounds are flat and compact, easy to explore — a full visit and stroll takes about 40 minutes. During leaf season the temple accepts a visiting donation and offers limited-edition amulets. Arriving right at opening on a weekday morning gives the cleanest air and the best light for photos.

千葉公園.count: Colorful foliage scattered throughout the park
千葉公園.address: 千葉縣千葉市中央区弁天3-1
千葉公園.access_train: About 15 min walk from JR Chiba Station
千葉公園.access_car: About 10 min from Anagawa IC on the Keiyo Road
千葉公園.tagline: An elegant pairing of urban color and water at the spring-fed pond in the heart of Chiba City.
千葉公園.desc:
Chiba Park is one of the city's signature urban green spaces, prized for its refined landscaping and easy accessibility. From mid to late November, the maples around the park's large pond, Watauchi-ike, reach their peak, with several hundred trees bursting into color and painting a rich autumn scene right in the middle of the city.

The visual highlight pairs the pond's edge, rowboats, and colorful foliage: vivid trees line the waterside boardwalk, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the colorful canopy alongside the distant city skyline, the scene feels open and refreshingly cool — a clean, early-autumn cityscape.

The park sits right in the city center on completely flat ground, ideal for an easy morning walk for independent travelers. Rowboats can be rented to view the shoreline color from the water. Set aside about an hour; weekday mornings see the fewest visitors and offer the best chance at a clean reflection.

六義園.access_train: About 7 min walk from Komagome Station (JR Yamanote Line)
六義園.access_car: Parking nearby is limited — taking the train is recommended
六義園.tagline: Step into a classical Edo-era strolling garden built around waka poetry, and visit Togetsukyo Bridge amid a lake full of color.
六義園.desc:
Rikugien is a landmark Edo-period strolling garden, built over seven years by the daimyo Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu to embody the imagery of classical waka poetry. From late November to early December, several hundred Japanese maples across the grounds reach their peak, dressing the sacred, tranquil space in vivid, lively color.

The garden's signature scene pairs an exquisite classical pond, an arched stone bridge, and full autumn color: rich foliage lines the gentle gravel paths, and when the mirror-still surface of the great pond, Daisensui, perfectly reflects the vermilion Togetsukyo Bridge alongside the surrounding color, the scene carries a refined, meditative elegance.

The grounds are flat with well-maintained paths, welcoming to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. A celebrated nighttime illumination runs during the leaf-viewing festival, making reflections even more dreamlike. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the cleanest, most classically Japanese shot.

小石川後樂園.access_train: About 3 min walk from Iidabashi Station (Toei Oedo Line)
小石川後樂園.access_car: Parking nearby is limited — taking the train is recommended
小石川後樂園.tagline: Walk a historic garden tied to the Mito Tokugawa family, and find Tsūten Bridge mirrored beside the great pond in autumn color.
小石川後樂園.desc:
Koishikawa Korakuen is a nationally designated Site of Scenic Beauty, built by Tokugawa Yorifusa, founder of the Mito Tokugawa house, with design input from the Chinese scholar Zhu Shunshui. From late November to early December, several hundred old maples around the garden's large pond reach their peak, dressing this historic site in classic, refined color.

The garden's signature composition pairs a vermilion Tsūten Bridge, the historic Tokujindō hall, and full autumn color: mossy stone paths and old wooden structures sit surrounded by the foliage, alongside a section modeled on West Lake in Hangzhou — together capturing the refined garden aesthetics of old Edo.

The garden's terrain is gently rolling with well-maintained paths, easy underfoot. Because it sits right next to the bustling Tokyo Dome district, daytime crowds can be heavy. Arriving right when the gates open on a weekday morning is strongly recommended for a quiet, atmospheric shot among the old buildings and color.

奧多摩湖.address: 東京都西多摩郡奥多摩町原5
奧多摩湖.access_train: About 10 min walk from Okutama Station (JR Ome Line), or by bus to "Okutama-ko"
奧多摩湖.access_car: About 50 min from Uenohara IC on the Chuo Expressway
奧多摩湖.tagline: Walk a hidden reservoir at the headwaters of the Tama River, with a floating bridge and the full color of the Okutama range.
奧多摩湖.desc:
Lake Okutama (the Ogōchi Reservoir) is a vast man-made lake straddling Tokyo and Yamanashi, formed by the Ogōchi Dam holding back the Tama River. From late October to mid-November, the beech and maple forest ringing its broad shoreline reaches its peak, dressing this green lung on Tokyo's edge in vivid color.

The signature sight here is Mugiyama's floating bridge set against the lake's colorful shoreline: the distinctive pontoon bridge gently sways over the emerald water, and when the still surface perfectly mirrors the towering Okutama range in the distance alongside the vivid foliage nearby, the scene feels open and refreshingly cool.

The lakeside promenade and waterside boardwalk are well maintained, ideal for an easy morning hike or a scenic drive. Mornings and evenings can turn breezy at this mountain lake, so bring something warm. A calm, clear morning gives the best chance at a perfect reflection.

鎌倉（鶴岡八幡宮）.address: 神奈川縣鎌倉市雪ノ下2-1-31
鎌倉（鶴岡八幡宮）.access_train: About 15 min walk from Kamakura Station (JR Yokosuka Line)
鎌倉（鶴岡八幡宮）.access_car: About 15 min from Asahina IC on the Yokohama-Yokosuka Road
鎌倉（鶴岡八幡宮）.tagline: Walk the ancient capital's guardian shrine of the Minamoto clan, and find Yanagihara and Genji ponds ablaze with color.
鎌倉（鶴岡八幡宮）.desc:
Tsurugaoka Hachimangu is a historic shrine with nearly a thousand years of history, ranked among Kamakura's three great shrines. From late November to early December, several hundred maples and cherry trees around the grand torii gate, main hall, and approach turn together, dressing the solemn sacred grounds in early autumn color.

The shrine's signature scene pairs its vermilion halls, ancient moss, and full autumn color — especially at Yanagihara Shinike and Genji Pond, where still water and a full canopy of foliage play off one another, perfectly capturing the temple's particular quiet and stillness.

The approach to the main hall is completely flat, with well-maintained gravel paths, welcoming to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. To avoid the busy crowds of worshippers and get the cleanest, most refined shot, arrive before 8am on a weekday. Limited-edition amulets are released during leaf-viewing season.

丹澤湖.address: 神奈川縣足柄上郡山北町中川
丹澤湖.access_train: About 30 min by taxi from Yamakita Station (JR Gotemba Line)
丹澤湖.access_car: About 40 min from Oi-Matsuda IC on the Tomei Expressway
丹澤湖.tagline: A broad reservoir cradled by the Tanzawa mountains, where Eisai Bridge and Miho Dam frame a full canopy of color.
丹澤湖.desc:
Tanzawa Lake is a large man-made reservoir cradled by the foothills of the Tanzawa mountains, ranked among Kanagawa's 50 finest scenic spots. From mid-November, maples and beeches spread along the several-kilometer lakeside trail and waterside park erupt into full color along the shore, dressing the whole lake area in vivid tones.

The signature view pairs a vermilion bridge, green mountains, and a full sea of color: foliage lines the clear lakeshore, and when the mirror-still surface reflects the iconic cable-stayed Eisai Bridge alongside the vivid color, the scene carries a pure, natural clarity.

The lakeside trail is well maintained and flat, ideal for independent travelers to enjoy an easy morning walk or a bike ride. Because the area sits in a mountain valley, a parasol is worth bringing along. Arriving in the early morning gives the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection of the foliage on the water.

三溪園.address: 神奈川縣橫浜市中区本牧三之谷58-1
三溪園.access_train: About 10 min by bus from Negishi Station (JR / municipal subway) to "Sankeien-mae"
三溪園.access_car: About 10 min from Ishikawacho IC on the Shuto Expressway
三溪園.tagline: Step into Yokohama's nationally designated Japanese garden and find a three-story pagoda mirrored in autumn color.
三溪園.desc:
Built by the businessman Hara Sankei, this sprawling garden is one of Yokohama's proudest nationally designated Scenic Beauty sites. From late November to early December, several hundred maples turn around the historic buildings and old farmhouses relocated here from Kyoto and Kamakura, releasing a deep, distinctly Japanese aesthetic.

The garden's signature composition pairs the old Tomyoji three-story pagoda with the surrounding maples: vivid foliage crowds old moss and wooden temple buildings beside the broad pond, and when mist drifts through, the whole scene looks like an ink-wash painting come to life.

The grounds are expansive with many historic structures to explore — set aside at least 1.5 hours. A weekday morning is strongly recommended for the quiet, contemplative atmosphere this historic garden is known for, and the best light for photography.

大山寺.address: 神奈川縣伊勢原市大山724
大山寺.access_train: About 30 min by bus from Isehara Station (Odakyu Line) to "Oyama Cable," then cable car
大山寺.access_car: About 30 min from Atsugi IC on the Tomei Expressway
大山寺.tagline: Climb the long stone approach to Oyama Afuri Shrine through a tunnel of maple, lit up at night.
大山寺.desc:
Oyama-ji sits partway up Mount Oyama in Isehara, a historic and richly storied temple of the Shingon Daikakuji school. From mid to late November, several hundred Japanese maples along the long stone stairway to the main hall reach their peak, earning it a reputation as one of the Kanto region's finest maple temples.

The highlight here is the interplay between the stone steps, mossy stone-child statues, and a full canopy of color: climbing the winding, ancient stone stairway, you're flanked by walls of foliage that rise almost to shoulder height. A celebrated nighttime illumination during the leaf-viewing festival turns the whole mountainside gold.

You can ride the Oyama Cable Car partway up, but the path from Oyama-ji Station still involves a fair slope and stone steps, so sturdy, non-slip hiking shoes are strongly recommended. Evening illumination draws heavy crowds — for a clean, empty shot of the tunnel of maple, a weekday morning is best.

彌彥公園.count: About 300 maples, especially striking during the illumination
彌彥公園.address: 新潟縣西蒲原郡彌彥村彌彥
彌彥公園.access_train: About 10 min walk from Yahiko Station (Yahiko Line)
彌彥公園.access_car: About 30 min from Sanjo-Tsubame IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
彌彥公園.tagline: Walk the wooded retreat behind Echigo's first shrine and find a vermilion moon-viewing bridge amid a 16-hectare valley of color.
彌彥公園.desc:
Yahiko Park sits right beside the famous Yahiko Shrine, a historic 16-hectare garden blending Japanese tradition with the natural landscape. From late October to mid-November, the park's celebrated "Momiji-dani" (Maple Valley) reaches its peak, with several hundred old maples bursting into color across the valley.

The park's signature scene is the pairing of the vermilion Kangetsu Bridge with a full canopy of color: a rustic wooden arched bridge spans the clear stream, with cascading red-and-gold maple following the mountainside beneath it, and when the nighttime illumination comes on, dreamlike light plays across the foliage for a deeply traditional, meditative atmosphere.

The park's terrain is gentle with well-maintained paths, ideal for a slow-paced family visit steeped in history. The main route is friendly to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. Set aside about an hour; weekday mornings see the fewest visitors and offer the best chance at a clean reflection.

奧只見湖.count: Foliage reflected across the lake is especially striking
奧只見湖.address: 新潟縣魚沼市湯之谷芋川
奧只見湖.access_train: About 75 min by bus from JR Joetsu Line Koide Station
奧只見湖.access_car: About 60 min from Koide IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
奧只見湖.tagline: Ride a vintage paddle-wheel boat into one of Japan's largest man-made lakes and find golden beech deep in the mountains.
奧只見湖.desc:
Lake Okutadami is a vast man-made reservoir straddling Niigata and Fukushima, ranked among Japan's 100 finest hidden destinations. From mid to late October, the beech and maple forest ringing its broad shoreline reaches its peak, wrapping the deep blue lake in vivid, dramatic color.

The signature experience pairs raw, primeval scenery with a vintage paddle-wheel sightseeing boat: drive the scenic lakeside road through golden wilderness on both sides, or ride the Okutadami sightseeing boat to view the color spilling down the shoreline from the water — with the towering Echigo Sanzan range as a backdrop, the whole scene feels vast and open.

Because this is a deep, high-altitude mountain valley, temperatures near mid-October already approach single digits, so bring a warm coat and windproof headwear. The road typically closes for winter by early November due to snowfall, so check the official site for the latest conditions. A calm, clear morning gives the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection.

苗場.count: Broad foliage along the Dragondola route and at the summit
苗場.address: 新潟縣南魚沼郡湯沢町三国
苗場.access_train: About 30 min by bus from JR Joetsu Shinkansen Echigo-Yuzawa Station to "Naeba Ski Resort"
苗場.access_car: About 30 min from Yuzawa IC on the Kan-etsu Expressway
苗場.tagline: Ride Japan's longest gondola and look down over 5.5 kilometers of unbroken autumn color across the Naeba highlands.
苗場.desc:
Naeba Highland is a resort built along natural rolling hills, beautiful in every season. From mid-October to early November, the once-green slopes turn into a sea of color, with thousands of maples and beeches changing together to dress the entire wild mountainside in vivid tones.

The must-do experience is riding the 5,481-meter Naeba Dragondola, reportedly Japan's longest gondola. Rising slowly through the highland breeze, riders look down from a bird's-eye view over a carpet of red and gold that stretches endlessly across the valley terrain — a genuinely striking sight.

Because this is high-altitude terrain, it feels noticeably cooler than the lowlands, making it a perfect early-autumn escape from the heat. There's almost no cover along the exposed highland route, so hold onto your hat. The one-way ride takes about 25 minutes; departing in the morning gives the best light on Lake Futai below, when the color is at its most vivid.

高田城址公園.count: Colorful foliage spread across the park
高田城址公園.access_train: About 20 min by bus or taxi from JR Hokuriku Shinkansen Joetsumyoko Station
高田城址公園.access_car: About 20 min from Joetsu IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
高田城址公園.tagline: Climb the reconstructed turret tied to Tokugawa Mitsukuni and look out over a moat blazing with maple color.
高田城址公園.desc:
Takada Castle Ruins Park was built on the site of the old Takada Castle, seat of the Edo-era Takada domain, and is nationally famous for its cherry blossoms. From late October to early November, several hundred maples across the park turn together, dressing the imposing old castle walls and reconstructed wooden turret in early autumn color.

The signature scene pairs the historic moat, the striking turret, and full autumn color: vivid foliage lines the gentle waterway, and when the still surface perfectly mirrors the white-walled "Gokuraku Bridge" alongside the color, the scene carries a refined, traditionally Japanese elegance.

The park's terrain is completely flat with well-maintained historic paths, welcoming to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. Local cultural events are often held on weekends during the leaf-viewing festival. Set aside about an hour; early morning offers the fewest crowds and the best chance at a clean reflection.

昇仙峽.count: Abundant foliage runs the full 4 km length of the gorge
昇仙峽.access_train: About 40 min by bus from JR Kofu Station to "Shosenkyo-guchi"
昇仙峽.access_car: About 30 min from Kofu-Showa IC on the Chuo Expressway
昇仙峽.tagline: Listen to the Arakawa roar through dramatic rock formations at what's often called Japan's finest gorge, framed in full color.
昇仙峽.desc:
Mitake-Shosenkyo is celebrated as "Japan's finest gorge," a nationally designated Scenic Beauty site cut through imposing granite cliffs. From mid-October to late November, because of the gorge's dramatic elevation change, color spreads downward from the upper reaches, dressing the sheer rock walls in vivid, riotous autumn tones.

The most striking view pairs the solitary peak Kakuenho, the 30-meter Sen'ga Falls, and fiery maple color: standing on Tenko Bridge, you can watch the rushing clear stream throw up white spray as it winds through golden foliage, with the 180-meter rock face and the color cascading below it forming a single, dramatic frame.

The gorge's walking trails are well maintained and flat, ideal for a family-friendly riverside hike. Since the main viewpoints sit on open terraces above the gorge, arriving between 10am and noon lets sunlight reach the valley floor directly — the best window for saturated color and landscape photography.

山中湖.count: Abundant foliage around the lakeshore and at Flower Fantasia Park
山中湖.address: 山梨縣南都留郡山中湖村山中
山中湖.access_train: JR to Otsuki Station, transfer to the Fujikyuko Line to Fujisan Station, then about 30 min by bus
山中湖.access_car: About 20 min from Gotemba IC on the Tomei Expressway
山中湖.tagline: Stand at the closest of the Fuji Five Lakes to the mountain, and catch both a full canopy of maple and the illumination at Asahigaoka.
山中湖.desc:
Lake Yamanaka is the largest and highest of the Fuji Five Lakes. From mid-October to mid-November, the "Momiji Kaido" (Maple Road) along the Asahigaoka lakeshore reaches its peak, with several hundred maples turning together to dress this celebrated natural spot in vivid color.

The signature view here pairs the majestic Mount Fuji, the lakeshore, and full autumn color: bands of red and gold trace the shoreline, and when the clear water perfectly mirrors Fuji's silhouette alongside the lush foliage, the scene carries a striking, dynamic symmetry.

The lakeside road is well maintained with a comfortable waterside boardwalk, perfect for an easy bike ride. A dreamlike nighttime illumination runs during the leaf-viewing festival, making reflections even more ethereal. A calm, clear morning gives the best chance at a perfect mirror image of the foliage on the lake.

清里高原.count: Foliage spreads across the whole highland
清里高原.address: 山梨縣北杜市高根町清里
清里高原.access_train: Immediately at Kiyosato Station (JR Koumi Line)
清里高原.access_car: About 30 min from Nagasaka IC on the Chuo Expressway
清里高原.tagline: Walk a Nordic-style highland retreat on Mount Yatsugatake's southern slopes, past Higashizawa Bridge amid endless color.
清里高原.desc:
Kiyosato Highland sits on the broad slopes of Mount Yatsugatake at roughly 1,200 meters, a beloved resort known for its crisp, open-air atmosphere. From mid-October to early November, the beech and maple forest around the highland gorge reaches its peak, dressing the entire wooded mountain path in vivid, colorful splendor.

The most striking sight here is the pairing of the vermilion Higashizawa Bridge with the distant peak of Mount Akadake: from Seisenryo or the Kiyosato highland overlook, the massive 138-meter arched bridge spans the deep Kawamatagawa gorge, with several kilometers of golden-and-red foliage spreading beneath it — a truly dramatic view.

The highland terrain is open, with well-maintained flat trails connecting each viewpoint, ideal for independent travelers to hike or drive at an easy pace. Mornings and evenings at this altitude can turn breezy and cool, so bring a warm layer. Weekday mornings are best for having this remote, tranquil scenery to yourself.

西湖療癒之里根場.count: Foliage around the thatched-roof gassho-style village
西湖療癒之里根場.address: 山梨縣南都留郡富士河口湖町西湖根場2710
西湖療癒之里根場.access_train: JR to Otsuki Station, transfer to the Fujikyuko Line to Kawaguchiko Station, then about 40 min by bus
西湖療癒之里根場.access_car: About 30 min from Kawaguchiko IC on the Chuo Expressway
西湖療癒之里根場.tagline: Step into a traditional thatched-roof village by Lake Saiko and find old farmhouses framed by Mount Fuji in autumn color.
西湖療癒之里根場.desc:
Saiko Iyashi no Sato Nenba is a preserved historic village on the shore of Lake Saiko that faithfully recreates Japan's traditional thatched-roof "kabuto-zukuri" farmhouses. From late October to early November, maples on both sides of the village and the hillside behind it turn together, washing the rustic valley in deep, early autumn color.

The village's signature composition pairs its traditional thatched-roof houses, a stream, and Mount Fuji in autumn color: rows of rustic wooden buildings sit alongside vivid foliage and a small footbridge over the stream, and with Fuji rising majestically in the background, the whole scene feels like stepping into a classic Japanese landscape.

The village's paths are well laid out and flat, and each thatched house holds a small museum, craft workshop, or historical display. It draws noticeably fewer visitors than nearby Lake Kawaguchi. Arriving before dawn on a weekday morning gives you the cleanest streetscape and the best light for photos.

輕井澤（雲場池）.count: The reflections on the pond's surface make for a striking scene
輕井澤（雲場池）.address: 長野縣北佐久郡輕井澤町輕井澤
輕井澤（雲場池）.access_train: About 15 min walk from JR Hokuriku Shinkansen Karuizawa Station
輕井澤（雲場池）.access_car: About 10 min from Karuizawa IC on the Joshin-etsu Expressway
輕井澤（雲場池）.tagline: A retreat at the foot of Mount Asama known as "Swan Lake," where ten thousand tsubo of maple meet the water.
輕井澤（雲場池）.desc:
Kumoba Pond sits in the historic resort town of Karuizawa, affectionately nicknamed "Swan Lake" for its shape, said to resemble a resting swan. From mid-October to early November, the maple forest ringing the long, narrow pond reaches its peak, dressing this tranquil retreat in vivid, lively color.

The signature scene here is the interplay of the narrow mirror-like pond and a full canopy of color: bands of vivid crimson and orange line the gentle gravel path, and when the mirror-still water perfectly reflects the blue sky alongside the dense larch and maple on both sides, the scene feels open and refined.

The loop path around the pond is completely flat and well maintained, taking about 20 minutes to walk in full — welcoming to strollers and visitors with grandparents in tow. As a world-famous destination, daytime crowds can be heavy with tour groups. Experienced photographers strongly recommend an early weekday morning for the best chance at a perfect mirror reflection.

戶隱.count: Abundant foliage around Togakushi Shrine and along the Okusha approach
戶隱.access_train: About 60 min by bus from JR Nagano Station to "Togakushi"
戶隱.access_car: About 40 min from Nagano IC on the Joshin-etsu Expressway
戶隱.tagline: Climb into the sacred grounds of Togakushi's nine-headed dragon worship, past Zuishinmon gate and a thousand-year avenue of cedar.
戶隱.desc:
The foot of Mount Togakushi has been a site of mountain asceticism since ancient times, famed nationwide for its deeply storied five Togakushi shrines. From early to late October, the primeval forest around the grand torii and old shrine buildings turns into a sea of red, dressing the sacred, solemn grounds in early autumn color.

The signature composition here pairs the vermilion Zuishinmon gate, thatched roofs, and a thousand-year-old cedar grove: colorful foliage crowds old stone lanterns and towering ancient trees, and walking the two-kilometer approach to the Okusha shrine, the interplay of stillness and color perfectly captures the temple's particular quiet.

The path from Zuishinmon to Okusha is a long, natural, gently sloping gravel trail, so sturdy hiking shoes with good grip and support are strongly recommended. Mountain mist often settles here in the early morning — stone Buddha statues glimpsed through drifting fog alongside the foliage make for the most mysterious, atmospheric shots, and mornings also mean fewer worshippers.

鏡池.count: The pond's surface reflects the Togakushi range and full autumn color
鏡池.address: 長野縣長野市戶隱中社
鏡池.access_train: About 60 min by bus from JR Nagano Station to "Kagami-ike Iriguchi," then a short walk
鏡池.access_car: About 40 min from Nagano IC on the Joshin-etsu Expressway
鏡池.tagline: Find a hidden volcanic pond deep in the Togakushi highlands where the sheer Togakushi range mirrors perfectly in full autumn color.
鏡池.desc:
Kagami-ike sits deep in the Togakushi highlands at roughly 1,000 meters, a compact, celebrated volcanic pond renowned across the Hokuriku region. Each October, the beech and maple forest around its shore reaches peak color, dressing this natural landmark in vivid splendor — a must-visit for landscape photographers.

The sight that made this pond famous online is the perfect pairing of glass-clear water with the rugged Togakushi range: standing on the purpose-built waterside boardwalk, you'll find the water so still and unrippled that it flips the gray, jagged cliffs and the lush foliage around them into a flawless, symmetrical mirror image.

The pondside path is gentle and well maintained, with a rustic café nearby, making for an easy, relaxed visit. Mornings on this highland pond are calmest, with the least wind — arriving on a clear, still morning, when sunlight filters through the trees onto the foliage, gives the best chance at a deeply atmospheric mirror shot.

松本城.count: hundreds of colorful trees throughout the castle park
松本城.access_train: About 15 min walk from Matsumoto Station on the JR Shinonoi Line
松本城.access_car: About 10 min from the Matsumoto IC on the Nagano Expressway
松本城.tagline: Climb Honshu's oldest surviving five-story, six-floor castle keep and take in the black lacquered tower framed by moat-side maples.
松本城.desc:
Built during the Eisho era, Matsumoto Castle ranks among Japan's four National Treasure castles, famed nationwide for its striking black-and-white silhouette known as the 'Crow Castle.' Each year from late October to early November, the hundreds of maples planted throughout the grounds turn scarlet in unison, dressing the towering old walls in early-autumn color.

The scene's signature draw is the classic pairing of the castle's black lacquered keep, its vermilion gate, and the maples framing it. The colorful trees crowd the gentle moat, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the soaring National Treasure keep, the snow-capped Northern Alps in the distance, and the full sweep of autumn color, the composition opens into a scene of refined Japanese aesthetics.

The park's terrain is completely flat and its old paths are well maintained, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. Inside the National Treasure keep, though, the stairways are extremely steep (up to a 61-degree pitch), so watch your footing. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a perfect mirror-still shot.

金澤城公園.count: hundreds of colorful trees throughout the park
金澤城公園.fee: Free (Ishikawa Gate, Sanjukken Nagaya and other buildings ¥320)
金澤城公園.access_train: About 15 min by bus from JR Kanazawa Station to Kenrokuen-shita / Kanazawa Castle
金澤城公園.access_car: About 20 min from the Kanazawa-nishi IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
金澤城公園.tagline: Climb the ramparts of Maeda Toshiie's unconquered stronghold for a blaze of maple color along the moat below the Hishi Yagura turret and Gojukken Nagaya.
金澤城公園.desc:
Kanazawa Castle Park occupies the former site of the Kanazawa Castle of the Maeda clan, lords of the Kaga domain in the Edo period, right beside Kenroku-en. Each year from late October to mid-November, the park's famous maple slopes reach their peak, with hundreds of trees turning scarlet together to dress the massive white-plastered walls in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the historic moat, the imposing stone ramparts, and the maples framing them. The colorful trees line the gentle waterway, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the white-walled Hishi Yagura turret and the full spread of color, the scene opens into an elegant expression of Japanese aesthetics and the legacy of the Maeda clan.

The park's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained stone paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. During the autumn-color festival, a dreamlike evening illumination makes the reflections even more ethereal. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot of this historic castle.

鶴仙溪.count: colors the full 1.3km length of the gorge
鶴仙溪.address: 石川縣加賀市山中溫泉
鶴仙溪.access_train: About 20 min by bus from Kaga-Onsen Station on the JR Hokuriku Main Line to Yamanaka Onsen
鶴仙溪.access_car: About 20 min from the Kaga IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
鶴仙溪.tagline: Wander the first gorge walkway of Yamanaka Onsen, lost in the Korogi Bridge, the Ayatori Bridge, and a sea of autumn color.
鶴仙溪.desc:
Kakusenkei is a hidden 1.3km gorge carved along the Daishoji River deep in this hot-spring town, ranked among Hokuriku's top spots for autumn foliage. Each year from mid- to late November, the towering primeval forest on both banks and the maples along the old moat change color together, blanketing the deep ravine in a riot of red and gold.

The signature sight is the meeting of the rustic Korogi Bridge, the strikingly modern Ayatori Bridge, and the gorge's autumn color in one frame. Walking the well-maintained riverside boardwalk, you'll find a calm jade-green stream on one side and a cascading, layered tapestry of color pouring down the steep cliffs on the other — a blend of modern lines and traditional beauty.

The gorge walkway is flat and well maintained, perfect for an easy morning hike paired with a soak in the hot springs. Because the main viewing bridges and waterside boardwalks are narrow, please don't linger there for photos or set up large tripods. Visit on a weekday morning, when the light reaches deepest into the valley.

西山公園.access_train: About 20 min walk from Sabae Station on the JR Hokuriku Main Line
西山公園.access_car: About 5 min from the Sabae IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
西山公園.tagline: Wander this sprawling water-garden oasis in Sabae and marvel at a rippling carpet of color from 1,600 blazing Iroha maples.
西山公園.desc:
Nishiyama Koen, ranked among Japan's 100 Best Urban Parks, is one of Hokuriku's largest and most complete autumn-foliage destinations. Each year from mid- to late November, the park's roughly 1,600 Iroha maples and other maple trees change color together, blanketing the natural hillside in a riot of red and gold.

The visual highlight is the classic pairing of a traditional Japanese garden, a vermilion bridge, and a full carpet of color. Climbing the zigzagging path toward the summit, you're flanked by dense, blazing maples the whole way, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the tall tunnel of autumn leaves, the scene opens into the height of horticultural artistry.

The park is spacious with gently rolling terrain, and its wide, well-maintained paths make it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. It's also home to the free Nishiyama Zoo, famous for its red pandas, making it a great choice for families. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for a relaxed stroll and sweeping photos.

刈込池.count: autumn color and mirror reflections around a deep-mountain pond at the foot of Mt. Haku
刈込池.hours: Access depends on the mountain trail (during White Road opening season)
刈込池.address: 福井縣大野市南六呂師
刈込池.access_car: About 60 min from the Ono IC on the Chubu-Judan Expressway (no public transport)
刈込池.tagline: Make the pilgrimage to a hidden volcanic pond at the foot of Mt. Haku and capture Mt. Sannomine reversed in a perfect mirror of color.
刈込池.desc:
Karikomi-ike is a pristine, little-known volcanic dammed pond hidden upstream on the Uchinami River, quiet and crystal clear. Each year from mid- to late October, the mountain birch and Japanese beech ringing the pond reach their peak, dressing the deep primeval forest in vivid color — a spot photographers in the know consider the ultimate hidden gem.

What has made this pond famous online is the perfect reflection of towering Mt. Sannomine on its glass-clear surface. Standing on the dedicated waterside boardwalk, you'll find the water so still it holds a flawless double of the golden-and-red mountainside and blue sky above it, framed in a breathtaking, expansive composition.

Reaching Karikomi-ike requires about an hour on foot from the Koike parking area, along a natural trail with rocky steps and steep sections — proper hiking shoes and a warm, windproof jacket are strongly recommended. Aim for a clear, windless morning, when the water is most likely to turn into that perfect mirror.

養浩館庭園.count: refined autumn color throughout the strolling pond garden
養浩館庭園.access_train: About 15 min walk from Fukui Station on the JR line
養浩館庭園.access_car: About 15 min from the Fukui IC on the Hokuriku Expressway
養浩館庭園.tagline: Stroll this historic circuit garden once kept by the Fukui domain lords and savor the refined harmony of the lakeside residence and autumn maples.
養浩館庭園.desc:
Yokokan Teien is a fine garden that faithfully preserves the look of the Edo-period villa of the Matsudaira clan, lords of the Fukui domain, and is regularly ranked among the top gardens in an American Japanese-garden magazine. Each year from mid- to late November, the maples ringing the garden's broad central pond come into color, dressing this historic site in classical elegance.

The visual focus is the dialogue across time between the exquisite classical lakeside residence, the reflecting pond, and the maples. The rustic sukiya-style building appears to float on the water; sit on its tatami and look out, and the still pond perfectly mirrors the pink and crimson foliage — a scene of quiet, elegant Japanese beauty where movement and stillness intertwine.

The garden's terrain is completely flat, and its old paths are well maintained, making for an easy, comfortable walk. Being right in central Fukui, it's very convenient to reach — ideal for an unhurried morning stroll for independent travelers. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning to capture the wood grain of the old buildings in soft light for evocative, story-rich shots.

惠那峽.address: 岐阜縣恵那市大井町惠那峡
惠那峽.access_train: About 10 min by taxi from Ena Station on the JR Chuo Main Line
惠那峽.access_car: About 10 min from the Ena IC on the Chuo Expressway
惠那峽.tagline: Ride a sightseeing boat down the Kiso River and marvel at the Oi Dam's towering cliffs framed by a valley full of autumn color.
惠那峽.desc:
Enakyo is a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty — a dammed gorge carved over the ages by the Kiso River and reshaped by the construction of the Oi Dam. Each year from late October to mid-November, tall maples along the steep, gray, jagged cliffs on both banks reach their peak, dressing the deep gorge in a riot of color.

The visual highlight is the interplay of strength and softness between the jagged rock formations, the jade-green water, and the layered autumn color. Take a leisurely ride on the Enakyo sightseeing boat and you'll pass naturally formed rocks like Kasa-iwa (Umbrella Rock) and Beni-iwa (Crimson Rock) threading through golden groves, set off by the clear water in an open, dynamic composition.

The area is well laid out, with flat, easy walking along the main viewing route and waterside park paths, very friendly to visitors with elderly companions or strollers. As a classic destination, it's also very convenient by car. Visit between 10am and noon, when sunlight reaches straight down into the gorge and the autumn colors are at their most vivid.

下呂溫泉.count: colors the hot-spring town and the nearby thatched-house village
下呂溫泉.access_train: Immediately on foot from Gero Station on the JR Takayama Main Line
下呂溫泉.access_car: About 30 min from the Hida-Kanayama IC on the Tokai-Hokuriku Expressway
下呂溫泉.tagline: Wander one of Japan's three great hot-spring towns on the Hida River and savor the thatched Gero Onsen Gassho Village and its illuminated autumn leaves.
下呂溫泉.desc:
Gero Onsen, ranked alongside Kusatsu and Arima among Japan's three great hot springs, is a hot-spring town steeped in history. Each year from early to mid-November, the 'Gero Onsen Gassho Village' and the nearby 'Momiji no Sato' (Maple Village) beside the hot-spring street reach their peak, with hundreds of maples turning brilliant red to dress the town in sacred, classic color.

The signature scene is the dialogue across time between the rustic thatched-roof farmhouses, the hot-spring steam, and the autumn maples. Colorful trees crowd around old stone lanterns, and when the evening illumination switches on, the whole hillside transforms into a golden world — a dreamlike, deeply Asian-aesthetic scene set against the still water.

The hot-spring street and village paths are flat and well maintained, ideal for an easy morning stroll paired with a hot-spring day trip. As a world-class destination, it draws large crowds during the day. Visit on a weekday morning or during the evening illumination for the best chance at evocative, story-rich shots.

飛驒高山.count: abundant color throughout the old town and around the Takayama Jinya
飛驒高山.access_train: About 10 min walk from Takayama Station on the JR Takayama Main Line
飛驒高山.access_car: About 45 min from the Hida-Kiyomi IC on the Tokai-Hokuriku Expressway
飛驒高山.tagline: Wander the traditional wooden streets along the Miyagawa River and catch the vermilion Nakabashi Bridge ablaze against a river of maple color.
飛驒高山.desc:
Hida Takayama preserves a complete Edo-period townscape of wooden buildings, affectionately known as 'Little Kyoto of Hida.' Each year from mid-October to mid-November, hundreds of maples surrounding the old streets and the banks of the Miyagawa River turn scarlet together, dressing the storied town in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the vermilion Nakabashi Bridge, Edo-period buildings, and the maples framing them. The colorful trees crowd the gentle riverbank, and when the still Miyagawa mirrors the bright red bridge, the rustic wooden merchant houses, and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into a study in refined Japanese aesthetics.

The old town is completely flat, with well-maintained old stone-paved streets, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The surrounding area is rich with cultural exhibits and Hida beef cuisine, ideal for independent travelers who like an unhurried pace. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best atmospheric shots.

修善寺.count: abundant autumn color along the bamboo path and the Katsura River
修善寺.access_train: About 7 min by bus from Shuzenji Station on the Izuhakone Railway to Shuzenji Onsen
修善寺.access_car: About 50 min from the Numazu IC on the Tomei Expressway
修善寺.tagline: Wander the oldest hot-spring town on the Izu Peninsula and lose yourself in the bamboo path, the vermilion Katsura Bridge, and Shuzenji Temple's maples.
修善寺.desc:
Shuzenji Onsen, ranked among Japan's 100 Best Hot Springs, is Izu's oldest hot spring, threaded through by the Katsura River. Because it sits in a warm hot-spring valley, its foliage turns relatively late — each year from mid-November to early December, the maples around the historic Shuzenji Temple and the riverside change color together into a riot of vivid hues.

The most representative expression of Japanese aesthetics here is the classical dialogue of the vermilion Katsura Bridge, the bamboo path, and the full spread of autumn color. Walking the well-maintained riverside promenade, the lush green bamboo and the cascading red-and-gold maples create a striking visual contrast, complemented by the town's distinctive old buildings for a scene of real depth.

The hot-spring town's paths are flat and well maintained, very friendly to visitors with elderly companions or strollers. During the autumn-color festival, Shuzenji Temple's garden opens to the public for a limited time — well worth the visit. Arrive on a weekday morning, when there are fewer worshippers, for the best window to capture the classic, evocative atmosphere.

熱海梅園.count: distinctive autumn color throughout the garden
熱海梅園.fee: Free (fee charged during the plum festival)
熱海梅園.access_train: About 20 min by bus from Atami Station on the JR line to Baien
熱海梅園.access_car: About 20 min from the Ishibashi IC on the Seisho Bypass
熱海梅園.tagline: Step into Honshu's latest-turning foliage spot and catch early-winter maples, an old wooden bridge, and 500 trees performing together.
熱海梅園.desc:
Atami Baien is famous nationwide as a spring plum-blossom destination, but it's also known as the place where Honshu's autumn foliage turns latest of all. Each year from late November to mid-December, the roughly 500 old maple trees planted here reach their peak — timing so late that visitors can sometimes catch early-winter maples and early-spring plum blossoms in the same frame.

The visual core is the mirrored interplay of a classic, water-fed stream, old stone bridges, and the maples above them. Colorful trees line the gentle gravel paths, and the still water perfectly reflects the garden's several rustic wooden bridges together with the full sweep of color, building a layered scene with an elegant, meditative Eastern quality.

The grounds are well planned with gently rolling terrain, making it easy for the whole family to wander while soaking in the history. During the foliage season, an evening illumination makes the reflections even more ethereal. Visit on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for a relaxed stroll and the perfect shot.

濱松城.count: abundant color throughout the castle park
濱松城.address: 靜岡縣浜松市中央区元城町100-2
濱松城.access_train: About 15 min walk from Hamamatsu Station on the JR line
濱松城.access_car: About 20 min from the Hamamatsu IC on the Tomei Expressway
濱松城.tagline: Climb the 'Castle of Success' where Tokugawa Ieyasu came of age, and take in its rough-hewn stone ramparts ablaze with moat-side maples.
濱松城.desc:
Hamamatsu Castle, built in the Edo period, is famous nationwide as the place where Tokugawa Ieyasu spent his formative years, earning it the affectionate nickname 'Castle of Success.' Each year from late November to early December, the park's hundreds of maples turn scarlet together, adding a soft touch of autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the rugged, nozura-style stone ramparts, the reconstructed keep, and the maples framing them. The colorful trees crowd the gentle moat, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the weathered, history-laden walls and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into the grand, historic presence of this castle.

The park's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained old paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The keep's interior houses a rich collection of historical artifacts. Set aside about an hour for a stroll — weekday mornings are quietest, and best for a perfect mirror shot of this historic castle.

名古屋城.count: abundant color throughout the castle park
名古屋城.address: 愛知縣名古屋市中区本丸1-1
名古屋城.access_train: About 5 min walk from Shiyakusho Station on the Nagoya Municipal Subway
名古屋城.access_car: About 5 min from the Marunouchi IC on the Nagoya Expressway
名古屋城.tagline: Wander one of Japan's Three Great Castles and catch its golden shachihoko-topped keep framed by the maples of Ninomaru Garden.
名古屋城.desc:
Nagoya Castle, built on the order of Tokugawa Ieyasu, is a magnificent historic site ranked among Japan's Three Great Castles. Each year from late November to early December, hundreds of maples turn scarlet together around the grand old moat, the Honmaru Palace, and the famed Ninomaru Garden.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the golden shachihoko-topped roof, the imposing stone ramparts, and the maples framing them. Colorful trees crowd around old moss-covered ground beneath towering ancient trees, and when the still moat perfectly mirrors the grand keep and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into a study in refined Japanese aesthetics.

The park's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained stone paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The recently restored Honmaru Palace features exquisite woodwork inside and is well worth a visit. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot of this historic castle.

東山動植物園.count: about 1,000 maples and other colorful trees in the park
東山動植物園.address: 愛知縣名古屋市千種区東山元町3-70
東山動植物園.access_train: About 3 min walk from Higashiyama Koen Station on the Nagoya Municipal Subway Higashiyama Line
東山動植物園.access_car: About 5 min from the Higashiyama Koen IC on the Nagoya Expressway
東山動植物園.tagline: Wander this sprawling urban nature oasis and marvel at the gassho-zukuri farmhouse, the big pond, and a dense corridor of maple foliage.
東山動植物園.desc:
Higashiyama Zoo and Botanical Gardens is a vast urban nature park combining a large botanical garden, a zoo, and historic architecture. Each year from mid- to late November, hundreds of maples reach their peak around the historic gassho-zukuri farmhouse, relocated here from Gifu Prefecture, in the botanical garden section.

The visual highlight is the classic pairing of the traditional thatched roof, a reflecting pond, and the surrounding maples. The colorful trees line the gentle waterway and gravel paths, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the rustic old building and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into the height of horticultural artistry.

The park's paths are entirely flat and barrier-free, making it easy for families with elderly companions or strollers to wander at ease. The park is also home to the famous Higashiyama Sky Tower, offering sweeping views from above. Set aside about two hours for a stroll — weekday mornings are quietest and best for wide, atmospheric shots.

定光寺.count: deep-mountain autumn color around the temple
定光寺.address: 愛知縣瀬戸市定光寺町373
定光寺.access_train: About 10 min walk from Jokoji Station on the JR Chuo Main Line
定光寺.access_car: About 20 min from the Kasugai IC on the Tomei Expressway
定光寺.tagline: Visit the mausoleum of Tokugawa Yoshinao, founder of the Owari Tokugawa line, and walk a tunnel of maples to this Tokugawa family shrine.
定光寺.desc:
Jokoji is an ancient Rinzai-sect temple with over 1,300 years of history, set at the foot of the mountains in Seto. Each year from mid- to late November, hundreds of maples and other maple-family trees along the approach to the main hall, 'Muiden,' and the nationally Important Cultural Property 'Genkyoko Mausoleum,' reach their peak, dressing the sacred site in solemn color.

The most representative composition here is the historic dialogue between the imposing wooden mountain gate, the stone steps, and the maple grove. Colorful trees crowd around old moss-covered stone lanterns and beneath towering ancient trees; when afternoon mist drifts through the mountains, the maples glimpsed through the haze best capture the quiet, historic, meditative mood unique to this old temple.

Reaching the main hall and mausoleum requires climbing some natural stone paths and long staircases — comfortable, non-slip shoes are strongly recommended. The surroundings are quiet and relatively free of crowds. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is clearest, for the best window to capture the temple's classic, atmospheric scenery.

彥根城.count: 500+ trees across the castle park and Genkyuen Garden
彥根城.access_train: About 15 min walk from Hikone Station on the JR Biwako Line
彥根城.access_car: About 10 min from the Hikone IC on the Meishin Expressway
彥根城.tagline: Climb one of the twelve surviving original castle keeps of the Ii clan and take in the National Treasure tower mirrored in the autumn colors of Genkyuen Garden.
彥根城.desc:
Hikone Castle, built in the Keicho era, is a magnificent castle that has preserved its complete Edo-period fortifications and is one of Japan's five National Treasure castles. Each year from late November to early December, the famous daimyo garden 'Genkyuen,' right beside the moat, comes into its foliage season, dressing the imposing white-walled old castle in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the National Treasure three-star keep, views of Lake Biwa, and the maples. The colorful trees line the gentle waterway, and when the mirror-still pond perfectly reflects the towering keep, the rustic wooden bridges, and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into a study in refined Japanese aesthetics.

The castle sits on a natural hill, and reaching the keep requires climbing a fairly steep old stone staircase — non-slip shoes are recommended — while the Genkyuen Garden below is flat and easy to walk. During the foliage festival, an evening illumination adds a dreamlike touch. Visit on a weekday morning for the quietest atmosphere.

石山寺.count: about 300 maple trees on the grounds
石山寺.access_train: About 10 min walk from Ishiyamadera Station on the Keihan Ishiyama-Sakamoto Line
石山寺.access_car: About 10 min from the Seta-Higashi IC on the Meishin Expressway
石山寺.tagline: Visit this Shingon head temple tied to Murasaki Shikibu and see its striking wollastonite outcrops and main hall lit up amid autumn maples.
石山寺.desc:
Ishiyamadera, founded by the priest Roben and set on the banks of the Seta River, is famous nationwide as the temple where Murasaki Shikibu is said to have conceived 'The Tale of Genji' — a head temple of the Tozan school of Shingon Buddhism. Each year from mid- to late November, hundreds of old maples burst into color around the temple's massive outcrop of wollastonite, a nationally designated Natural Monument.

The most representative scene here is the interplay of strength and softness between the striking black wollastonite cliffs, the Tahoto pagoda, and the maple grove. The rustic wooden main hall spans the rugged rock, with a deep-red sea of maples spilling down the valley slope at its feet. When the evening illumination switches on, dreamlike light plays across the foliage for a scene of real depth.

The temple grounds are well laid out with flat gravel paths, though part of the route to the Tahoto pagoda includes natural stone steps — comfortable walking shoes are recommended. During the foliage festival, the temple collects a visiting offering and offers a limited-edition red seal stamp. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is clearest, for the best photos.

比叡山延曆寺.count: abundant color across the vast temple precincts
比叡山延曆寺.address: 滋賀縣大津市坂本本町4220
比叡山延曆寺.access_train: About 11 min by cable car from Hieizan-Sakamoto Station on the JR line to Enryakuji Station
比叡山延曆寺.access_car: About 40 min from the Kyoto-Higashi IC on the Meishin Expressway
比叡山延曆寺.tagline: Wander the sacred forest grounds of the Tendai sect's head temple and marvel at the layered color along the Enryakuji road and Konpon Chudo hall.
比叡山延曆寺.desc:
Hieizan Enryakuji, straddling Kyoto and Shiga, is a World Heritage head temple of the Tendai sect, revered as the mother of Japanese Buddhism. Sitting at an elevation of about 800 meters, its foliage turns relatively early — each year from late October to mid-November, the entire sacred mountain is blanketed in a rich gradient of red and gold.

The core appeal is the historic dialogue between the vividly colored old temple halls, the Hieizan driveway, and the maple groves. Colorful trees crowd tightly along the old stone-paved approach, especially in the 'Todo' precinct, where old buildings set among vividly colored cliffs look most ethereal when afternoon mist drifts through the mountains.

Because the temple spans an enormous area (divided into the Todo, Saito, and Yokawa precincts), driving or taking the well-run shuttle bus between areas is strongly recommended. Mornings and evenings bring strong winds and a chill in these deep mountains, so bring a warm coat for photography. Visit on a weekday morning for the quietest, most solitary deep-mountain atmosphere.

嵐山.address: 京都府京都市右京区嵯峨天龍寺芒ノ馬場町
嵐山.access_train: Immediately on foot from Arashiyama Station on the Hankyu Arashiyama Line; about 5 min walk from Saga-Arashiyama Station on the JR Sagano Line
嵐山.access_car: About 5 min from the Arashiyama IC on the Kyoto Jukan Expressway
嵐山.tagline: Wander the Oi River waterfront by Togetsukyo Bridge and take in the layered color of the Hozu Gorge and Mt. Katsura.
嵐山.desc:
Arashiyama is a sprawling resort area combining historic sites, bamboo groves, and dramatic nature. Each year from late November to early December it reaches peak foliage, as maples relay their color from Togetsukyo Bridge and Tenryuji Temple all the way to the Hozu Gorge, dressing the entire green mountainside in deep autumn hues.

The core appeal is the classic combination of the elegant Togetsukyo Bridge, traditional yakatabune boats, and layered autumn color. Walking the gentle path along the Oi River, you'll see traditional wooden pleasure boats gliding across the jade-green water, set against the crimson-and-gold mountainside of Arashiyama behind — an open, visually striking composition.

The area covers a lot of ground, so riding the Sagano Scenic Railway or taking the Hozugawa River boat trip is strongly recommended for different angles on the gorge's autumn color. It's well shaded and pleasantly cool here, making it ideal for a full day trip. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best relaxed stroll and scenic photography.

東福寺.count: about 2,000 maple trees below Tsutenkyo Bridge
東福寺.address: 京都府京都市東山区本町15丁目778
東福寺.access_train: About 10 min walk from Tofukuji Station on the JR Nara Line / Keihan Main Line
東福寺.access_car: About 10 min from the Kamogawa-Higashi IC on the Hanshin Expressway
東福寺.tagline: Walk the Tsutenkyo Bridge of this great Zen temple and be stunned by the Senyokan gorge ablaze in a sea of maple color.
東福寺.desc:
Tofukuji, in Kyoto's Higashiyama ward, is a top-ranked Zen temple counted among the city's Five Great Zen Temples. Each year from late November to early December, the roughly 2,000 'Tsutenkaede' maples around the steep Senyokan gorge change color together, blanketing this deep mountain ravine in a riot of color.

The most stunning centerpiece is the view from Tsutenkyo Bridge looking down over the Senyokan gorge's autumn foliage. Standing on the huge wooden corridor bridge, you look down on what feels like a crashing sea of crimson maples below; when morning light flickers through the canopy and scatters across the greenery, the visual impact is striking.

As one of Kyoto's top foliage spots, stopping to take photos on the Tsutenkyo and Gaunkyo bridges is banned during peak season to keep things safe. The temple grounds have plenty of natural gravel paths and old stone steps, requiring some stamina. It's best to arrive right at opening on a weekday, for the quietest atmosphere and the best light for photography.

南禪寺.count: abundant autumn color throughout the grounds and around the Suirokaku aqueduct
南禪寺.address: 京都府京都市左京区南禪寺福地町
南禪寺.access_train: About 10 min walk from Keage Station on the subway Tozai Line
南禪寺.access_car: About 20 min from the Kyoto-Higashi IC on the Meishin Expressway
南禪寺.tagline: Wander the highest-ranked Zen temple in Japan and catch its dry rock garden and the old red-brick Suirokaku aqueduct wreathed in maples.
南禪寺.desc:
Nanzenji holds the highest rank among Japan's Zen temples, sitting above even the 'Five Mountains of Kyoto.' Each year from late November to early December, hundreds of maples reach their peak around the temple's expansive old grounds and its Sanmon gate, wrapping the imposing wooden buildings in a blaze of red — one of Kyoto's celebrated early-autumn destinations.

The visual highlight is the classical dialogue between the nationally Important Cultural Property Sanmon gate, moss, and the red-brick Suirokaku aqueduct. The retro arched waterway, built in the Meiji era, appears together with the cascading red-and-gold foliage above and the rustic stone steps below — a scene where movement and stillness intertwine to capture the temple's deep sense of history.

The grounds are completely flat, with well-maintained stone paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. Nearby are the famous Hojo Garden and Tenju-an, plus the chance to try traditional yudofu tofu. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best classic, atmospheric photos.

北野天滿宮.count: about 350 maple trees on the grounds
北野天滿宮.hours: 10:00–16:00 (during the foliage season, Momiji-en / Kamiyagawa garden)
北野天滿宮.address: 京都府京都市上京区馬喰町
北野天滿宮.access_train: Immediately on foot from the Kitano Tenmangu-mae city bus stop
北野天滿宮.access_car: About 30 min from the Kyoto-Minami IC on the Meishin Expressway
北野天滿宮.tagline: Visit the head shrine of Sugawara no Michizane and see the historic Odoi earthworks, the Kamiyagawa River, and Uguisu Bridge in autumn color.
北野天滿宮.desc:
Kitano Tenmangu is the head shrine of all Tenmangu shrines across Japan. Each year from late November to early December, the shrine's western side opens for a limited time to reveal the 'Odoi' earthwork ramparts — built as a defense line by Toyotomi Hideyoshi — along with the attached 'Momiji-en' foliage garden, where about 350 old maples dress the gentle waterside in dazzling color.

The most representative classical composition here is the vermilion Uguisu Bridge, the Kamiyagawa stream, and the maples together in one frame. Colorful trees line the gentle river, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the historic bridge, old stone lanterns, and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into refined Japanese aesthetics.

The Momiji-en garden follows the natural terrain, with well-maintained paths that make for an easy, comfortable walk. During the foliage festival, an evening illumination makes the reflections even more ethereal. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best classic, atmospheric shots.

貴船神社.count: about 200 colorful trees along the approach
貴船神社.address: 京都府京都市左京区鞍馬貴船町180
貴船神社.access_train: About 30 min walk from Kibuneguchi Station on the Eizan Railway, or take the bus to Kifune
貴船神社.access_car: About 40 min from the Kyoto-Higashi IC on the Meishin Expressway
貴船神社.tagline: Head into the deep mountains of northern Kyoto to this ancient water-god shrine and climb its lantern-lined stone stairway through old cedar and maple color.
貴船神社.desc:
Kifune Jinja sits in a deep mountain valley at the foot of Mt. Kurama — a historic shrine, deeply revered, that guards the source of the water. Because the high-altitude mountain climate runs cool, its foliage turns later than the lowlands, coming into full bloom from early to mid-November, when hundreds of Iroha maples dress the solemn shrine grounds in early-autumn color.

The most representative expression of Japanese aesthetics here is the historic dialogue between the long stone stairway lined with kasuga lanterns, the vividly colored old shrine buildings, and the maples. Colorful trees crowd the neatly arranged rows of vermilion lanterns on either side, and when the lights come on at dusk, the play of light and shadow across the foliage evokes a deep, mysterious Eastern spirituality.

Reaching the main hall requires climbing several hundred old stone steps — comfortable, non-slip shoes are strongly recommended for worship and photography. Mountain mornings here are prone to mist, and the stone steps and maples glimpsed through drifting fog take on a mysterious beauty. Riding the Eizan Railway through the 'Momiji Tunnel' is another favorite recommended by locals.

大阪城公園.address: 大阪府大阪市中央区大阪城1-1
大阪城公園.access_train: Immediately on foot from Osakajokoen Station on the JR Osaka Loop Line
大阪城公園.access_car: About 5 min from the Morinomiya IC on the Hanshin Expressway
大阪城公園.tagline: Wander beside the massive stone ramparts of the Otemon gate and catch the nationally Registered Cultural Property keep framed by a 300-year-old ginkgo.
大阪城公園.desc:
Osaka Jo Koen is a vast historic urban park built around the grand old moat and Honmaru Palace. Each year from early November to early December, the park's celebrated foliage promenade reaches its peak, with hundreds of towering ginkgo trees turning golden together to dress the imposing castle walls in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the massive stone ramparts, the gold-leafed white castle keep, and the autumn color. The colorful trees line the gentle moat, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the towering keep, a giant ginkgo tree some 300 years old, and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into the grand presence of this historic castle.

The park's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained old paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The surrounding area includes the Nishinomaru Garden and rich historical exhibits, ideal for independent travelers who like an unhurried pace. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot of this historic castle.

萬博紀念公園.count: about 3,800 maples and other colorful trees in the park
萬博紀念公園.address: 大阪府吹田市千里万博公園1-1
萬博紀念公園.access_train: Immediately on foot from Banpaku-kinen-koen Station on the Osaka Monorail
萬博紀念公園.access_car: About 10 min from the Suita IC on the Meishin Expressway
萬博紀念公園.tagline: Wander the sprawling grounds of the former 1970 World Expo site and see the Tower of the Sun set against a modern tableau of maple streams and waterfalls.
萬博紀念公園.desc:
Banpaku Kinen Koen is a vast urban oasis built on the former site of the 1970 World Expo. Each year from early to late November, over 20 varieties and roughly 10,000 maple and zelkova trees around the 'Momiji-dani' (Maple Valley) on the west side of the park's Japanese Garden, and throughout the Nature and Culture Garden, reach their peak together, blanketing the sprawling grounds in vivid color.

The visual centerpiece is the interplay of the avant-garde Tower of the Sun, a clear stream, and a full carpet of color. Walking the well-maintained, gently graveled paths, you'll find bands of red and yellow flowers lining the gentle waterway. When morning light filters through the canopy and falls on the trickling Momiji-dani waterfall, framed together with the towering Tower of the Sun in the distance, the scene captures a refined, modern landscape aesthetic.

Most of the park's terrain is completely flat, with excellent barrier-free paths and wooden boardwalks, very friendly to visitors with elderly companions or strollers. During the foliage festival, the tea house in the Japanese Garden opens for a limited time. Arrive right at the 9:30am opening on a weekday for the best pure, sweeping shots of the foliage.

勝尾寺.count: about 1,000 maple trees on the grounds
勝尾寺.hours: 08:00–17:00 (until 18:00 on weekends, extended during the foliage season)
勝尾寺.address: 大阪府箕面市粟生間谷2914-1
勝尾寺.access_train: About 30 min by bus from Senri-Chuo Station on the Kita-Osaka Kyuko Line
勝尾寺.access_car: About 30 min from the Toyonaka-Minami IC on the Kinki Expressway
勝尾寺.tagline: Visit the 23rd temple of the Saigoku Kannon pilgrimage, home to countless victory-daruma dolls, amid mist-wreathed water and autumn color.
勝尾寺.desc:
Katsuoji sits in the wooded hills of Minoh, an ancient temple famed nationwide for granting victory in all endeavors, its grounds lined with countless 'Victory Daruma' dolls. Each year from mid-November to early December, the temple's vast grounds, built along the mountainside, are dressed in autumn color as thousands of maples and beech trees change together.

The core appeal is the historic dialogue between the misty, water-wreathed foliage and the daruma dolls. Blue and purple blooms spread along the shore of Kannon Pond and the hillside, and when mist sprays out over the pond at set times like something from a fairy tale, it appears alongside countless red daruma hidden among the flowers, taking on an especially mysterious, fantastical quality when lit up at night.

Because the entire temple is built into the hillside, the approach involves a fair number of steps — comfortable, non-slip shoes are strongly recommended. There's little shade on the grounds, so bringing a parasol is a good idea. Weekday mornings see fewer worshippers, making it the easiest time to capture a clean shot of the shrine grounds and the daruma.

姬路城.count: abundant color throughout the castle park and around Kokoen Garden
姬路城.access_train: About 15 min walk from Himeji Station on the JR line
姬路城.access_car: About 20 min from the Sanyo-Himeji-Higashi IC on the Sanyo Expressway
姬路城.tagline: Climb the never-conquered White Heron Castle and take in its five-story, six-floor National Treasure keep ablaze with moat-side maples.
姬路城.desc:
Himeji Castle was Japan's first site to be inscribed as a World Heritage Site, and it's one of the twelve castles in Japan with an original surviving keep. Each year from late October to mid-November, hundreds of maples turn scarlet together around the park's famous 'Sannomaru Plaza' and the old moat, dressing the pure white keep in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the brilliant white keep, the imposing stone ramparts, and the maples. The colorful trees line the gentle moat, and when the still water perfectly mirrors the majestic National Treasure keep and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into a striking blend of grandeur and softness befitting this historic castle.

The castle sits on a natural hill, and reaching the keep requires climbing a fairly steep old stone staircase — non-slip shoes are recommended. The keep's interior is well preserved. Set aside about 1.5 hours; a weekday morning visit best avoids the crowds, for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot of this historic castle.

六甲山.count: abundant autumn color near the summit and around Arima Onsen
六甲山.address: 兵庫縣神戸市灘区六甲山町北六甲4512-98
六甲山.access_train: About 30 min by bus from Rokko Station on the Hankyu Kobe Line
六甲山.access_car: About 20 min from the Nishinomiya-Yamaguchi IC on the Hanshin Expressway
六甲山.tagline: Ride the retro Rokko cable car and look out over the multi-island beauty of the Seto Inland Sea and a mountainside striped with color.
六甲山.desc:
Rokkosan is a highland resort beloved in every season, rising just beside the city of Kobe. Each year from mid-October to mid-November, its once-green slopes transform into a riot of color as thousands of maples and beech trees change together, dressing the wild mountain forest in vivid hues.

The most celebrated view here is the meeting of a bird's-eye panorama from the sky observatory and the layered mountainside of color. Ride the 'Rokko Cable' slowly up into the air, feel the cool highland breeze, and look down from a god's-eye view over a color carpet that stretches endlessly with the terrain of the valley, taking in the vast Seto Inland Sea in the same glance.

Being at high elevation, it's noticeably cooler here than on the plains below, making it a fine escape for early-autumn foliage viewing. The open highland terrain offers almost no shelter, so be sure to secure your tripod and hat when shooting outdoors. Climb on a clear morning for the best visibility, when the sweeping views and flowering landscape come together perfectly.

有馬溫泉.count: abundant autumn color around the hot-spring town and Zuihoji Park
有馬溫泉.address: 兵庫縣神戸市北区有馬町
有馬溫泉.access_train: Immediately on foot from Arima-Onsen Station on the Kobe Electric Railway
有馬溫泉.access_car: About 20 min from the Nishinomiya-Yamaguchi IC on the Hanshin Expressway
有馬溫泉.tagline: Wander this gorge town, one of Japan's three ancient hot springs, and savor Zuihoji Park, the vermilion Nene Bridge, and illuminated autumn color.
有馬溫泉.desc:
Arima Onsen, ranked alongside Dogo and Shirahama among Japan's three ancient hot springs, is a hot-spring town steeped in history. Each year from early to mid-November, the nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty 'Zuihoji Park,' right beside the hot-spring street, reaches its peak, with some 2,000 old maple trees bursting into color and dressing the lush green valley in a riot of red and gold.

The most representative classical scene here is the dialogue across time between the 'Nightfall Garden,' tied to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the vermilion Nene Bridge, and the autumn maples. Colorful trees crowd around old stone lanterns, and when the evening illumination switches on, the whole hillside transforms into a golden world, offset by the still water for a scene rich in Eastern aesthetics.

The hot-spring street and park paths are well maintained, ideal for an easy morning stroll paired with a hot-spring day trip. As a world-class destination, it draws large crowds during the day. Visit on a weekday morning or during the evening illumination for the best chance at evocative, story-rich shots.

奈良公園.address: 奈良縣奈良市登大路町30
奈良公園.access_train: About 5 min walk from Kintetsu-Nara Station on the Kintetsu Nara Line
奈良公園.access_car: About 20 min from the Tenri IC on the Nishimeihan Expressway
奈良公園.tagline: Wander this vast ancient-capital oasis and catch Todaiji's giant ginkgo and wild deer wandering through autumn color.
奈良公園.desc:
Nara Koen is a huge urban oasis spanning about 500 hectares, home to World Heritage sites like Todaiji Temple and Kasuga Taisha Shrine. Each year from early November to early December, the park's famous foliage fields reach their peak, with hundreds of towering ginkgo and maple trees turning color together to dress the park in early-autumn hues.

The most iconic sight here is the meeting of wild deer and a golden carpet of fallen leaves. Amid old stone lanterns and the Yoshikigawa stream, herds of deer amble across the leaf-strewn golden carpet, framed beneath a canopy of vivid color — a perfect expression of nature's own religious beauty.

The park's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained paths, making it easy going for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The surrounding area has excellent amenities, ideal for a full day trip. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest and sunlight filters through the treetops onto the foliage — perfect for capturing flawless reflections.

吉野山.count: abundant mountain-wide autumn color, said to rival its famous spring cherry blossoms
吉野山.address: 奈良縣吉野郡吉野町吉野山
吉野山.access_train: Cable car or on foot from Yoshino Station on the Kintetsu Yoshino Line
吉野山.access_car: About 50 min from the Koriyama IC on the Nishimeihan Expressway
吉野山.tagline: Climb this World Heritage mountain of mountain asceticism and take in 30,000 trees blazing into a layered carpet of color.
吉野山.desc:
Yoshinoyama, a World Heritage site, is one of the great sacred mountains of Shugendo mountain asceticism, world-famous for its 'Hitome Senbon' — a thousand cherry trees at a glance. Each year from mid-October to early November, the 30,000 trees covering the mountain turn color together, blanketing the sprawling highland ridges in a single vast, layered tapestry of color.

The greatest visual impact comes from the composition of Kinpusenji Temple's Zao-do Hall against the deep mountain valley and the surrounding color. Looking out from Yoshimizu Shrine or the Hanayagura Observatory, the red-and-gold gradient stretches up and down the steep slopes, framed together with the old wooden Buddhist halls — an open, expansive scene of powerful religious grandeur.

Although a ropeway can take you partway up, the mountaintop sites are scattered and natural slopes connect the various shrine halls, so professional non-slip hiking shoes are essential. Mountain mornings here are prone to mist, and the foliage glimpsed through drifting fog takes on a mysterious, ethereal beauty — choose a clear morning with good visibility for the best sweeping shots.

長谷寺.count: 1,000+ trees along the covered stairway and throughout the grounds
長谷寺.access_train: About 15 min walk from Hasedera Station on the Kintetsu Osaka Line
長谷寺.access_car: About 30 min from the Tenri IC on the Nishimeihan Expressway
長谷寺.tagline: Wander the 'Temple of Flowers' at the foot of Mt. Hase and climb its 362-step covered stairway to a maple-framed hall overlooking the valley.
長谷寺.desc:
Hase-dera sits at the foot of Mt. Hase, an ancient temple of the Shingon Buzan school famed nationwide as the 'Temple of Flowers.' Each year from mid-November to early December, hundreds of Iroha maples burst into color around the cliffs surrounding the main hall and throughout the deep-mountain grounds, dressing the sacred site in rich autumn hues.

The most representative composition here is the historic dialogue between the Important Cultural Property, a 362-step covered stairway, and the maples. The rustic wooden corridor climbs with the mountain's contours, its latticed windows framing views of cascading red-and-gold foliage outside; climb to the main hall's cantilevered 'Reido stage' and you can take in the entire valley's carpet of color in one sweep.

The long covered stairway is well maintained and roofed against rain, but because the whole temple is built into the hillside, walking it requires some stamina — comfortable shoes are recommended. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is clearest and the morning service opens the main icon — the best special window for atmospheric, classic photos.

室生寺.count: abundant autumn color around the five-story pagoda and throughout the grounds
室生寺.access_train: About 15 min by bus from Murouguchi-Ono Station on the Kintetsu Osaka Line
室生寺.access_car: About 60 min from the Tenri IC on the Nishimeihan Expressway
室生寺.tagline: Visit this Shingon temple deep in the Uda mountains, known as 'Women's Koyasan,' and walk the maple tunnel of Yoroizaka to its National Treasure pagoda.
室生寺.desc:
Muroji is a head temple of the Shingon sect, hidden away in a deep mountain valley and famous nationwide as 'Women's Koyasan' for having long welcomed female worshippers, unlike Mt. Koya itself. Each year from mid-November to early December, hundreds of old maples throughout the vast sacred grounds and around the halls built into the mountainside change color together, dressing the solemn site in classical elegance and deep atmosphere.

The most representative scene here is the dialogue across time between the National Treasure — Japan's smallest wooden five-story pagoda — the old moss-covered stone steps, and the full sweep of maples. Look up from 'Yoroizaka,' the slope in front of the Nio Gate in particular, and you'll see rows of natural stone steps wrapped in cascading crimson maple shadow, with layers of old wooden shrine buildings crowded by vivid blooms — a scene with the deep history and mysterious meditative quality unique to this old temple.

The main routes to the Drum Tower and five-story pagoda are mostly natural stone steps, with some sections of uneven terrain — comfortable, professional-grade running shoes are strongly recommended for visiting and photography. During the foliage festival, an evening illumination is held. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning, when the air is clearest, for the best chance to capture this Zen temple's distinctive atmospheric scenery.

那智大瀑布.count: abundant autumn color in the primeval forest around the falls
那智大瀑布.address: 和歌山縣東牟婁郡那智勝浦町那智山
那智大瀑布.access_train: About 25 min by bus from Kii-Katsuura Station on the JR Kisei Main Line to Nachisan
那智大瀑布.access_car: About 80 min from the Nanki-Tanabe IC on the Hanwa Expressway
那智大瀑布.tagline: Climb to the World Heritage grounds of Kumano Nachi Taisha and be stunned by Japan's tallest waterfall framed in deep-mountain foliage.
那智大瀑布.desc:
Nachi Otaki, with a drop of 133 meters, sits within the sacred grounds of Kumano Nachi Taisha and Seiganto-ji Temple, revered as the sacred body of Nachisan worship and inscribed as a World Heritage Site. Each year from late November to early December, the towering broadleaf primeval forest surrounding the falls' steep gorge changes color together, dressing this great natural landmark in a riot of hues.

The most dramatic scene here is the grand pairing of the triple cliff face, the cascading falls, the Seiganto-ji three-story pagoda, and autumn color. From the classic viewing platform, watch the blue-green torrent thunder straight down, with mist and boulders churning at its base, while the vermilion three-story pagoda of Seiganto-ji stands off to the side against a sprawling, layered carpet of gold and red — a scene of tremendous, open grandeur.

The approach to 'Hirō Shrine' at the base of the falls has well-maintained, gentle stone steps, making it relatively easy and safe to walk. Because the heavy spray makes some sections slippery, non-slip athletic shoes are strongly recommended for viewing and photography. Visit on a clear morning, when the light is best, for the perfect shot pairing water, sky, and crimson maples.

和歌山城.count: abundant color throughout the castle park
和歌山城.address: 和歌山縣和歌山市一番丁3
和歌山城.access_train: About 10 min by bus from Wakayama Station on the JR Kisei Main Line
和歌山城.access_car: About 10 min from the Wakayama IC on the Hanwa Expressway
和歌山城.tagline: Climb the castle of the 550,000-koku Kishu Tokugawa domain and see its white keep mirrored in the famed Nishinomaru Garden.
和歌山城.desc:
