Wakayama Castle, built atop the historic Torafusu Hill, is ranked among Japan's 100 Fine Castles and famed as the seat of the Kishu Tokugawa, one of the three great Tokugawa branch families. Each year from late November to early December, the celebrated 'Nishinomaru Garden' (Momijidani Garden) in the castle's northwest corner reaches peak foliage, taking on a refined, classical elegance.

The core appeal is the mirrored interplay of the white castle keep, the sukiya-style Enyokaku pavilion, and the autumn maples. Colorful trees crowd the clear inner moat, and when the mirror-still water perfectly reflects the history-laden wooden pavilion and the full sweep of color, the scene opens into the refined Japanese aesthetics of a daimyo garden.

The castle sits on a natural hill, and reaching the keep requires climbing a fairly steep old stone staircase — non-slip shoes are recommended. At the garden's Koshoan tea house, you can sip matcha while admiring the foliage. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the best chance to enjoy the classical garden's quiet atmosphere and ideal photography light all to yourself.

根來寺.count: about 100 maple trees and abundant color throughout the grounds
根來寺.access_train: About 15 min by taxi from Iwade Station on the JR line
根來寺.access_car: About 5 min from the Iwade-Negoro IC on the Hanwa Expressway
根來寺.tagline: Wander the Daimon River gorge at this Shingi Shingon head temple and see Japan's largest wooden pagoda framed by 'Momiji-dani' foliage.
根來寺.desc:
Negoroji is a historic old temple founded by the priest Kakuban, famous in the Sengoku era for its powerful warrior-monk force, the Negoro-shu. Each year from late November to early December it enters foliage season, with the primeval trees lining both banks of the Daimon River along the temple's 'Momiji-dani' (Maple Valley) turning color together, dressing this sacred site in vivid, vibrant hues.

The core visual appeal is the layered reflection of the National Treasure — Japan's largest wooden pagoda — set against a gentle waterside and a wall of color. Looking out over the clear pond, the towering, all-white 40-meter wooden pagoda stands majestically, mirrored perfectly in the still water alongside the surrounding blooms — a scene where movement and stillness intertwine, capturing the quiet, meditative sense of history unique to this ancient temple.

The paths between the main halls are flat and open, very friendly for visitors with elderly companions, making for an easy morning stroll. Negoroji's grounds are extensive and pair well with the nearby Negoro SL Park for a full day trip. Arrive in the early morning for the best chance to capture the deep meditative atmosphere and an empty, undisturbed view of this historic site.

大山.count: abundant color around Daisenji Temple and Mt. Goen
大山.address: 鳥取縣西伯郡大山町大山
大山.access_train: About 50 min by bus from Yonago Station on the JR San'in Main Line to Daisenji
大山.access_car: About 20 min from the Mizoguchi IC on the Yonago Expressway
大山.tagline: See the 'Hoki Fuji' blaze into gold across western Japan's largest beech primeval forest.
大山.desc:
Mount Daisen, nicknamed 'Hoki Fuji' for its resemblance to Mt. Fuji, is the highest peak in the Chugoku region. Each year from late October to early November, western Japan's largest primeval beech forest, covering the mountain's slopes, changes color together, blanketing the dramatic, rugged peaks in a riot of red and gold.

The most dramatic visual highlight is the striking contrast, seen from the Kagikake Pass Observatory, between the barren gray south wall and the layered color carpet spreading below. The bare, exposed cliff face stands against an endlessly rolling carpet of gold and red at the mountain's foot — an open, layered scene of grand natural beauty.

Well-maintained scenic roads connect all the major viewpoints, making it very convenient to drive between them. At this high elevation, late-autumn mornings are extremely cold, so bring plenty of warm, windproof outerwear for photography. Visit in the late morning on a clear day, when backlighting brings out the sharpest detail in the mountain ridges and the foliage.

三瓶山.count: broad swaths of color from the foothills to the mid-slopes
三瓶山.address: 島根縣大田市三瓶町多根
三瓶山.access_train: About 45 min by bus from Oda-shi Station on the JR San'in Main Line
三瓶山.access_car: About 30 min from the Mizuho IC on the Hamada Expressway
三瓶山.tagline: Wander Nishinohara in Daisen-Oki National Park and take in silvery pampas grass against a highland ring of color.
三瓶山.desc:
Mt. Sanbe is a striking mountain formed of a ring of volcanic peaks — Otosanbe, Mesanbe, and others — part of Daisen-Oki National Park. Each year from mid-October to early November, the natural broadleaf forest covering the slopes changes color in relay, adding rich early-autumn hues to the broad open fields.

What has made this spot famous online is the meeting of surging waves of silvery pampas grass across the vast Nishinohara meadow and the colorful mountains behind. Dense stands of pampas grass sway in the cool highland breeze, catching flashes of golden light, set against the vividly colored volcanic peaks beyond — an open, dynamic composition with real visual punch.

The foothills have excellent flat walking paths and a sightseeing chairlift, very friendly for visitors with elderly companions and families out for a hike. The mountain offers little shade, but late-autumn temperatures here are very comfortable. Visit on a weekday morning for a chance to catch the mysterious, dreamlike scenery of drifting morning mist.

後楽園.count: about 200 colorful trees in the garden
後楽園.address: 岡山縣岡山市北区後楽園1-5
後楽園.access_train: About 15 min by bus from Okayama Station on the JR line to Korakuen-mae
後楽園.access_car: About 15 min from the Okayama IC on the Sanyo Expressway
後楽園.tagline: Wander this Edo-period daimyo strolling garden, one of Japan's Three Great Gardens, and see Chishio-no-Mori's maples mirrored beside Okayama Castle.
後楽園.desc:
Korakuen, meticulously built by Okayama domain lord Ikeda Tsunamasa, is a landmark Edo-period daimyo garden and ranks among Japan's Three Great Gardens. Each year from mid-November to early December, 'Chishio no Mori' (Forest of a Thousand Dyes) on the garden's east side, planted with about a hundred maple trees, reaches peak foliage, lending this historic site a classical elegance.

The visual focus is the dialogue across time between the view from the summit of Mt. Yuishin overlooking Chishio no Mori, the clear pond, and the black-walled Okayama Castle. Colorful trees line the gentle waterway, and when the mirror-still 'Sawa no Ike' pond perfectly reflects the winding stream, the thatched tea house, and the black-and-gold keep of the 'Crow Castle,' the scene achieves refined Japanese aesthetics.

Most of the garden's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained paved paths and lawns, very friendly for wheelchairs and strollers. During the special evening illumination of the foliage festival, the fantastical water reflections feel even more ethereal. Arrive right at opening on a weekday morning for the best quiet, classical garden scenery.

錦帯橋.count: abundant autumn color along the Nishiki River and throughout Kikko Park
錦帯橋.access_train: About 15 min by bus from Iwakuni Station on the JR Sanyo Main Line to Kintai-kyo
錦帯橋.access_car: About 15 min from the Iwakuni IC on the Sanyo Expressway
錦帯橋.tagline: Wander the clear waters beside this five-arched wooden bridge and marvel at Kikko Park's old Kikkawa castle grounds ablaze with maple color.
錦帯橋.desc:
Kintai-kyo is a uniquely designed, world-class five-arched wooden bridge spanning the clear Nishiki River, ranked among Japan's three great bridges. Each year from mid- to late November, hundreds of old maples reach their peak in Kikko Park right beside the bridge and in Momijidani Park across the river, dressing this historic bridge in early-autumn color.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the uniquely designed five-arched wooden bridge, Mt. Yokoyama, and the autumn maples. The colorful trees line the gentle waterfront, and when the still Nishiki River perfectly mirrors the bridge's graceful curves and the full sweep of color, Iwakuni Castle can also be glimpsed on the hilltop in the distance — a scene of refined Japanese aesthetics.

The parks on both riverbanks are completely flat, with well-maintained old paths, very friendly for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The bridge itself has a distinctive wooden step structure inside, so watch your footing while crossing. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a clean, empty mirror shot.

内子の町並み.count: autumn color along the Edo-period streets and in the surrounding hills
内子の町並み.address: 愛媛縣喜多郡内子町内子
内子の町並み.access_train: About 10 min walk from Uchiko Station on the JR Yosan Line
内子の町並み.access_car: About 5 min from the Uchiko-Ikazaki IC on the Matsuyama Expressway
内子の町並み.tagline: Wander the imposing white-walled merchant streets of Yokaichi-Gokoku and see the Taisho-era Uchiko-za theater framed in classic autumn color.
内子の町並み.desc:
Uchiko is a well-preserved Important Preservation District for traditional buildings, the 'Yokaichi-Gokoku' quarter, home to merchant families who grew wealthy on wax and washi paper from the late Edo period through the Taisho era. Each year from mid- to late November, the old trees along the historic streets and their gardens turn color together, dressing the white-and-gold walls in early-autumn hues.

The core appeal is the classic pairing of the imposing white-walled merchant mansions, the gabled wooden architecture, and the classic autumn foliage. Strolling the 600-meter stone-paved historic street, the traditional wooden Uchiko-za theater appears alongside deep-red maple shadows spilling over the walls above — a scene that feels like stepping back in time, rich with human history.

The entire historic street is flat and easy to walk, very friendly for visitors with elderly companions and independent travelers who enjoy a slow pace and quiet surroundings. Autumn mornings here are pleasantly cool. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best purely atmospheric, historic photography.

四万十川.count: abundant primeval-forest color along the river
四万十川.address: 高知縣四万十市西土佐
四万十川.access_train: JR Dosan Line to Kubokawa Station, transfer to the Yodo Line to Ekawasaki Station
四万十川.access_car: About 60 min from the Shimanto-cho Chuo IC on the Kochi Expressway
四万十川.tagline: Wander 200km of untouched wilderness along 'Japan's last clear stream' and see the Sada submersible bridge framed in a full sweep of color.
四万十川.desc:
The Shimanto River, running 196km without a single major dam, is famed nationwide as 'Japan's last clear stream' — a top-tier natural, ecologically rich river. Each year from mid- to late November it enters foliage season, as the broad open fields and natural forest along both banks, winding through the mountains of Shikoku, put on coats of gold and deep red.

The most representative scene here is the meeting of the historic, railing-less 'chinka-bashi' submersible bridge, the gentle jade-green current, and the full sweep of color. Standing at the water's edge, where the river runs clear like a blue-green ribbon, you can see the railing-less 'Sada Chinka-bashi' set against the layered, gold-and-red carpet of color spreading over the mountains behind — a scene of tremendous openness.

The road along the river is flat and open, with complete bicycle rental and sightseeing boat facilities, very friendly for elderly companions and family day trips. There's no shelter at all here, so a clear morning shows off the water's transparency at its best — ideal for capturing this internet-famous natural landscape.

雲仙仁田峠.count: sweeping, spectacular color across the mountain pass
雲仙仁田峠.address: 長崎縣雲仙市小浜町雲仙
雲仙仁田峠.access_train: About 60 min by bus from Shimabara Station on the Shimabara Railway to Nita Toge
雲仙仁田峠.access_car: About 80 min from the Isahaya IC on the Nagasaki Expressway
雲仙仁田峠.tagline: Ride the Unzen Ropeway up to a sky-high plateau and marvel at the active volcano Mt. Fugen amid Japan's most vivid three-tier foliage.
雲仙仁田峠.desc:
Unzen Nita Toge, sitting at an elevation of about 1,000 meters within Unzen-Amakusa National Park, is Nagasaki's premier large-scale foliage destination. Thanks to its high elevation and latitude, it turns earliest in all of Kyushu — from late October to early November, more than a hundred species of high-mountain broadleaf natural forest on Mt. Fugen reach their peak together.

The most breathtaking view comes from riding the 'Unzen Ropeway.' As you rise slowly into the sky on the cool mountain breeze, you look down over a god's-eye view of a color carpet that stretches endlessly with the terrain, and when the calm water and Shimabara Bay — sometimes even the Aso mountain range — appear together in the distance, the scale and visual impact are immense.

Although the ropeway takes you directly to the Myoken-dake summit observatory, this high plateau sees strong winds and a chill year-round, so bring a warm windproof coat for photography. The summit paths are flat and well maintained, very friendly for elderly companions. Climb on a clear morning with good visibility for the best sweeping shots of the open fields and the mountainside in bloom.

鍋ヶ滝.count: color in the cave behind the falls and the surrounding primeval forest
鍋ヶ滝.address: 熊本縣阿蘇郡小国町黒渕
鍋ヶ滝.access_train: About 30 min by taxi from Bungo-Mori Station on the JR Kyudai Main Line
鍋ヶ滝.access_car: About 30 min from the Kusu IC on the Oita Expressway
鍋ヶ滝.tagline: Step into a mysterious cave behind the falls at the foot of Mt. Aso and be stunned by a curtain of water framed in a full valley of color.
鍋ヶ滝.desc:
Nabegataki is a specially designated scenic waterfall formed by a massive ancient eruption of Mt. Aso. Each year from mid- to late November it reaches peak foliage, as towering maples and beech trees transform into a brilliant carpet of color, dressing this hidden forest gorge in vivid, vibrant hues.

The most dramatic centerpiece here is the chance to walk into the legendary 'Uramino-taki' behind the falls. Standing inside the broad natural rock cave and looking out, the crystal-clear curtain of water — a 10-meter drop, 20 meters wide — looks like a giant ribbon, set off by the golden foliage outside for a scene of pure, ethereal beauty.

The path to the base of the falls is fitted with a gentle, comfortable wooden boardwalk and steps, but heavy spray keeps the surface perpetually slippery — non-slip athletic shoes are strongly recommended. To protect the fragile natural landscape, entry is by online reservation only. Visit on a weekday morning for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot.

仙巌園.count: abundant autumn color throughout the garden
仙巌園.address: 鹿兒島縣鹿兒島市吉野町9700-1
仙巌園.access_train: About 30 min by bus from Kagoshima-Chuo Station on the JR line to Senganen-mae
仙巌園.access_car: About 20 min from the Kagoshima-Kita IC on the Kyushu Expressway
仙巌園.tagline: Wander the Shimazu clan's celebrated daimyo garden and catch the towering active volcano Sakurajima framed by a sweep of maple color.
仙巌園.desc:
Senganen (also known as Isoteien) is a massive strolling-pond daimyo garden, a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty, built by Shimazu Mitsuhisa, lord of the Satsuma domain. Each year from late November to early December, hundreds of maples throughout the garden reach peak foliage, dressing this historic site in classical elegance and vibrant color.

The most representative sight here is the grand pairing of smoking Sakurajima volcano, Kinko Bay, and the autumn maples. Standing in the open central garden plaza, you can take in the towering, distant Sakurajima volcano, a still reservoir pond, and the vivid crimson maples swaying at the waterside all in one frame — a scene of tremendous scale balanced with softness.

Most of the garden's terrain is completely flat, with well-maintained paved paths, very friendly for visitors with elderly companions or strollers. The well-preserved Shimazu family 'Goten' residence features exquisite woodwork inside and is well worth a visit. Arrive on a weekday morning, when crowds are thinnest, for the best chance at a perfect mirror shot of this historic site.

首里城公園.types: Fukugi (Garcinia subelliptica), Banyan — Okinawa's autumn is defined mainly by flowering and evergreen plants rather than foliage
首里城公園.count: subtropical vegetation, with no pronounced autumn color
首里城公園.address: 沖繩縣那霸市首里金城町1-2
首里城公園.access_train: About 15 min walk from Shuri Station on the Okinawa Urban Monorail (Yui Rail)
首里城公園.tagline: Climb the World Heritage ruins of the Ryukyu Kingdom's royal palace and take in Shureimon Gate, its vintage red walls, and early-winter blooms.
首里城公園.desc:
Shurijo Koen preserves several centuries of Ryukyu Kingdom history in a magnificent World Heritage royal palace complex. Because Okinawa's climate stays warm year-round, flowering here turns latest of anywhere in Japan, not coming into its own until early December, when it dresses the imposing vermilion castle walls in autumn accents.

The core appeal is the perfect blend of the iconic Shureimon Gate, the imposing fortress walls, and Japanese-style blooms. The rustic Tang-style hip-and-gable wooden gate and stone-paved streets are closely surrounded by potted hydrangeas locally cultivated in Okinawa alongside Western varieties, set off against the sea and sky in the distance for a scene rich with exotic character.

The palace grounds are well laid out; while some areas include steep stone steps and sloped walls, the main visitor route is fitted with even walkways and escalators. There's an air-conditioned cultural exhibition hall on site. Visit in the morning to catch the wood grain of the old buildings in soft light, for the best story-rich, atmospheric shots.

大雪山.types: Rowan (Nanakamado), Erman's birch, mountain sorrel (herbaceous foliage)
大雪山.count: the largest-scale mountain range to turn color earliest in all of Japan
大雪山.address: 北海道上川郡東川町旭岳溫泉
大雪山.access_train: About 90 min by 'Ide-yu Go' bus from Asahikawa Station on the JR line
大雪山.access_car: About 1 hour from the Asahikawa-Kita IC on the Doo Expressway
大雪山.tagline: Climb Japan's earliest-turning northern peaks and take in high-mountain conifers set against a blazing crimson tundra.
大雪山.desc:
Daisetsuzan National Park is Japan's largest national park, famous nationwide as the place where autumn color arrives earliest in the country. Thanks to its high elevation and latitude, high-mountain plants begin changing color as early as late August, and by early to mid-September the whole mountain range is blanketed in a rich gradient of red and gold.

The visual highlight is a richly layered 'three-dimensional color carpet.' Ride the 'Kurodake Ropeway' or the 'Asahidake Ropeway' slowly up into the sky and look down over a vast natural palette woven from rowan, Erman's birch, and other high-mountain plants intertwined with deep-green conifer forest — a visually striking effect.

As the front line of Japan's foliage season, temperatures near the summit already approach freezing by mid-September, so a proper windproof, insulated mountaineering jacket is essential for viewing and photography. Mountain weather here changes fast, so a clear morning with good visibility is strongly recommended for the most dramatic shots of these majestic peaks.

中禪寺湖.fee: Free (no admission fee around Chuzenji-ko; Kegon Falls observation deck, adults ¥570)
中禪寺湖.access_train: About 45 min by bus from Tobu-Nikko Station on the Tobu Nikko Line or Nikko Station on the JR line, toward Chuzenji Onsen
中禪寺湖.access_car: About 20 min from the Kiyotaki IC on the Nikko-Utsunomiya Road; the Iroha-zaka road gets congested during the foliage season, so a weekday early-morning departure is recommended
中禪寺湖.tagline: Stand at the foot of Mt. Nantai in Nikko and take in the double impact of Kegon Falls' headwaters and lakeside autumn color.
中禪寺湖.desc:
Chuzenji-ko sits within Nikko National Park, a natural dammed lake at an elevation of 1,269 meters. Each year from mid- to late October, the maples and Japanese oak (mizunara) forest ringing its broad shoreline reach peak foliage, dressing this storied summer-resort lake in vivid, lively color.

The most iconic view is the layered panorama from the Hangetsuyama Observatory. Climb to the heights and you can frame the vividly colored 'Hatchō Deshima' peninsula — stretching into the lake like a dragon's tail — together with towering Mt. Nantai behind it and the deep blue lake below. The autumn color along the banks of nearby Kegon Falls is another must-shoot spot.

Because the 'Iroha-zaka' mountain road gets extremely congested during Nikko's foliage season, it's strongly recommended to set out before daybreak on a weekday. Winds on the summit plateau are strong and it feels noticeably cooler up there, so bring a thin windproof jacket for photography. Clear mornings are the best time to capture a perfect lake reflection alongside the autumn colors.
